title: v0.62.327: price filter matches the displayed $ (money-band tier) + drops signal-less venues
body:
## Bug (audited)
Selecting **$** in Cuisine search still showed venues at **$100 / $20–40**. The filter WAS wired (client `filters.prices` → server post-filter), but broke in effect:
- **Dimension mismatch**: filter matched Google **`priceLevel`** (★ tier) while the card shows **`priceRangeDisplay`** (actual menu money, from `priceRange`) — uncorrelated.
- **Null pass-through**: `v.priceLevel == null || …` let every unknown-tier venue through (many SG venues have no `priceLevel`), so they showed whatever money range they had.

## Fix (operator-approved: filter on money + tighten nulls)
- **currency-format.js** — new `priceTierFromRange(priceRange)`: buckets the range's per-pax midpoint into 1–4 via SGD bands ($ <S$15 · $$ 15–40 · $$$ 40–80 · $$$$ ≥80), converting other currencies through the existing USD-pivot baseline (coarse is fine for 4 buckets — no live FX).
- **index.js** — all 3 price-filter sites (warm-seed, main `/api/cuisine/search`, nl-path) now: `tier = priceTierFromRange(v.priceRange) ?? v.priceLevel`; **drop** venues with no price signal when a filter is active. The filtered dimension now equals the **shown money**.

## Verify
- node --check (index.js, currency-format.js, test). `priceTierFromRange` unit-tested: SGD bands, MYR/JPY FX conversion, null→fallback (all pass). 3 filter sites updated, 0 old null-pass lines remain.

title: v0.62.328: Clipboard PR #1 — storage groundwork (per-card HASH, TTL rule, cabinet/drawer primitives, cascade-delete)
body:
## Summary

First slice of the v0.7 Clipboard 4-PR cycle. **No user-visible change** — the chat `/clipboard` flow and the existing `/api/cuisine/copy-{one,all}` writes behave exactly as before. What changes is the underneath.

### Schema shift

- Cards become per-card Redis HASHes (`card:<chatId>:<cardId>`) so each card carries its own TTL. A favourite card can `PERSIST` while a non-favourite catch-all card carries 30 days — one shared LIST TTL couldn't express that.
- `clip:<chatId>` becomes a cardId-only index LIST (PERSIST, cap 50).
- `card_locs:<chatId>:<cardId>` SET is the O(1) inverse index for "is this card referenced elsewhere?"

### TTL rule (single source-of-truth helper `recomputeCardTtl`, applied on every card mutation)

| State | TTL |
|---|---|
| ⭐ favourite | `PERSIST` (operator-locked: *"favourite card will be kept forever and not be affected by TTL 30 days"*) |
| placed in any drawer | 1 year |
| catch-all only | 30 days |

### Lazy migration

Old-shape JSON entries promote in-place to HASH + index at the same slot, preserving original `ts` and 30d TTL. Zero downtime, no data loss.

### New file `clipboard-store.js`

Cabinet ZSET, cabinet HASH, drawer-metadata LIST, per-drawer cardId LIST, `card_locs` inverse index. CRUD for cabinets / drawers / placements. 11 segments (`dayBreak` · `breakfast` · `brunch` · `lunch` · `lateLunch` · `teaBreak` · `earlyDinner` · `dinner` · `supper` · `nightSnack` · `wholeDay`). Operator-locked caps enforced server-side (**12** cabinets / **20** drawers per cab / **10** cards per drawer / **80**-char cabinet name / **990**-char card note). Drawer `location` is `{ lat, lng, label }` so PR #3 can plug the cuisine TMA's shared `LocationField` via Vite alias.

### Cascade-delete (operator-locked rules)

| Card state | Drawer/cabinet delete result |
|---|---|
| ⭐ favourite | record survives in catch-all, stays `PERSIST` |
| still placed in another drawer | record survives, other placement intact, TTL → 1y |
| single-placed non-favourite | `softDeleteCard` drops the HASH |

`reindexDrawersAfterDelete` re-keys the inverse index when a middle drawer is removed.

### Back-compat

Public surface preserved: `pushClip` · `listClips` · `getClip` · `clearClips` · `removeClip` · `renameClip` — `index.js` callers at lines 4037–4124 + 7812–7839 keep working byte-identically.

### What's NOT in this PR (lands in PRs #2 / #3 / #4)

- **PR #2** — 16 `/api/clipboard/*` HTTP endpoints; `/clipboard` chat reply gains an inline "📋 Open Clipboard" button; `setChatMenuButton`; share-token mint + fork flow.
- **PR #3** — new `web/clipboard/` Vite app; 11-segment drawer UI; drag / long-press gestures; shared `LocationField` via Vite alias; the bordered **"Sketchbook / Clipboard"** panel below the cuisine TMA's Location field (operator-locked entry-point spec captured at `doc/v0.70_.MD` § "Locked UI decisions for the Clipboard cycle", PR #1289).
- **PR #4** — cabinet sort UI (name / location / date); drawer manual reorder; `cb.share` / `cb.fork` / `cb.add_drawer` / `cb.add_cabinet` analytics.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --check clip-store.js && node --check clipboard-store.js` → OK
- [x] `npm test -- --run` → **141 files / 3591 tests / 100% green** (16.3s)
- [x] New `clip-store.test.js` covers: TTL rule table (5 cases incl. favourite-AND-placed → PERSIST, flip-off restoration), migration (4 cases incl. mixed-list + on-the-spot via `getClip`), lazy purge (skip-from-results + LREM-by-value after iteration), `softDeleteCard` + `getCardById`
- [x] New `clipboard-store.test.js` covers: every cap (12 / 20 / 10) rejects N+1, dedup within same drawer, **duplicates across drawers PERMITTED** (operator-locked), location validation, the 4 cascade rules end-to-end via `deleteDrawer` + `deleteCabinet`, inverse-index consistency through reindex
- [x] Worktree at `../gia-clipboard-pr1` off `origin/main` (`ea8ecc7`) to avoid filesystem races with the parallel doc-session on PR #1289

## Notes on coordination

This PR was built in a separate git worktree to avoid clobbering the parallel session's work on the v0.70 doc PR (#1289). Different branch, different file surface — the only theoretical hotspots are `package.json`, `doc/.serial-state.yml`, and the new Journal file, all of which rebase cleanly because PR #1289 doesn't touch them.

Hourly recheck cron from this session is still armed for PR #1289.

title: v0.62.329: Clipboard PR #2 — API surface (16 endpoints, drawer-share + fork, integration tests)
body:
## Summary

Second slice of the v0.7 Clipboard 4-PR cycle. **No user-visible change yet** — the cuisine TMA still doesn't know how to talk to these endpoints (PR #3) and the `/clipboard` chat reply still ships the legacy text listing (also PR #3). What lands here: **16 routes** under `/api/clipboard/*` with one auth chokepoint + one carve-out, the drawer-share mint + fork round-trip, and comprehensive integration coverage.

> **⚠️ Stacked on #1301.** This PR depends on the per-card HASH helpers shipped by PR #1 storage groundwork. The branch is `claude/clipboard-pr2-api` off `claude/clipboard-pr1-storage`. When #1301 merges, rebase to main is clean (no file overlap — PR #2 doesn't modify `clip-store.js` or `clipboard-store.js`).

### The 16 endpoints

| # | Method | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | GET | `/state` | catch-all count + cabinet list (light) |
| 2 | GET | `/cabinet/:id` | full cabinet + drawers + cards (heavy) |
| 3 | POST | `/cabinet` | create (cap-12) |
| 4 | PATCH | `/cabinet/:id` | rename / emoji / location / dates / sortDirection |
| 5 | DELETE | `/cabinet/:id` | cascade per operator-locked rules |
| 6 | POST | `/cabinet/:id/drawer` | add (cap-20, segment + dayTag? + location?) |
| 7 | DELETE | `/cabinet/:id/drawer/:n` | cascade + reindex |
| 8 | PATCH | `/cabinet/:id/drawer/:n` | dayTag / location / optional `moveTo` manual reorder |
| 9 | POST | `/card/:id/place` | placement (cap-10 per drawer) |
| 10 | POST | `/card/:id/unplace` | remove placement |
| 11 | POST | `/card/:id/move` | atomic unplace+place |
| 12 | PATCH | `/card/:id` | name / note (≤990) / favourite (toggles PERSIST via `recomputeCardTtl`) |
| 13 | DELETE | `/card/:id` | hard-drop HASH + walk every placement |
| 14 | POST | `/cabinet/:id/drawer/:n/share` | mint token + persist to drawer meta |
| 15 | GET | `/shared/:token` | **PUBLIC** — the token IS the auth |
| 16 | POST | `/shared/:token/fork` | authed; optional `cabinetId` target |

### Auth model

Single chokepoint `app.use('/api/clipboard', requireInitDataFromBodyOrHeader)` with the public `GET /shared/:token` registered **before** the gate so Express matches it without auth. Dev-bypass (`SKIP_INIT_DATA_AUTH=true`) falls back to `?chatId=` / body for preview/curl.

### Share + fork

Share payload (`kind: 'dr_share'`) goes through the existing `share.js` helper (7-day TTL, 10-char base64url token). The drawer's `shareToken` is written back onto the metadata entry. The owner's `chatId` is **stripped** from the public read so a forwarded link can't be used to enumerate the owner.

Fork: `pushClip` mints fresh cardIds in the caller's catch-all; if `cabinetId` is provided, `addDrawer` creates a fresh drawer with the same segment / dayTag / location and each card is `placeCard`'d into it.

### Error mapping

Structured errors from `clipboard-store` → HTTP codes: `name-required` / `invalid-segment` / `missing-args` → 400, caps → 409 + `cap` field, `*-not-found` → 404, `redis-failure` → 503.

### What's NOT in this PR (PR #3)

- New `web/clipboard/` Vite app + 11-segment drawer UI + drag/long-press gestures
- Shared `LocationField` import via Vite alias from `web/cuisine/`
- Bordered "Sketchbook / Clipboard" panel below the cuisine TMA's Location field (operator-locked entry-point spec at `doc/v0.70_.MD`)
- `/clipboard` chat reply gaining the "📋 Open Clipboard" inline button
- `setChatMenuButton` on bot startup

## Test plan

- [x] `node --check index.js && node --check clipboard-routes.js` → OK
- [x] `npm test -- --run` → **142 files / 3660 tests / 100% green** (20.3s, **+69 over PR #1's 3591**)
- [x] New `clipboard-routes.test.js` (28 `it` cases): in-process Express + Node `http.request` (no `supertest` dep added). Covers auth carve-out, cap enforcement at HTTP layer, cascade-delete preserving favourites, drawer reorder via `moveTo` with `card_locs` reindex consistency, share → fork round-trip, public read 404 on expired token, owner-chatId not leaking on public reads.
- [x] Fake redis extended with `set` / `get` for plain strings (needed by `share.js`)
- [x] Worktree at `../gia-clipboard-pr2` stacked on `claude/clipboard-pr1-storage`

## Notes on stacking

Until #1301 merges, this PR's mergeable state shows main as the base. The actual review commits ride on top of PR #1's storage commit. Merging order should be:
1. Merge #1301 first.
2. Rebase this onto main (clean — no file overlap).
3. Merge this.

body:
## Summary

Third slice of the v0.7 Clipboard 4-PR cycle — **the headline PR**, and the first one users see. Stacked on PR #2's branch so the new TMA can talk to the 16 endpoints PR #2 mounted.

### Three deliverables in one PR

**1. NEW `web/clipboard/` Vite app** (12 files + 13 component/lib modules)

- own bundle at `/app/clipboard` (vite base `/app/clipboard/`, output `public/clipboard/`)
- **hash router** with 3 routes:

title: v0.62.331: Clipboard PR #4 — polish + analytics (cabinet sort, drawer reorder arrows, cb.* events)
body:
## Summary

Fourth and **final** slice of the v0.7 Clipboard cycle. Three additive polish items on top of PR #3's TMA bundle. Closes the cycle.

> **⚠️ Stacked on #1303 → #1302 → #1301.** Merge order: **#1301 → #1302 → #1303 → #1304**. Branch is `claude/clipboard-pr4-polish` off `claude/clipboard-pr3-tma`.

### 1. Cabinet sort UI (`CabinetGrid.jsx`)

| Sort | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **newest** (default) | by `modifiedAt` descending |
| **A–Z** | by `name` (locale-aware, case-insensitive) |
| **location** | alpha by `location` field; empty-location cabinets sort last |
| **trip date** | by `dateStart` with `dateEnd` fallback; cabinets without dates sort to the bottom by `modifiedAt` |

- Surfaced only when `cabinets.length > 1`
- Sort is client-side `useMemo`; active key held in component state, **not persisted** (operator hasn't asked for a per-user pref + the 12-cap keeps re-sort cheap)

### 2. Drawer manual reorder (`DrawerRow.jsx` + `CabinetView.jsx` + `App.jsx`)

- Explicit **▲ ▼ arrows** in each drawer header, stacked compact to the left of the segment emoji
- `canMoveUp` / `canMoveDown` computed against `totalDrawers`; arrows dimmed at the boundaries; `aria-label="Move up/down"` for accessibility; `stopPropagation` so they don't trigger the collapse-toggle next to them
- `onMove(from, to)` plumbed up to `App.jsx` → `api.updateDrawer(cabId, from, { moveTo: to })` which hits **PR #2's** `PATCH /cabinet/:id/drawer/:n` endpoint (server-side re-keys `card_locs:<chatId>:<cardId>` across the shift — covered by PR #2's existing reorder test)
- **Long-press drag of the whole drawer header deferred** — arrows cover the common "move up one slot" intent and avoid fighting the existing card-drag long-press recogniser inside the drawer body

### 3. `cb.*` analytics events (`clipboard-routes.js`)

NEW `track(redis, chatId, event, fields)` helper wraps `vlogIf(redis, chatId, { ns: 'cb', event, ...fields })`. Never throws (analytics must not affect the user-facing response).

| Event | Where fired | Notable fields |
|---|---|---|
| `cb.add_cabinet` | `POST /cabinet` | `cabId`, `hasLocation`, `hasDates` |
| `cb.delete_cabinet` | `DELETE /cabinet/:id` | `cabId` |
| `cb.add_drawer` | `POST /cabinet/:id/drawer` | `cabId`, `segment`, `hasLocation` |
| `cb.place_card` | `POST /card/:id/place` | `cardId`, `cabId`, `drawerIdx`, `alreadyPresent` |
| `cb.move_card` | `POST /card/:id/move` | `cardId`, `from`, `to` |
| `cb.share_drawer` | `POST /cabinet/:id/drawer/:n/share` | `cabId`, `drawerIdx`, `cardCount` |
| `cb.fork_drawer` | `POST /shared/:token/fork` | `token`, `forkedCount`, `intoCabinet` |

Gated by the per-chat verbose flag — `vlogIf` is a no-op when off; at most one Redis GET per request when verbose is engaged. Surfaces as `[VLOG <chatId>] {...}` JSON lines in Railway logs only when `/verbose on` is set for that chat.

## What's NOT in this PR

- **Long-press drag of the whole drawer header** — arrows cover the intent; can be a follow-up if data shows it's needed
- **Vite alias to shared `LocationField`** for the `AddDrawerSheet` drawer-location picker (still a free-text label field). Full picker integration requires the alias config + dependency tracing of `countries.js` / `cities.js` / `jb-focus-points.js` / `coords-to-country.js`. Not blocking ship.
- **`setChatMenuButton` repoint** decision — main menu still routes to `/app/menu` hub. Cross-platform Telegram-cache invalidation deserves its own PR.
- **Native-linguist QA pass** on the 32 i18n keys × 5 langs
- **BotFather short-name registration** for `clipboard` — external operator action

## Test plan

- [x] `node --check clipboard-routes.js` → OK
- [x] `npm test -- --run` → **142 files / 3660 tests / 100% green** (20.5s)
- [x] `npm run build:clipboard` → 180 KB JS / 11 KB CSS / 46 modules / 1.71s
- [x] Sort chips only appear when `cabinets.length > 1`; default sort is "newest"
- [x] Reorder arrows dimmed at boundaries (▲ at index 0, ▼ at last)
- [x] `track()` calls only fire on success path, never throw
- [x] Worktree at `../gia-clipboard-pr4` stacked on `claude/clipboard-pr3-tma`

## Closes the v0.7 Clipboard cycle

PRs #1+#2+#3+#4 cover storage (HASH schema + TTL rule + cascade), API (16 endpoints + share/fork), TMA (Vite bundle + cuisine entry-point + chat door), polish+analytics. Next strategic moves are parked in the v0.70 roadmap doc (PR #1289).

title: v0.62.345: price filter — add 4th tier ($$$$) so Manila/fine-dining is selectable
body:
**Bug:** In Manila (and any city with fine-dining ≥ S$80), venues render `$$$$` on the card but **no filter pill could match them** — the filter offered only `$`/`$$`/`$$$`, and the server matches each pill by exact tier, so tier-4 venues were unreachable. Selecting `$$$` excluded them.

**Root cause:** Google Places `priceLevel` has 4 paid levels (Inexpensive→Very Expensive = $→$$$$) and `ResultCard` already labels all 4, but the *filter* was capped at 3.

**Fix (4 levels everywhere):**
- `QuickFilters.jsx` — `PRICES` adds `$$$$` (flex-wrap row, no layout change).
- `state.js` — `PRICE_LEVELS` URL-param allow-list adds `$$$$`.
- `index.js` — copy-syntax tokenizer + `cleanPrices` cap lifted 3→4.

Server tier matchers already use `p.length` + `priceTierFromRange` (1–4) — no change needed there.

The four levels: `$`=Inexpensive · `$$`=Moderate · `$$$`=Expensive · `$$$$`=Very Expensive.

title: v0.62.352: free-text price filter — deterministic $ parse (fixes '$ shows $$$$')
body:
Operator: typing 'french crepe with $' returned Montrachet ($$$$). Root cause: free-text price tier is parsed by the LLM (tell-gia), which **drops a bare '$' symbol**, so no price filter is applied. The server post-filter is correct — it just never received prices.

Fix: derive the price tier **deterministically** from the raw text ('$' run → tier, '$'→[$] tier-1 only, up to '$$$$') and override the LLM's prices whenever a '$' is present. Words like 'cheap' still go through the LLM (override returns null with no '$'). Also extends VALID_PRICES + the prompt to the 4th tier, matching #1321.

title: v0.62.353: city change + 🔍 now searches the new location (regression fix)
body:
Operator: change the city, tap 🔍 — search still ran on the PREVIOUS location.

Root cause: a previewed city is committed in `triggerSearch` by calling `onLocationSelect` then `return`. That relied on onLocationSelect to auto-fire — but **v0.62.183 made onLocationSelect no-auto-fire**, so 🔍 committed the new anchor and returned WITHOUT searching; the visible results stayed on the old anchor (Raffles Place).

Fix: after committing, `triggerSearch` now runs the search itself at the just-committed city, passing the anchor **explicitly** to avoid the stale-state race (v0.61.237 lesson). No policy reversal — picks still don't auto-fire; only the explicit 🔍 tap searches.

title: v0.62.374: fix chat search — venue-filter over-drop + classifier outage decline
body:
Two confirmed bugs from Railway logs (both kill chat free-text + /s search):

**Bug B — 'mee soto' found 6, dropped all.** v0.62.117 surfaced Google `types[]` on FanOut venues; `passesVenueFilter` rejects any venue whose `types[]` hits NON_FOOD_TYPES — but that set has **establishment** + **point_of_interest**, which Google tags on ~every place → every result dropped. Fix: a `GENERIC_TYPES` allowlist so those generics are only droppable as a venue's *primaryType*, not in `types[]`.

**Bug A — 'spicy thai' declined.** On a Gemini **503 outage** the intent classifier returned `'ambiguous'`, which the chat handler treats as 'decline' → no search at all. Fix: classifier now **fails OPEN** to a dish search on the raw text (both the no-key and all-models-down paths). Genuine LLM 'ambiguous' still declines.

Updated the two intent-fallback tests to the fail-open contract. venue-filters tests unaffected (Lau Pa Sat etc. drop by name).

Note: the Clipboard black-screen is separate (needs the browser console) — still open.

title: v0.62.376: throttled 'AI busy' notice when search classifier degrades
body:
## What
When the Gemini search-intent classifier fails open during an outage (no key / all models down), the chat free-text search now still runs on the raw text and sends one friendly, throttled notice so the user knows results are the direct-match fallback and can retry for the smarter pass.

## Changes
- gemini-client.js: both classifySearchIntent fail-open returns now carry degraded: true (normal/model-fallback returns unchanged).
- index.js: new sendDegradedNotice(redis, chatId, lang) — Redis-throttled (NX+EX 180s, once / 3 min per chat), en/fr copy, never throws/blocks. Wired into the chat free-text handler after the search when the classifier degraded.

## Why
Operator option 1: a light busy notice only on genuine degradation — not every search, throttled per chat.

title: v0.62.498: Menu TMA auto-detect gates on anchorLoading (tighten 800ms first-launch race)
body:
## What

Tightens the Menu TMA **first-launch location race** surfaced in the location-cache trace.

Menu has **no browser location cache** (React state + server Redis SSOT via `/api/cuisine/user-location`) and **no boot gate**. The residual was a race: the auto-detect `useEffect` waited a **fixed 800 ms `setTimeout`** for the initial user-location fetch before firing `runAutoDetect`. A slow fetch (>800 ms) let auto-detect run while `anchor` was still `null`; the timer could also fire before `setAnchor` committed.

## Fix (1 web file — `web/menu/src/App.jsx`)

- Dropped the `setTimeout(…, 800)` + cleanup.
- Gate on the existing **`anchorLoading`** state, which flips `false` in **every** terminal branch of the fetch (`.then` / `.catch` / no-Telegram). Auto-detect now fires the instant the fetch settles — never later, never before the anchor commits (`setAnchor` batches with `setAnchorLoading(false)`).
- Added `anchorLoading` to the effect deps.
- **No timer added to any boot gate** — Menu has none; this only sequences auto-detect.

## Verify

esbuild JSX parse clean · vitest green (the one `clipboard-routes` timeout is a pre-existing full-suite flake — passes in isolation, unrelated file) · `web/menu` build clean (245 kB).

G4: eyeball first-launch on a **slow** connection — anchor resolves before auto-detect, no jump-to-default.

title: v0.62.501: TMAs prefer device locale (navigator) over Telegram-app locale — fixes French UI on French phone w/ English Telegram
body:
**Report:** a French native user on a Samsung S22 saw English pills/wording across multiple TMAs.

**Root cause (traced, shared by all 5 TMAs).** `getActiveLocale` precedence was `localStorage 'gia.locale'` → **Telegram app `language_code`** → `navigator.language` → `'en'`, short-circuiting on the first supported hit. `language_code` is the **Telegram client UI** language, not the phone's. A French user whose Telegram app is English sends `language_code: "en"`, so the chain stopped at `"en"` and never consulted `navigator.language` (`fr-FR` → `fr`). Region-tag hypothesis **refuted** — every resolver already normalises `fr-FR`→`fr`; it was pure precedence.

**Amplifier cleared:** `GET /api/cuisine/user-language` uses `getUserLang` (explicit-only), not `resolveLang`, so `hydrateFromServerOnce` can't clobber the device detection — no server change.

**Fix (5 web files, `getActiveLocale` only).** Prefer the device locale over the Telegram-app locale, keeping the supported-or-skip fall-through (unsupported device locale → Telegram hint → `'en'`); `localStorage 'gia.locale'` stays highest.
- cuisine / menu / transport: `detectFromTelegram() || detectFromNavigator()` → `detectFromNavigator() || detectFromTelegram()`
- hawker: navigator block moved above the Telegram block
- clipboard: reads navigator (supported-check) before the Telegram-first `getLanguage()`

**Trade-off (accepted):** an English phone with a deliberately-French Telegram now defaults to English on first load — the in-app 🌐 toggle sets French and persists.

**Verify:** `node --check` clean on all 5; cuisine+menu+hawker+transport build in CI.

## What

Operator: *"i thought there is a spec on language"*. **There wasn't one.** The language strategy was real but **unwritten** — it lived only in the `scripts/translate-content.mjs` header comment, five per-surface `SUPPORTED` arrays, and a retrospective stocktake. This PR authors the **normative spec**.

## The spec — `doc/Technical/technical-0_62_522-09_07_26-0914.md`

| § | Contents |
|---|---|
| **1** | The authoritative **8 locales** (`en fr id ru de zh ja es`) + all **7 declaration sites** |
| **2** | **Two-tier model** — hand-authored master is *never mutated*; Gemini writes `*.generated.js` overlays merged at load; hand-authored wins |
| **3** | Scope: **prose only**. `cooking-methods.js` excluded (search-routing token index). **Proper-Noun Policy** — dish/cuisine/place names are *identity, not copy*. Translation is deliberately **ungrounded**; *drafting* is grounded |
| **4** | Pipeline mechanics — `MODEL_CHAIN`, `BATCH_SIZE=14`, cascade on 503/404 but **not** 429 (shared quota bucket) |
| **5** | The **11-step add-a-language procedure** |
| **6** | Related records |

Introduces rules **L-1 … L-11**. Deprecated table entry #1 retires *"strategy lives in a code header"*.

title: v0.62.523: language selection criterion — L-12 / L-13 (closes the [UNVERIFIED])
body:
## What

v0.62.522 §1.2 left exactly one thing open — **`[UNVERIFIED]`: why *these* eight languages?** No rationale existed anywhere in the repo. This PR closes it by **operator decision**, not by reconstruction.

## The decision (gate G3)

Two questions were put explicitly, and answered:

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| **Criterion?** | **Global Telegram reach** — not SG relevance, not hybrid tiers |
| **Ship locale changes?** | **Document only** — no app change |

The operator **ratifies the existing eight** and elects to *document the tension rather than resolve it*.

## Evidence gathered

- **Telegram publishes no per-country MAU.** Only the ~1 B global total is **OFFICIAL**; every per-country figure is a third-party **ESTIMATE**, and sources disagree by **2–3×**. This caveat is now written into the spec so no number is mistaken for authoritative data.
- **`zh` and `ja` fail a pure reach test** — Telegram is **blocked in mainland China** (2015; removed from the China App Store, 2024), and **LINE** holds ~80% of Japan. They are retained as **recorded exceptions**, carried on SG grounds: mainland China is Singapore's **#1 arrival market** (3.08 M, 2024, STB — official) and ~30% of residents speak Mandarin at home (Census 2020, SingStat — official).
- **Malay (`ms`)** — a Singapore **official language** — and **Vietnamese (`vi`)** (~Telegram's 7th-largest base) both outrank **German**, the weakest shipped locale on both axes. Recorded as **deferred candidates**, not oversights.

## Change — amended, not rewritten

`doc/Technical/technical-0_62_522-09_07_26-0914.md`:

- **§1.2.a** — the prior `[UNVERIFIED]` paragraph, preserved **verbatim** (AU-7).
- **§1.2.b** — the decision record. Adds **Rule L-12** (selection criterion + the zh/ja exception) and **Rule L-13** (revisit trigger: if Soleat becomes *a Singapore food app that happens to be on Telegram* rather than *a Telegram app that happens to be about Singapore food*, re-open L-12 — `ms` and `vi` go first).

Per the standing rule: *"Don't silently rewrite."* The gap stays readable in place, so the trace runs top-to-bottom — the gap existed, evidence was gathered, a human decided.

title: v0.62.524: Cuisine TMA fix — stalled result stream hung forever on slow phones
body:
## What

Operator: *"the UI results experience, sometimes slower phones are not populating the details and caused a letdown."*

## Root cause (traced, not guessed)

My own first hypothesis — a documented **6s client fetch timeout** racing the detail-fetch — was **wrong**. No such constant exists anywhere in the live v2 client (`grep` confirms; the only 6000ms constant is server-side in `footfall-signal.js`, unrelated, and already tightened to 3500ms in v0.62.229).

The real defect is worse: **`web/cuisine/src/v2/lib/api.js`'s `postJsonStream()` NDJSON read loop had no deadline at all.** On a connection that **stalls** — stops delivering bytes without erroring or closing (common on flaky mobile networks) — `reader.read()` never resolves. `searchCuisine()`'s promise never settles → the loading spinner never clears → cards sit on base-only fields (no photos/address/rating/hours/walk-minutes) forever, with **no error state and no retry**.

## Fix

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `api.js` | `STREAM_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS=15000`. Each `reader.read()` races a **per-chunk** stall timer (reset on every chunk — a slow-but-flowing stream is never cut off, only a genuine stall). On stall: `reader.cancel()`, resolve with a best-effort partial tagged `streamStalled: true`, instead of hanging. |
| `App.jsx` | Wires the result into the **existing but previously dead** `degradedNotice` state — an amber, icon+border (colour-blind-safe), already 7-language-authored *"↻ Search hiccup — tap 🔍 to try again"* banner that was declared and rendered but **never triggered anywhere in the codebase**. |

## Verify

- Base `origin/main @ v0.62.523` (069cb7c9), fetched via `gh api …?ref=main`. **Not** the local iCloud tree — found **~70 PRs behind HEAD** mid-fix (unrelated drift, logged below); this PR was built from a fresh scratch clone instead.
- `esbuild` parse ✓ both files.
- Full `vite build` of the Cuisine TMA — clean (2 pre-existing chunk-size warnings, unrelated).
- Full root `npm test -- --run`: **3699/3699 passed**, 144 files.
- Inside the `gia-preflight` trigger set (TMA result render/fetch).

## Known gaps (logged, not bundled into this fix)

1. **`degradedNotice` has no `id` (Indonesian) branch** — pre-existing; it was dead code until this PR gave it a trigger.
2. **`doc/Technical/Technical.md:31`**'s "6s TMA timeout" line is stale — doesn't match the live client. Doc fix, not code; separate pass.
3. **No `[Cuisine-Diag]` equivalent in v2** — added one `console.log` as a placeholder only.
4. **`ResultCard.jsx`'s per-card social-profile fetch has the identical silent-failure shape** (AbortController, no timeout) — deliberately **not** bundled here (one root cause per PR); worth a follow-up.
5. **Local iCloud git tree is ~70 PRs behind `origin/main`** — unrelated housekeeping finding, not part of this fix.

title: v0.62.572 — Cuisine: fix map blackout with a ResizeObserver (map went black full-bleed / behind the fixed header)
body:
Operator (IMG_0730-0734): the map was BLACK across the landscape carousel and
whenever a picker/editor opened. The v0.62.571 narrow resize fix (on
[fill, topInset]) didn't catch it.

Root cause: Google Maps caches its viewport size at init and paints stale /
unloaded (black, worse in monochrome) tiles when its element resizes
underneath it — which now happens on a picker-open full-bleed, the
fixed-header layout, and rotation.

- web/cuisine/src/v2/components/MapPanel.jsx — replaced the effect with a
  ResizeObserver on the map container (rAF-debounced) that re-syncs on EVERY
  size change (`google.maps.event.trigger(map, 'resize')` + keep the centre;
  skips while the element is 0-size), plus a 120 ms first-paint safety net.

title: v0.62.574 — Cuisine: remount-key fixes the tablet map blackout (root cause) + tighter Other picker rows
body:

Root cause of the iPad fullscreen map blackout: the `fill` prop toggled ONE
live MapPanel container between framed (height:68vh) and full-bleed (absolute
inset-0) — an in-place Google Maps canvas resize, which is what paints the map
black on the Telegram-fullscreen WebKit view. Hawker never hits it because it
mounts a separate HawkerMapPanel for framed vs full-bleed (the map remounts,
never resizes).

Fix (follow hawker codes): key <MapPanel> on `cuisine-map-${drawerMode}` on the
tablet (isWide) and a constant `cuisine-map-phone` on phones, so every
framed<->full-bleed / orientation transition remounts a fresh map (no in-place
resize -> no blackout), exactly like Hawker's expand. This also makes the
fill/carousel "tabs-in-front-of-the-full-bleed-map" mode stable+reachable on the
tablet (the header is already sticky top-0 z-30 over the flex-1 fill map) —
the essence of #1 without any backdrop-blur-over-full-bleed overlay.

#2: tightened CountryDropdown + CityDropdown option rows py-1.5 -> py-1 +
leading-tight (operator: "so much row spacing to show countries and cities in

set-location and Putrajaya set-location last month?"

auto-detect resolves the city + a non-ambient re-push slips past D787).

already guards with explicit-pick-wins, but the visibility-refetch applied the

the pick WINS -- the field no longer reverts to the city. Holding the committed

title: v0.62.599 — Transport StationCard: preserve Sun/PH first trains + stop mislabelling no-timing rows as termini
body:
Two P2 findings from the Codex review of the v0.62.598 StationCard
(merged #1607), fixed here as a fresh PR:

1. Sunday/PH first train was dropped. trainTimes() collapsed first_sat
   and first_sun_ph into one weekend value; when Saturday equalled the
   weekday time, the distinct Sun/PH first train (e.g. HarbourFront NEL
   Sun/PH 6:07 vs 5:47) was never shown. Sat (satFirst) and Sun/PH
   (sunFirst) are now kept separate and each rendered only when it
   differs from the weekday time.

2. No-timing rows were always labelled "Terminates here", mislabelling
   TEL stations whose note says timings-unavailable / not-yet-open.
   trainTimes now returns noTimes (not terminal); DirectionRow shows
   "Terminates here" only when the note is a real terminus note (new
   noteIsTerminal /termin/i) or absent, else renders the note verbatim.

i18n: +mrt.sat / +mrt.sunPh (en/fr). Tests updated for the new trainTimes
shape (incl. the Sun/PH regression) + new noteIsTerminal cases.

title: v0.62.612 — viewport: detect a touch tablet from the physical screen so Cuisine stops reverting to the phone layout
body:
Operator (confirmed on iPad/Android touch tablet): the Cuisine TMA keeps
reverting to the phone layout. Root cause: the shared use-viewport hook
classified the device from the LIVE Telegram webview size (innerWidth/Height),
and a tablet required min(w,h) >= 768. Telegram opens/collapses the Mini App to
a partial height, dropping min(w,h) < 768, so a real tablet mis-read as mobile
(phone layout) and could revert mid-session. The tg.js fullscreen gate already
keys off window.screen (physical), so the two disagreed.

Fix (web/_shared/lib/use-viewport.js): a coarse-pointer device whose PHYSICAL
short edge (min(window.screen.w, window.screen.h)) >= 768 is a tablet even when
the transient webview min-dim < 768. Once a tablet, always a tablet, so it can
never flip back to phone. Cannot promote a phone (screen < 768) or a desktop
(fine pointer). Shared across cuisine/hawker/transport.

Verified via Playwright (screen/viewport/touch sims): tablet-collapsed-sheet
OLD=mobile -> NEW=tablet; phone + desktop unchanged. All three builds green;
npm test 3738/3738 across 147 files. Not a regression from recent work (hook
unchanged since v0.62.546).

title: v0.62.635 — Cuisine iPad mini: fix map freeze past zoom 15 (viewport-cull train pills)
body:
Operator P.S. (symptom confirmed = "freezes / becomes unresponsive"): the
Cuisine map hangs when zoomed past 15 on iPad mini.

Root cause: default layers are colour(monochrome)+train; at z>=15
trainTier('cuisine') returns {station:'pill', cap:0}, so all ~180 MRT stations
become heavy named-pill DOM markers and all attach to the map (most off-screen),
and the un-debounced `idle` listener rebuilds the whole set on each zoom-settle
— a main-thread hang on the memory-constrained tablet.

Fix (web/cuisine/src/v2/lib/mapOverlays.js applyVisibility train branch):
viewport-cull at z>=15 — a station outside map.getBounds() (and not the
pinned/tapped one) gets marker.map=null and is skipped (not pushed to items, so
demoteByOverlap only sees on-screen stations). At street-level zoom the visible
set is a handful of stops, not 180; only off-screen pills are dropped.

Cuisine maxZoom stays 20 (the z18/cap23 request was Train-only). Transport is
unaffected — its detail mode caps visibleList to 3 stations.

title: v0.62.647 — vanilla swipe-to-close bottom sheet: assessment + component (44px handle, velocity+distance physics, dvh/VisualViewport, scroll lock), not yet wired
body:
New self-contained component at web/_shared/components/bottom-sheet/ — CSS, canonical
HTML and vanilla JS, no framework and no build step.

- CSS maps every colour to --tg-theme-bg-color / --tg-theme-text-color /
  --tg-theme-hint-color / --tg-theme-section-separator-color, each falling back to this
  repo's mapped --tg-bg/--tg-text/--tg-hint and then to a literal. Surface is OPAQUE
  (a translucent sheet has no guaranteeable contrast over arbitrary map tiles);
  light mode gets a drop shadow, dark mode a hairline top border.
- Responsive: margin-inline auto + max-width 640px (560px at >=700px and in landscape)
  so the sheet is never a full-width slab on iPad or Telegram Desktop; max-height
  88dvh portrait / 78dvh landscape, clamped again by the Visual Viewport height;
  @supports fallback to vh for legacy webviews.
- Handle zone is a real <button> with a minimum 44px hit area.
- JS: trailing-120ms velocity window (a slow drag ending in a flick reads as a flick),
  close on velocity OR total travel distance, upward-flick rebound veto, rubber-banded
  over-drag, separate touch and mouse event families locked by drag.kind, content-to-
  sheet handoff only at scrollTop 0, position:fixed body scroll lock (iOS WKWebView
  ignores overflow:hidden), scrim touchmove swallowed so the map cannot pan behind,
  Visual Viewport listener for software keyboards, Escape + focus trap + focus restore.
- Transitions removed for the whole drag (1:1 finger mapping) and a custom
  cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1) restored on release.

Additive only: no TMA imports it, so Hawker/Transport keep the existing
web/_shared/components/BottomSheet.jsx unchanged until the swap is approved.

title: v0.62.648 — Hawker + Train default to Cuisine's carousel with a list-toggle drawer; fix the Tailwind palette that was silently deleting the drawer handle
body:
Two things, one message.

1. THE DRAWER HANDLE WAS NEVER PAINTED.

Every TMA declared its Telegram palette in tailwind.config.js as raw strings
('tg-hint': 'var(--tg-hint, #98989f)'). Tailwind emits .text-tg-hint from that,
but it CANNOT emit an opacity variant — a raw var() string has nowhere to put
the alpha — so it discards the utility silently. No rule, no warning, no
fallback. Grepping the shipped hawker CSS for bg-tg-hint/70 returned nothing:
the bottom sheet's grabber was a fully transparent 48x6 box. The v0.62.620 pass
that tried to fix the same complaint by enlarging the bar could not have worked.

The same silent drop killed every bg-tg-bg/80 glass bar (so bars meant to be
80% opaque over the map were 100% transparent), every border-tg-accent/50 pill
outline, and 178 rules in total across the five apps.

- NEW web/_shared/lib/tg-colors.js — function-valued palette. No opacity → the
  bare var(); with opacity → a color-mix carrying the alpha. color-mix is
  already a hard dependency (styles.css defines --tg-hint with it).
- All five tailwind.config.js spread ...tgColors. Emitted opacity rules after
  the fix: cuisine 68, menu 39, transport 34, hawker 30, oversight 7.
- BottomSheet.jsx — grab zone 26px -> min 44px; the grabber also carries an
  inline backgroundColor so it can never silently vanish again; release physics
  gain a velocity term shared with the vanilla component, choosing the snap from
  the position projected 140ms forward rather than where the finger stopped.
- NEW __tests__/tg-colors.test.js — 10 tests, including a per-app assertion that
  no config re-inlines a raw tg-* string.

2. CAROUSEL IS NOW THE DEFAULT, AND THE LIST TOGGLE OWNS THE DRAWER.

- Transport: the phone-portrait always-on drawer branch (v0.62.609) is removed.
- Hawker: new viewMode ('carousel' | 'list', default 'carousel') plus a
  ViewToggleButton mirroring Transport's footer pill, and layout.list /
  layout.map i18n keys. The v0.62.642 portrait auto-drawer meant a portrait iPad
  never saw the carousel cards at all.

Both apps now match Cuisine: carousel by default on every device, one explicit
toggle into the over-the-map drawer.

Verification: all five vite builds green; full suite 3791/3791 across 150 files
(was 3781/149); a Playwright layout smoke drove both apps at 744x1133 and
390x844 — 28/28 assertions green (both mount, both default to the carousel with
no drawer, both footers carry the toggle, the toggle opens exactly one drawer
over the map, grab zone measures 44px, the grabber reports a real
non-transparent background at 0.8 opacity, the toggle returns to the carousel,
zero JS errors on all four profiles). Live Telegram client UNVERIFIED
in-sandbox.

Blast radius, flagged deliberately: the palette fix changes rendering across all

title: v0.62.649 — fix the v0.62.648 regression that put NaN in every BARE colour utility; apply the 60% peek / 75% dock glass standard
body:
1. REGRESSION FIX (mine, from v0.62.648).

The function-valued palette assumed opacityValue was absent or numeric. For the
BARE utility it is neither: Tailwind passes the literal string
'var(--tw-bg-opacity)' so bg-opacity-* keeps working. Number() of that is NaN,
so every bare utility emitted

  .bg-tg-card{background-color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--tg-card) NaN%,transparent)}

— invalid CSS, dropped by the browser. v0.62.648 fixed every /NN utility and
broke every bare one, which is far worse. The operator's loading-overlay
screenshot shows it exactly: the card has no fill and its border-tg-accent frame
fell back to currentColor (the black outline).

Any non-finite opacity now falls back to the plain var(), which is the correct
rendering — Tailwind sets --tw-bg-opacity to 1 for the bare utility anyway.
Two regression tests added: the bare-utility var string returns the plain var(),
and no opacity argument shape of any kind can produce NaN.

2. THE GLASS STANDARD, applied uniformly across the three map TMAs.

  active card  opaque                                 (already correct)
  peek cards   bg-tg-card/60 + .liquid-glass          (cuisine was /70; hawker
                                                      + transport were /60 but
                                                      used backdrop-blur-md)
  footer       bg-tg-bg/75 + .liquid-glass-dock       (cuisine /80; hawker /80
                                                      + blur; transport /95)

.liquid-glass-dock was Cuisine-only CSS — hawker's own source comment said so —
and is now ported verbatim into hawker + transport styles.css, so all three
share one dock treatment. These surfaces were authored with these opacities long
ago; the palette bug meant they had never rendered, which is what put the
numbers up for review in the first place.

Verification: all five vite builds green, and the emitted stylesheets checked
directly — zero NaN in any of the five, bare utilities emit var(--tg-*), /NN
utilities still emit color-mix, bg-tg-card/60 and bg-tg-bg/75 present in all
three map apps. Full suite 3793/3793 across 150 files (was 3791). The two-app
Playwright smoke was extended with paint assertions and rerun — 36/36 green,
including a bare bg-tg-* utility computing to an OPAQUE colour (alpha exactly 1,
the direct regression guard) and the footer dock computing to alpha 0.75, on
both apps at both viewports. Live Telegram client UNVERIFIED in-sandbox.

Lesson recorded in the journal: v0.62.648's tests passed while shipping this.

title: v0.62.650 — Train card density pass (disclosure back on the name strip, line names that fit, "Normal" gone, amenities as text, 2/3-column list) + Cuisine 2px gap
body:
CUISINE. ResultDrawer's bottom offset becomes calc(4.5rem|6rem + 2px). The gap
was zero on purpose — v0.62.277/285 dropped the strip to hug the dock ("no gap")
— so the card's bottom pill sat flush on the "S$xx ~ xx · N gems | ★ …" bar.

TRAIN, the operator's six items.

1. The collapse disclosure moves off the card foot and back onto the name strip
   as a right-aligned word + triangle; the foot pill is deleted. That reclaimed
   row is where most of the height parity between a 2-line and a 1-line card
   comes from. The strip itself still does NOT toggle — only the button does — so
   a card tap still bubbles to onTap and focuses the map (v0.62.641 must not
   regress).
3. Line-name font steps with the station's line count: 12px single, 11px two,
   10px three-or-more, so "East-West" / "Downtown" / "Thomson-East Coast" fit
   instead of truncating to "East-We…". The operator's point 3 was truncated
   mid-sentence; they picked full-names-smaller-font when asked.
4. "Normal service" is gone from the per-line row and the collapsed summary —
   the coloured dot carries it (title attribute for hover/AT) and the word
   appears only when a line is NOT normal. Paired with a new disruption TAB above
   the card (same construction as the v0.62.646 "future" tab, status colour, ⚠ +
   word), so the exception is the loudest thing on the card, not the quietest.
5. Exits and bus stops drop the bordered pill for plain link-coloured text, one
   per row — which is what lets the description fit. Three new pure helpers:
   exitLabel (the rich feed says `label`, station-exits.json says `exit`, and
   Paya Lebar's own array mixes "Exit A" with bare "E" — the card read `.label`
   only, hence the bare letters), busStopDesc, dedupeBusStops (the feed repeated
   81111 three times).
6. List grid goes 1 → 2 columns on a phone and 2/3 → 3 on every tablet/desktop in
   both orientations; a new .gia-list-dense class steps every absolute
   text-[Npx] inside the drawer grid down by exactly 1px — needed because the
   card's type is absolute, so no rem/em scale on an ancestor could reach it.

Honest gaps, stated rather than buried: exact pixel-equal height for a 2-line vs
1-line card is not achievable while both lines show — the changes close most of
it but a 2-line card is still one row taller. Bus-stop descriptions render only
when the server supplies them; the blanks in the screenshot come from an
unpopulated Redis stop-metadata hash, which the client cannot fix. Exits have no
description in the data at all — what shipped is the full normalised label.

title: v0.62.651 — viewport-width columns (2/3/4), the line-order legibility fix for non-locals, and tap-to-blink
body:
1. DYNAMIC COLUMNS.

Device-class buckets cannot answer this. An iPad in landscape (1133px) and a
desktop window (1440px+) are both `isWide`, but only one has room for four
readable cards — and no device guess re-flows when a Telegram Desktop window is
resized. Both the Train list and the Hawker drawer list now use viewport-width
breakpoints: grid-cols-2 / min-[700px]:grid-cols-3 / xl:grid-cols-4.

700px is deliberate, not Tailwind's md default of 768: the iPad mini is 744px
wide in portrait and v0.62.650 shipped the operator's explicit request for THREE
columns there, which a 768 breakpoint would have silently broken. 700 is also
TABLET_MIN_EDGE in classify-viewport.js, so the CSS and the JS classifier now
agree on where a tablet starts.

2. THE FOREIGNER PROBLEM — the substantive one.

MRT stations are an ORDERED SEQUENCE, and a single column encoded that for free:
reading down the list IS travelling along the line. Two, three or four columns
destroy it — nothing says whether to read across or down, and a visitor has no
reason to know that EW1 -> EW2 -> EW3 counts along the track. The grid was
silently discarding the one piece of information a stranger needs most.

Fixed without giving up the columns: a line-order header above the grid (line
badge, full line name, both termini with a direction arrow, stop count) and an
explicit ordinal on every card ("3/35") on the name strip. Together the order is
readable at ANY column count, which is what a width-driven grid requires.
Rendered only where a sequence exists, so the carousel is untouched.

3. TAP TO BLINK.

The jump already worked (setCenter + zoom 18, v0.62.634) but there was no blink,
so on a busy map — especially in LIST mode, where the drawer covers the lower
half — you could not tell which pin the tap had landed on. Cuisine's flashPin
ported into MrtMapPanel as a focusedStation effect: a transient expanding ring in
the line's own colour, ~1.6s, then removed. It draws no permanent marker and
never touches the pin layer, so it cannot interfere with renderPins' lifecycle.

Hawker got the same breakpoint grid — the operator hadn't checked it on desktop
and it had the identical problem (isWide collapsed iPad-landscape and desktop
into one 2-column layout).

Verification: transport + hawker builds green; full suite 3806/3806 across 151
files. The Playwright smoke was extended to seven device profiles (adding hawker
desktop 1440x900, transport iPad-landscape 1133x744, transport desktop 1440x900)
and given a real coarse-station stub so the Train grid actually renders — all
green, with the column count asserted from computed gridTemplateColumns at every
width: 390->2, 744->3, 1133->3, 1440->4, in both apps. The blink is unverified on
a live map (Google Maps cannot render in-sandbox).

Also: a {/* … */} comment opening a parenthesised JSX expression broke the build
a fifth time (hawker). The tma-hook-deps-tdz guard test caught it.

title: v0.62.652 — carousel card count scales to ultrawide: the basis ladder AND the track cap were both holding it down
body:
Two separate ceilings; fixing only one would not have moved the number.

1. THE BASIS LADDER stopped at md (768px): basis-[60%] / sm:31% / md:22% and
   nothing beyond, so a 1920px desktop showed the SAME ~4.5 cards as a 768px
   tablet — every extra pixel went into making each card wider rather than
   showing more of the line. Extended to xl:17% / min-[1600px]:13.5% /
   min-[2000px]:11% for the Train, and xl:24% / min-[1600px]:19% /
   min-[2000px]:16% for Hawker + Cuisine (their cards carry more content each,
   so they need more width each).

2. THE TRACK ITSELF was capped — Transport's carousel at max-w-6xl (1152px) and
   Cuisine's at max-w-[1600px] — so on a 2560px ultrawide the carousel occupied
   less than half the screen and the ladder could not express itself. Now
   xl:max-w-none (Transport) and min-[1800px]:max-w-none (Cuisine). This is the
   one that actually unlocked ultrawide: before it, 1920 and 2560 both measured
   exactly 8.0 cards.

min-w-[9rem] added as a floor on the Train card so the top of the ladder can
never squeeze a card below readable width; the track scrolls instead.

On "aspect ratio", stated rather than silently substituted: how many cards fit
ACROSS is width divided by card width. Aspect ratio only enters via height, which
changes how tall a card may be (max-h-[52vh]), not how many sit side by side. So
the ladder is keyed to width, all the way to ultrawide.

Verification: transport + hawker + cuisine builds green; full suite 3806/3806
across 151 files. The Playwright smoke gained a measured card-fit probe (track
width divided by real card width from getBoundingClientRect, not a class-string
check) and three new profiles. Measured before -> after: transport 1440 4.5->6.4,
transport 1920 ~4.5->8.1, transport 2560 8.0->9.9, hawker 1920 3.3->6.0. All
green across ten device profiles. Live client UNVERIFIED in-sandbox.

Caveat: those are card SLOTS, not cards fully in focus — the end cards still
render as glass half-peeks, so fully-opaque cards number ~2 fewer.

title: v0.62.653 — the one qualified line name gets its own row; every line-name step drops 1px
body:
"East-West Line (Changi br…" was the worst of both: the qualifier was present
and unreadable.

Scope checked before building: grepping data/stations.json shows EXACTLY ONE
line in the LTA feed carries a parenthetical qualifier — "East-West Line (Changi
branch)" — against nine plain names. So the fix must leave the other nine
visually identical, and it does.

- NEW pure helper splitLineName(name, canonical) in station-card-utils.js:
  splits a trailing parenthetical into {main, qualifier}. When the caller
  supplies a canonical name it wins, because data/stations.json says "Changi
  branch" while lines.js — and the line chip the user just tapped — says "Changi
  Airport Branch". Matching what is already on screen beats echoing the feed's
  shorthand. Guarded so a canonical name equal to the main name can never render
  "X (X)".
- LineSubCard renders the qualifier on its own row beneath the line name, and
  every step of the font ladder drops 1px per the operator's blanket
  instruction: name 12/11/10 -> 11/10/9 by line count, qualifier 9px (8px on a
  3-line interchange).
- StationCard imports LINES_BY_CODE to supply the canonical name.

Verification: transport build green; full suite 3811/3811 across 151 files (was
3806) — +5 splitLineName tests covering the real feed string, the canonical-name
preference, all nine unqualified names left untouched, the "X (X)" guard, and
totality. The ten-profile Playwright smoke rerun all green. Live client
UNVERIFIED in-sandbox.

Note on scope: the 1px step-down applies to the line-name ladder, not to every
string on the card. The instruction was conditional ("if cannot see the whole
description") and the line-name row is the one that was truncating;
blanket-shrinking the card would have undone tuning from v0.62.643-650.

title: v0.62.654 — three TMAs on one behaviour; a real auto-expand listener; one definition of "wide"
body:
The fullscreen GATE was already byte-identical across the three apps (diffed in
the prior audit). What was missing was listening for the result.

1. AUTO-EXPAND, a real bug. useViewport re-measured on resize, visualViewport
   resize, orientationchange — and three HARD-CODED TIMERS at 250/700/1500ms,
   which are a guess at when Telegram finishes resizing the webview after
   requestFullscreen(). Telegram announces it exactly, via fullscreenChanged and
   viewportChanged, and nothing was listening: a transition slower than 1500ms
   left the layout stuck on the pre-expand classification for the whole session,
   with nothing to re-measure until the user resized or rotated. Both events are
   now subscribed and unsubscribed in the shared hook, so all five TMAs gain it.

2. CUISINE BROUGHT INTO LINE. Removed the v0.62.564 effect that FORCED
   drawerMode by orientation whenever isWide (so a wide portrait device could not
   stay on the carousel — every rotation reset the choice), and the gate that hid
   the list/map toggle in wide landscape (which left a desktop user with no route
   to the list at all). All three now default to the carousel everywhere with one
   explicit toggle.

3. ONE DEFINITION OF "WIDE". GRID_BREAKPOINTS + LIST_GRID_CLASS +
   gridColumnsForWidth exported from classify-viewport.js, with a guard test
   asserting both app grids carry the declared literal and reintroduce neither
   md: nor lg: grid-cols.

REGRESSION I CAUSED AND CAUGHT, worth recording: writing LIST_GRID_CLASS as a
TEMPLATE INTERPOLATION put an un-evaluated arbitrary-width variant into a file
inside every app's Tailwind content glob. Tailwind read it as a mixed-unit
screens config and DISABLED the arbitrary min-width/max-width variants entirely,
silently dropping the 3-column rule from all five stylesheets — the iPad mini and
iPad landscape lost their third column, and the only sign was one "warn -" line.
Caught by the ten-profile smoke, not the unit tests. Fixed to a plain literal —
and then the explanatory COMMENT re-triggered it, because the scanner reads
comments too. Two guards added: the test asserts the declaration line contains no
interpolation, and the smoke measures computed columns.

Verification: all five builds green with ZERO Tailwind warnings (confirmed absent
in all five and confirmed present on the broken intermediate); full suite
3821/3821 across 152 files (was 3811/151); ten-profile smoke all green with
columns measured from computed gridTemplateColumns at 390/744/1133/1440/1920/
2560; a new expand-check harness drives all three apps with a Telegram stub that
records handlers, fires fullscreenChanged, then simulates a LATE expand to 1440
after the old timers would have expired — all three wired, no errors. Live client
UNVERIFIED in-sandbox.

Remaining gap, stated: Cuisine's list is still page-flow, not an over-the-map
BottomSheet drawer. Defaults and toggles now match; the list's presentation does
not. That wants its own PR.

title: v0.62.655 — Cuisine's result list becomes an over-the-map drawer, opening at a measured 1.5 cards
body:
Closes the last consistency delta from the audit: Cuisine's vertical result list
had NEVER been a drawer. It sat in page flow BELOW the map, which is exactly why
Cuisine was the one map app without the over-the-map layer Hawker and Train have
had since v0.62.648. Defaults and toggles were aligned at v0.62.654; this aligns
the presentation.

- Shared BottomSheet gains an optional peekPx prop that overrides the COLLAPSED
  snap with a real PIXEL height instead of a viewport fraction. This is the
  mechanism behind "1.5 card height": 1.5 cards is a fact about the CARD, not
  about the screen, so a vh fraction lands right on one device and wrong on every
  other. The fraction stays as the fallback, so Hawker and Train are untouched.
- Cuisine's map is now full-bleed in BOTH modes. Because `fill` no longer varies,
  the v0.62.574 framed↔full REMOUNT — which existed only to dodge the iPad
  blackout on an in-place canvas resize — has nothing left to guard against, and
  the remount key is now constant.
- The ~350-line ResultPanel is WRAPPED IN PLACE by a new ResultSheetShell, which
  renders a BottomSheet when list mode is active and a bare fragment otherwise.
  Wrapping rather than relocating keeps every existing ref, scroll handler,
  pagination hook and flash-highlight wiring untouched — the panel does not know
  it is inside a sheet — and horizontal mode is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The collapsed height is MEASURED from the first real rendered card
  (1.5 * cardHeight + 44px handle band), re-measured on resize and after 400ms,
  so the half-card cut off at the fold is correct on every device.

Caught by the guard test: my measurement effect's dependency array referenced
`cursor`, declared LATER in the component. A dep array is evaluated during
render, so that would have thrown "Cannot access 'cursor' before initialization"
on every render — a white screen. tma-hook-deps-tdz.test.js caught it before any
build did; second time that guard has paid for itself this session.

Verification: cuisine build green; full suite 3821/3821 across 152 files; the
ten-profile Hawker/Train smoke rerun all green (unchanged, as intended); a new
Cuisine harness mounts at 390x844, 1024x1366 and 1440x900 with zero JS errors.

HONEST GAP: the drawer's RENDERED state is UNVERIFIED. Reaching Cuisine list mode
needs a full venue-search round trip that cannot be stubbed cheaply in-sandbox,
so the 1.5-card peek, the handle and the drag are proven by construction and by
the shared component's own tests, not by observation. This is the change most
likely to need a second pass — check it first.

Because that permanently bloats every future clone, the choice went to the operator with a ~20 MB reduced-mirror alternative. **The operator chose the full mirror, exactly per protocol** — maximum reproducibility, accepting the size cost. The choice and its reasoning are recorded verbatim in `VAULT_README.md`, so the decision is auditable rather than inferred.

title: v0.62.657 — Cuisine drawer device check found two real bugs: native swipe conflict, and a peek selector matching nothing
body:
The device check you did (screenshot `IMG_3693`) is the O-56 check flagged as highest-priority since v0.62.655. It found the shipment was broken in **two independent ways**, confirming the caution recorded at the time was warranted.

## Bug 1 — pulling the handle drags the whole Mini App

`web/cuisine/src/api/tg.js` never called `disableVerticalSwipes()`. Hawker and Transport both call it (v0.62.610) because **Telegram's own vertical swipe-to-minimise competes with a draggable `BottomSheet` handle for the same downward drag — and, being native, always wins.** Cuisine never needed this before v0.62.655 because it never had a draggable drawer; the moment it gained one it inherited the exact bug the other two apps had already fixed.

Now wired identically, feature-detected for Bot API 7.7+.

## Bug 2 — the drawer never actually collapsed to a card height

The peek-height selector was `'[data-venue-card], article, .skeuo-card'` — and **none of the three exist anywhere in `ResultCard.jsx`** (grep-verified). Its root is a plain `<button data-pid={venue.placeId} className="w-full text-left rounded-lg border …">`. `listPeekPx` was therefore **permanently `null`** in production, and the sheet was always on its `0.80`-fraction fallback — nowhere near "1 card", exactly matching what your screenshot showed.

Fixed to `[data-pid]` — the same selector `ResultPanel.jsx` already uses for its own scroll-into-view logic. Multiplier also dropped **1.5 → 1** per your revised ask.

## The pattern, again

This is the **fourth** occurrence this arc of the same failure shape already logged at Register D-22–D-24: a declaration or selector matching nothing, failing silently, degrading to a fallback indistinguishable from a design choice. Every prior instance was a Tailwind class string; this one is a DOM selector — same shape, different layer.

## Verification

- `cuisine` build green; full suite **3821/3821 across 152 files**.
- The ten-profile Hawker/Train smoke and the three-viewport Cuisine mount harness both rerun all green (unaffected — neither touched file is shared).
- A **new targeted regression harness** confirms `disableVerticalSwipes()` fires on Cuisine init, and that `[data-pid]` matches a live element exactly as `ResultCard` renders it.

## Still not end-to-end verified

This fix corrects the two mechanisms a static read could prove broken. It does **not** run a live venue search and drag the real handle — that round trip still cannot be stubbed in-sandbox. Your screenshot remains the only evidence this drawer has ever rendered at all (logged as **O-62**).

title: v0.62.664 — URGENT: fix Telegram Desktop TMA unable to close (Menu, Clipboard, Oversight)
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: v0.62.663 (merged in #1668, ~45 min before this report) widened Menu's auto-fullscreen gate to Telegram Desktop and added a brand-new fullscreen step to Clipboard and Oversight — without checking that each already had a way to close once `requestFullscreen()` hides Telegram's native window chrome on desktop. Menu's own long-standing comment already named this exact failure mode ("fullscreen takeover with no chrome and no easy exit"), which is why desktop was originally excluded from its gate. ## Summary

**v0.62.680 — three Register follow-ups**

- **O-89 (M3 non-adoption, confirmed)** — recorded a permanent-exclusion decision in
  `web/_shared/lib/m3-tokens.js`: M3's literal type scale and literal elevation-shadow values are
  standing exclusions from any future M3 pass (the type scale runs larger than this dense mobile
  chrome already uses; the elevation shadows would overwrite Cuisine's glass system and
  Hawker/Transport/Menu's skeuomorphic system). Documentation-as-code only — no runtime change.
- **O-91 (SORT half)** — new `michelin-sort.js` implements
  `instr/GIA_Michelin_Footer_Pagination_AI_Prompt.md` §2's deterministic order (newest applicable
  *selected* award year → category rank 3★/2★/1★/Bib → alphabetical), wired into `index.js`'s
  `handleMichelinSearch` in place of the old `TIER_ORDER`-sort-plus-Fisher-Yates-shuffled-Bib
  pipeline. The shuffle only existed to vary Bib Gourmand exposure across taps; the spec's full
  determinism supersedes it (flagged in the Journal in case that variety was actually wanted).
  Dead `TIER_ORDER` constant removed. 9 new tests.
- **O-92 (pager / Back-End button overlap)** — the Michelin pager's `‹`/`›` used the omnidirectional
  `.gia-hit` touch-target class (8px invisible extension on every side), reaching horizontally into
  the adjacent Back/End button's grid cell in the same footer row. Switched to `.gia-hit-y`, the
  directional variant `styles.css` already documents for this "tightly-packed row" case. Zero
  visible-pixel change.

**v0.62.681 — two device-reported Cuisine regressions** (both: a guess standing in for a measurement)

- **First-load wait message** — the report was that an audit removed it. That was checked
  commit-by-commit and **disproved**: the overlay condition is unchanged since v0.62.484, and
  v0.62.671's only Cuisine edit was the Widen-switch thumb offset. The real cause is that nothing
  guaranteed the message stayed on screen long enough to read — the splash gate opens and fires the
  boot load in one commit, so a fast-settling boot search flips `loading` false within a frame or
  two and "Finding eateries…" flashes past. Added `bootOverlayHold`, a 900 ms minimum dwell armed
  only on the gate's boot-load branch (the saved≠device mismatch branch still opens an empty TMA
  with no hourglass), cleared by a timer that always fires and by 🛑 Stop.
- **Carousel card vs. the recommendation strip** — `ResultDrawer`'s bottom offset was the hardcoded
  guess `hasFilters ? '6rem' : '4.5rem'`, left over from v0.62.186 when the filter chips were their
  own full-width row. Since v0.62.192/281 they are the inline "Criteria (N) ▾" pill, so the footer's
  height no longer moves with filters — yet the drawer still lifted 24px whenever criteria existed,
  which is exactly the first-open-vs-later asymmetry reported. Now driven by a measured `stripLiftPx`
  (reads `.insight-glass`'s real top edge, scoped to the footer ref), holding the card a consistent
  2px above the strip in every state. Same measure-don't-guess fix as v0.62.674's footer reserve;
  the old `calc()` stays as a first-paint fallback only.

  `__tests__/michelin-sort.test.js`), including `tma-hook-deps-tdz.test.js`.
- `npx vite build` (cuisine) — green.
- Manual/device:

    year, 3★ → 2★ → 1★ → Bib.
  - Narrow phone: tap near the pager's `›` and the adjacent "↩ Back"/"🔚 End" and confirm taps land
    on the intended control.
  - Cold open: "Confirming your location…" → a readable "Finding eateries…" → results; 🛑 Stop

  - Carousel gap: with no cuisine picked, the card should sit ~2px above the "S$xx ~ xx · N gems"

title: v0.62.684–689 — carousel card spec (D-51), footer/glass fixes, four-corner ring labels, station-pick inspection overlay
body:
Six patch versions in one arc. The first three standardise the carousel card; the last three fix
two bugs found on the way and add the operator-approved station-pick inspection overlay.

## v0.62.684 — Cuisine carousel card spec (D-51)

**Width — one rule.** `basis-[min(82%,20rem)]` replaces the six-rung viewport-width ladder from
v0.62.652. That ladder produced 265→609px and was **non-monotonic**: an iPad mini in *portrait*
(744px, 24px under Tailwind's `md`) inherited the phone's 82% → **531px**, while the same device in
*landscape* took the 44% rung → **436px**. That inversion is exactly what was reported. The new rule
reproduces the operator's stated de facto exactly — 265px @375, 278px @393, **320px everywhere
else** — across all 12 device×orientation configs.

The audit also surfaced what had *not* been reported: **phone landscape rendered a 609px card**,
wider than the iPad mini case that prompted the work.

**Height — two collapsed tiers.** One global height is arithmetically impossible (phone landscape has
375–393px of viewport *total*; iPad mini portrait has 1133). `h-[13rem]` standard / `h-[7.5rem]`
short, `overflow-hidden` so the height is a guarantee. New `isShort` flag keys off viewport
**height**, never orientation.

**Truncation** — dish-hint and address go `truncate` → `line-clamp-2`. **Address** — new shared
`abbrev-address.js` drops a trailing postcode (end-anchored, so street numbers survive) and
abbreviates spelled-out states. **Glyphs** — `▸`/`▾`, lifted out of the i18n values.

## v0.62.685–686 — Hawker/Train audit, footer bug, liquid glass

| Device | Orient | Cuisine (new) | Hawker (before) | Transport |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 15 Pro | portrait | 278 | 278 | 217 |
| iPhone 15 Pro | landscape | 320 | 327 | 172 |
| **iPad mini** | **portrait** | 320 | **531** ❌ | 212 |
| **iPad mini** | **landscape** | 320 | **436** ❌ | 229 |
| iPad Pro 12.9″ | landscape | 320 | 287 | 214 |
| Desktop 1440 | — | 320 | 302 | 225 |

**Hawker carried the identical ladder and the identical inversion** — same one-line fix.
**Transport is deliberately left alone**: 164–229px *by design*, and crucially **no inversion**, so
it does not have the bug this work exists to fix. One outlier reported for decision (phone landscape
164px, ~7 tiles). **Glyphs unified across all three** — 48 strings de-glyphed.

**Footer placement bug.** `top`/`end` were not on the right. The row is `grid-cols-[1fr_auto_1fr]`
but its MIDDLE child is conditional, so with neither criteria nor pager present, Grid auto-placement
dropped the right cluster into column 2 and `justify-self-end` aligned it to *that* column's end.
`col-start-3` pins it. It looked correct in older screenshots only because a "Criteria (1)" pill
happened to be filling column 2.

**Liquid glass was structurally absent on wide screens.** The in-focus card surface was a flat
`bg-white` with no glass class; only half-peeking end cards got `.liquid-glass`. On a wide screen
*every* visible card is in focus, so the design never rendered there. New `.liquid-glass-focus`
(separate class — the dark-mode `!important` background would collide with the focused card's
light-palette var override). Honours `prefers-reduced-transparency`.

## v0.62.687 — the composer field, corrected

v0.62.683 matched the composer against `LocationField`'s **inner closed button**
(`border-tg-border`). The box the operator is actually looking at is the **outer surface**,
`loc-field-surface` — a named colour decision (`#cbd5e1` light / yellow-400 dark), not a theme
token, so `border-tg-border` was never going to land on it however it resolved. Also: details toggle
tightened + lightened (`px-1.5`, `/30` border, `/70` text) in Cuisine and Hawker.

## v0.62.688 — ring labels: four points on EVERY ring, at 9px

Previously a single NORTH label unless the ring was `fourSide` or exceeded `LARGE_RING_M`. That
default had **already produced two operator reports**, each patched one ring class at a time
(v0.62.543 by size, v0.62.586 by role). Making the four-point treatment universal ends the sequence
instead of adding a third exception.

Ring-activation audit, as asked: there is no toggle and no automatic draw anywhere — rings exist only
where a `ringLayer.draw()` call exists. Cuisine passes `results` (up to 3 rings); Hawker passes none
(always 2); **Transport had no ring layer at all**.

## v0.62.689 — station-pick inspection overlay (Hawker + Train)

One temporary amber pin per pick, its rings, and the **nearest 3 hawker centres**. Scoped as
approved: **station-only** (no road geocoding this round), **inspection overlay only** — the pin
never becomes the search anchor, never changes the active region, never re-ranks the card list, and
never survives a tap-out (D-53).

- New `web/_shared/lib/temp-pin.js`: `nearestByDistance`, `shortDist`, `tempPinNode`,
  `nearbyCentreNode`, `loadAllHawkerCentres`, `createInspectLayer`. The centre loader lives in
  `_shared` because **neither host had the full list** — Hawker's App holds only the active region,
  Transport's equivalent fetch is module-private to its own `mapOverlays.js`.
- **A DOM pin rather than 📍** (D-52): U+1F4CD is a colour emoji — the font supplies its own red
  artwork and CSS `color` cannot touch it, so "bold bright orangy-yellow" is unreachable that way.
  Three options surfaced; the custom amber pin was chosen. It also matches existing practice —
  `stationPillNode`, `busTierNode`, `amenityLabelNode` are all styled DOM.
- **Hawker's station field was inert.** Both `` instances had been rendered
  with **no `onSelectStation` at all** since v0.62.659 — a pick did nothing. Found while building
  this, not reported.
- **Train gains a ring layer** for the first time. No `showVenueTransit` there — the picked point IS
  a station, so "nearest stations" around it says nothing.
- Zoom 15 phone / 17 wide, from the existing `TAP_ZOOM_PHONE`/`TAP_ZOOM_WIDE`; read from a ref, since
  the globals that consume it register once and would otherwise pin the boot-time breakpoint.
- Nearby pills **always** show their distance (D-54): in the outer rail network the 3rd-nearest
  centre can be kilometres out, and the 750 m walk ring must never imply it is walkable.

## Known trades, flagged before approval

- **This reverses v0.62.577**, which removed a `max-w-[22rem]` cap because it gave *"more, flatter
  cards instead of a prominent centre + two glass half-peeks."* iPad mini landscape now shows ~3.0
  cards vs ~2.3. Surfaced twice and accepted.
- **Height numbers are arithmetic, not measurement** (no render harness, O-93) — likely one device
  tuning pass. Short tier shipped at 7.5rem, not the 7rem quoted (7rem couldn't fit a Michelin strip).
- **Hawker's height tiers use Hawker-sized values** (`8rem`/`5.5rem`), not Cuisine's 13/7.5 — its
  collapsed card carries 4 rows against Cuisine's 10. The spec is standardised; the pixels follow
  content. Tracked as O-109 if literal lockstep is wanted.
- **Road/address geocoding is not built** (O-110) — scoped to "station-only for now".
- **The overlay has never been seen on a device** (O-111): whether the amber pin reads against the
  greyscale base map, and whether three centre pills crowd at zoom 15, build and tests cannot answer.

## Test plan

- All touched TMA builds green (`_shared` changed, so consumers rebuilt).
- `npm test -- --run` — **155 files / 3884 tests** green, +28 across the arc.
- Compiled CSS grepped to confirm `.basis-[min(82%,20rem)]`, `.h-[13rem]`, `.h-[7.5rem]`,
  `.h-[8rem]`, `.h-[5.5rem]`, `.col-start-3`, `.liquid-glass-focus`, `.loc-field-surface`,
  `.border-tg-accent/30`, `.text-tg-accent/70` are actually **emitted** — the D-22…D-28
  silent-Tailwind-drop failure mode.
- Bundle greps confirm the new wiring shipped: `giaHawkerInspect` in the hawker bundle,
  `giaMrtInspect` + `centres-by-region` in the transport bundle.
- Device: iPad mini portrait and landscape should now match; address should no longer end in "…";
  ▸ should flip to ▾; `top`/`end` should sit hard right with no criteria pill; a station pick in
  Hawker/Train should drop one amber pin with rings and three labelled centres.

## Docs

`journal-0_62_684/687/689`, `register-0_62_684/687/689`; D-51…D-54 recorded; O-106…O-111 opened;
`.serial-state.yml` re-anchored to 01-08 '26 14:25 SGT (sovereign `data.gov.sg` source, TF-6/TF-9).
