title: v0.62.690 — road & address search via OneMap (closes O-110)
body:
The other half of the operator's original inspection-overlay request. v0.62.689 shipped *"train"*;
this ships *"road"* — closing **O-110**, which was opened one arc ago when that work was scoped to
"station-only for now".

## Upstream: OneMap, not Google Places (D-55)

The repo already had a working, authenticated, cached, rate-limited Google Places autocomplete pair
(`/api/cuisine/place-autocomplete` + `/place-resolve`). Reusing it would have been the shortest path.
It was rejected on three counts:

1. **Cost** — Places Autocomplete is billable, so a new caller is a spend decision (gate G4, default
   no). OneMap's `common/elastic/search` is **free and keyless**.
2. **Fitness** — the ask is *roads*. Places has no road-only type filter; OneMap returns
   `ROAD_NAME` / `BLK_NO` / `POSTAL` as first-class fields.
3. **Precedent** — OneMap is already this project's SG-authoritative source
   (`scripts/fetch-hawker-coords.js` calls this exact endpoint; `data/mrt-coords.json` was curated
   from OneMap geocodes in v0.62.519) and is **already legally cleared** in `doc/Legal` with the
   attribution "Source: OneMap / SLA". No new legal surface.

The feature is Singapore-only by construction (hawker centres, MRT), so OneMap's SG-only coverage
costs nothing here.

### A trap in the payload

The keyless call returns a top-level `"error": "Authentication token missing…"` **alongside a fully
populated `results` array**. Any caller that branches on `error` throws away good data. Both the
parser and the route key off `results` only, and the module header says so explicitly so the next
reader doesn't "fix" it.

### Correcting a standing doc note

`doc/Register/register-0_61_76` records *"the sandbox cannot reach OneMap"* (D-61.63). That is true
of `public/nearbysvc/getNearestBusStops`, which needs `ONEMAP_API_KEY`. It is **not** true of
`common/elastic/search`, which answers unauthenticated — verified reachable from the sandbox while
building this. Recorded as an AU-7 amendment that *narrows* the prior note rather than contradicting
it: left as-is, a future session would read it as "OneMap is unreachable" and reach for a paid
geocoder, which is exactly the decision this arc avoided.

## Two list-quality bugs the live payloads caught

Both were found by running **real** responses through the parser, not by reading the API docs.
Neither would have failed a build, a lint, or the tests written before the fixtures were captured.

- **Dedup by coordinate was not enough (D-56).** The first implementation keyed on `name|lat|lng`,
  which reads as obviously correct. A live `Jalan Kayu` query returns **six rows all titled "Jalan
  Kayu Estate"**, each a different house at different coordinates — nothing collapsed. Dedup is now
  **by name**. The cost is real and accepted: the live `Bishan` payload has "Bishan Loft" at blocks
  31 and 33, ~60 m apart, which now collapse to one row. Right for an *inspection* overlay answering
  "roughly here"; wrong for a booking flow.
- **ERP gantries are ordinary results (D-57).** On `Orchard Road`, **three of the first six rows**
  were toll gantries ("Orchard Road After Ymca - ERP(47)"). Filtered.

Measured on the live fixtures:

| Query | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `Orchard Road` | 6 rows, 3 of them ERP gantries | 5 useful — the road, a post office, a church, a hotel |
| `Jalan Kayu` | 6 rows, all "Jalan Kayu Estate" | 2 distinct |
| `Bishan` | 6 rows, "Bishan Loft" twice | 6 distinct, incl. **Bishan MRT Station** |

## What changed

**`onemap-search.js`** (NEW, root, CommonJS — beside `michelin-sort.js` / `places-address-parser.js`,
the existing home for server-side pure modules). Payload normalisation, `titleCase` that keeps
initialisms (MRT/NUS/HDB) upper and leaves `20A` alone, `addressLabel` → `"20 Bideford Road ·
S(229921)"`, handling for OneMap's literal `"NIL"`, SG bbox filter.

**`GET /api/geo/road-search`** — Redis `onemap:search:v1:{q}` at **24 h** (road geometry doesn't
move), 3-character floor, 6 s timeout. On any failure returns `{results: [], error:
'upstream_unavailable'}` rather than a 5xx, because the station half of the field must keep working
when OneMap doesn't.

**Auth — a deliberate non-gate (D-58).** Unauthenticated, on a neutral `/api/geo/` prefix, matching
`/api/transport/stations` and `/api/hawker/centres-by-region` — which **this same field already calls
unauthenticated**. Public catalogue data, no per-user payload, no billable upstream. `/api/cuisine/*`
would have bought free auth but misstated ownership. Since there's no chatId to key on,
`makeRateLimiter` gained an optional **`keyFn`** (default unchanged, so all five existing call sites
are behaviourally identical) and this route passes `req.ip`, cap 300/15 min. The limiter protects
**OneMap's service**, not a budget.

**`StationLocationField`** — roads are a **second section in the same box**, not a second field. The
two halves are deliberately asymmetric: stations stay a local substring filter (instant, offline,
**listed first, never waiting on the network**), addresses are a 250 ms-debounced call with the
`addrQuery` stale-response guard ported from Cuisine's `LocationField` (added there after Codex
review #216). If OneMap is slow or down, typing "Bishan" still resolves the station immediately and
the address section simply doesn't appear — that ordering *is* the failure plan. Section headers only
render when both kinds are present, so a station-only result set looks exactly as before. Copy
widened to "station or road" across all 8 locales.

**Hosts** — both selections call the same `onSelectStation` with `kind: 'station' | 'address'`.
**Hawker needed no change** (coordinate-based). **Transport did**: an address has no codes or lines,
so reaching `setFocusedStation` would render a StationCard detail panel for something that isn't a
station.

## Test plan

- `node --check` on all three changed `.js`; hawker + transport builds green.
- `npm test -- --run` — **156 files / 3901 tests** green, +17 new.
- Compiled CSS confirmed to emit `text-[10px]`, `uppercase`, `tracking-wide`, `text-tg-hint/80`,
  `border-t` in both bundles; `road-search` present in both JS bundles.
- **Live upstream exercised** for `Orchard Road` / `Bishan` / `Jalan Kayu` / `Toa Payoh Lor 6` / a
  deliberate miss. Every fixture in `__tests__/onemap-search.test.js` is trimmed from those real
  responses.
- Device: typing 3+ characters should show a "Roads & addresses" section under the stations;
  picking one should drop the amber pin with rings and the nearest 3 centres, and in Train must
  **not** open a station card.

## Known gaps

- **The route was never executed end-to-end in-sandbox (O-112).** The agent proxy returns 405 to this
  repo's axios (1.15.2; `/root/.ccr/README.md` documents that axios < 1.16.1 sends non-CONNECT
  requests the proxy rejects). `curl` reaches OneMap fine, so the **parser** is validated against real
  payloads and the route body by inspection — but the **axios call, Redis cache path and rate limiter
  are unexercised**. A sandbox artefact, not a production one; Railway has no such proxy. The axios
  pin was deliberately **not** bumped — that's an unrelated change to a shared HTTP client used
  throughout the server.
- `titleCase` mangles brand initialisms it doesn't know — the live fixture yields "Spc Toa Payoh
  Lorong 6" (O-113). Enumerating every brand is unbounded.
- Device confirmation outstanding (O-93, O-111), now covering the address rows too.

## Docs

`journal-0_62_690-01_08_26-1500.md`, `register-0_62_690-01_08_26-1500.md` (C-115…C-118, D-55…D-58,
O-112/O-113 opened, **O-110 closed**), AU-7 amendment to D-61.63, `.serial-state.yml` re-anchored to
01-08 '26 15:00 SGT (sovereign `data.gov.sg` source, TF-6/TF-9).

`public/doc/vibe-journal.html`, `public/doc/vibe-journal.json`.

The 14 PRs span Material-alignment Phase 2a/2b (token bridge), the M3 audit Tier 0/1, Michelin footer
pagination + the year/Bib filters, the typography + screen-size audit, O-95/96/97, O-89/91/92, the
carousel card spec (D-51) with the Hawker/Train audit, the footer grid-placement bug,
`.liquid-glass-focus`, four-corner ring labels, the station-pick inspection overlay, and the OneMap
road/address search.

**The PR listing's `merged` boolean is wrong.** Every row came back `"merged": false` — including
#1666–#1671, which are *already in the ledger as merged*, and #1684/#1685, which this session merged
by hand minutes earlier. `merged_at` was populated and correct throughout, and is what the catch-up
keyed on.

Taking the boolean at face value would have appended fourteen rows marked unmerged and quietly skewed

fail. It was caught only because six of the affected rows had known ground truth to check against.

string** (a contiguous block, #1552–#1667). The generator tolerates it, so this is latent rather than
broken, but any consumer doing a strict `===` join on `n` silently misses those 116. Deliberately not
repaired here: rewriting historical rows in an append-only data file is a bulk edit that would need a
G2 gate and buys no behaviour. New rows are written as integers.

title: v0.62.691 — carousel card line spacing (13rem → 12rem) + restore Cuisine's missing ⇱/⇲ map button
body:
Two operator reports from one device screenshot, plus the spec audit that was asked for first.

## 1. Line spacing — and why it was loose

Six collapsed rows — type/★/$, meta, 💵 price, 🍱 set-meal, Michelin, and the toggle — carried **no
`leading-*` class at all**, so they inherited Tailwind preflight's `html { line-height: 1.5 }`. The
rows someone had explicitly styled ran at 1.25 or 1.375. Three line-heights on one card, decided by
which rows happened to receive a class.

- **`leading-snug` on the horizontal card ROOT** — one class fixes all six; explicit per-row values
  still win on specificity (D-59). Fixing them individually would leave the same trap for row seven.
- **1.375, not 1.25** — tight buys ~6px more but risks clipping full-height CJK glyphs across the 8
  shipped locales (D-60).
- **Removed the `mt-*` doubling the parent's `gap-0.5`** — all gated on `horizontal`; the vertical
  list is byte-identical.
- **`h-[13rem]` → `h-[12rem]`** (−16px, −7.7%).

| Case | Content before | Content after | Box | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Typical card (the screenshot) | 178px | **165px** | 208 → **192** | slack 30 → 27 |
| Worst realistic (Michelin + 3 wrapped rows) | 252px | **233px** | 208 → **192** | over 44 → **41** |

**12rem is not taste** — it's the largest cut leaving every case no worse than before. At 11.5rem the
worst case overruns by 49px against today's 44px, i.e. the "improvement" makes the bad case worse
(D-61).

## 2. The missing ⇱/⇲ — the glyphs were never the bug

Operator: *"did you know the ⇱ (U+21F1) and ⇲ (U+21F2) is missing in Cuisine TMA. it is to expand the
embedded map like Train TMA and Hawker TMA"*. Both glyphs were in the source all along — the **button
was gated out**. `v0.62.190` hid it whenever `fill` was true and `onCollapse` absent, reasoning it
"would be a no-op button" there. That is the phone case.

It is also **exactly the state Transport was bug-reported for in v0.62.626 and Hawker in v0.62.627**.
Both were fixed by giving the button a real action, not by hiding it. Third report, one pattern.

Hawker's fix is **ported verbatim rather than re-derived**:

- `overlayFull` + `canOverlay = fill && !onCollapse` — precisely the hidden case. Gate deleted, so the
  button always renders; the formerly-dead case promotes the map to a full-viewport overlay.
- **`z-[35]`, not `z-30`** — the result carousel is `fixed … z-30` and paints *later* in the DOM, so an
  equal-z overlay sits *behind* the cards. That was Hawker's Codex-P2 catch. 35 clears the carousel and
  stays under the footer dock (z-40) so the Map toggle remains reachable.
- **A `resize` trigger on `[overlayFull, expanded]`** — promoting the wrapper to `fixed inset-0`
  changes the container out from under the Maps SDK, which otherwise paints at the stale size. Cuisine
  had *no* resize trigger at all before this.

Both of those were learned from bugs found *after* Hawker's first attempt. Copying the whole fix
rather than re-deriving it is what carried them forward.

## Operator rulings recorded

Two items from the audit were closed by instruction, not by build. Both moved to a new Register
**Accepted** section so a later session doesn't read either as an oversight:

- **Row-move — dropped.** *"dont move if you already trim off the spacing"*. The collapsed card keeps
  all ten rows.
- **Short tier — accepted as-is.** *"The short tier — phone landscape - dont change."* Its ~36px
  overrun (which can clip the ▸ toggle) is known, computed, and deliberately tolerated.

One item is now **genuinely open**: O-116, the `≈ A$…` conversion row orphaning on the short tier (the
💵 price row above it is gated `!isShort`, the conversion isn't). It had been parked behind the
row-move that is no longer happening.

## Test plan

- Cuisine build green; `npm test -- --run` **156 files / 3901 tests** green.
- Compiled CSS grepped with `grep -F` on the CSS-escaped literals: `.leading-snug`, `.h-\[12rem\]`,
  `.h-\[7\.5rem\]`, `.mt-0\.5`, `.mt-1{`, `.line-clamp-2`, `.z-\[35\]`, `.fixed`, `.inset-0` — all
  **EMITTED**.
- **Both ⇱ and ⇲ confirmed present in the built JS bundle.**
- Version string confirmed rebuilt into the bundle (`0.62.691`) — the footer renders it, so a bump
  without a rebuild would have shipped a stale label.
- Device: the collapsed card should be tighter and 16px shorter with the same rows; the vertical list
  unchanged; and the phone map should now show a fifth ⇲ button that opens a full-viewport map, with ⇱
  to return.

## Known gaps

**Every height number above is arithmetic from the class list, not measurement** (standing O-107 /
O-93). The short-tier overrun in particular is a prediction. The map overlay is verified by class and
bundle inspection only — Hawker's equivalent needed two follow-up fixes after its first device run,
which is precisely why its final form was copied wholesale here.

## Docs

`journal-0_62_691-01_08_26-1605.md`, `register-0_62_691-01_08_26-1605.md` (C-120…C-123, D-59…D-61,
O-115/O-118 → Accepted, O-116 open, **O-117 closed**); `.serial-state.yml` re-anchored to
01-08 '26 16:05 SGT (sovereign `data.gov.sg` source, TF-6/TF-9).

title: URGENT v0.62.692 — fix Hawker white-screen · v0.62.693 — carousel card measures its height
body:
Two fixes. The first is the urgent one.

---

# v0.62.692 — Hawker TMA white-screened on every load

`web/hawker/src/App.jsx:502`:

```js
const renderCentreCard = (c, i, glass = false, compact = false) => {   // ← no isShort
```

The **body** reads `isShort` twice — the D-51 height tier at `:541` and the stalls/status gate at
`:550`, both added in **v0.62.686**. `CentreCarousel` passes it as the 5th argument (`:241`), but it
was never added to the signature. Inside the function `isShort` is an **undeclared identifier**, and
reading one is a `ReferenceError`, not `undefined`.

Every centre card threw, `Array.map` propagated it, React tore down the tree —
`#root.innerHTML.length === 0`. The shell renders first, so the app goes blank **the moment centre
data arrives**.

**Fix:** one parameter, defaulted `false` so the four-argument list call site is unchanged.

### Every gate stayed green (D-62)

| Gate | Result | Why it couldn't catch it |
|---|---|---|
| `vite build` | ✓ built | Transpiles JSX; no scope analysis |
| `node --check` | pass | Parses only — syntax was valid |
| `npm test` | 3901 pass | None render a component (O-93) |
| CI (4 checks) | green | Same three + blob guardrail |
| Compiled-CSS emission grep | `.h-[5.5rem]`, `.h-[8rem]` **EMITTED** | Tailwind scans **source text** — emitted by code that could never execute |

That last row is the sharpest: the check this project invented to catch silent failures confirmed both
classes in v0.62.686 — true and meaningless at once. The crash also needs **data** to appear; with the
API 404ing the app renders a healthy-looking shell, which nearly produced a false all-clear.

Found by loading the built bundle in headless Chromium with the centres API mocked. `no-undef` swept
across all four app trees afterwards — only `__BUILD_VERSION__` (a Vite `define`) remains. `isShort`
was the only real one.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `#root` innerHTML | **0 chars** | **10,469 chars** |
| cards render | no | yes |
| page errors | `ReferenceError: isShort is not defined` | none |

---

# v0.62.693 — "there is lots of white space below"

v0.62.691's spacing pass was correct and insufficient. My model assumed an 8-row card; the operator's
are sparser — *Dirty Supper* has no cuisine type, no price row and therefore no `≈` conversion row:
~5 rendered rows in a box sized for ten.

**That is not a tuning error.** D-51 wants every card identical AND no wasted space, and a *constant*
cannot do both — it must be sized for the tallest card the set can produce, so every sparser card pays
for rows it doesn't have. D-61 had already fixed 12rem as the **floor** (below it, tall cards clip).
No number was left.

**So measure it.** `ResultDrawer` reads every collapsed card's natural height in a `useLayoutEffect`
and pins them all to the tallest:

```js
el.style.height = 'auto';            // release the constraint …
max = Math.max(max, el.scrollHeight);
el.style.height = prev;              // … and restore before paint
```

`scrollHeight` alone isn't enough — once a height is applied the content stops overflowing, so it
would report the applied height and the strip could never shrink again. `ResultCard` gains
`collapsedHeightPx` (inline, beats the class) and a `data-card-root` hook; `h-[12rem]` stays as the
first-paint fallback (**D-63**).

### Measured in a browser, not by arithmetic

| Fixture set | Card | applied | natural | slack |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mixed | Dirty Supper (sparse) | 202 | 117 | 85 |
| mixed | Treasure Paradise (Michelin, wrapped) | 202 | 202 | **0** |
| **all-sparse** (the reported case) | Dirty Supper | **117** | 117 | **0** |
| **all-sparse** | Dusk Restaurant | **117** | 117 | **0** |

**192px → 117px** in the reported case. In a mixed set the short card still matches the tall one —
that's D-51 working as specified.

### Found while measuring

**The carousel's loop clone had never been passed `isShort`.** On phone landscape every real card
rendered the short tier while the aria-hidden clone rendered the standard tier — a visible height jump
as the strip wrapped around. Surfaced only because the probe printed three cards and the third
disagreed with the other two.

---

## Test plan

- Hawker + Cuisine builds green; `npm test -- --run` **156 files / 3901 tests** green.
- Geometry and the crash both verified in headless Chromium. Probe entry and build output deleted —
  `git status` shows only source files changed.
- `public/` is gitignored and rebuilt by `postinstall`.
- Device: Hawker centre cards should appear again (carousel **and** two-panel list); Cuisine cards
  should sit tight to their content with no blank band under the ▸ toggle.

## Known gaps

- **v0.62.692's regression window is unestablished (O-119).** `isShort` entered that body in
  v0.62.686 (PR #1682), so Hawker has plausibly been crashing since then. Worth confirming against
  your own usage — if it worked yesterday, my window is wrong.
- v0.62.693 used **fixture** data modelled on the two screenshots; a live set may contain a card shape
  neither fixture covers.
- **The short tier is deliberately excluded** from the measurement — ruled *"dont change"* (O-115) —
  even though measuring would have fixed its known overrun.
- **O-121** (new): pre-existing nested `` in `ResultCard` (details toggle inside the card's
  button). Invalid HTML, surfaced by the probe, recorded rather than folded into a white-space fix.
- **O-122** (new): the measurement doesn't re-run for a late field that changes none of its
  dependencies.

## Docs

`journal-0_62_692` / `register-0_62_692` (C-124…C-126, D-62, O-119/O-120) and `journal-0_62_693` /
`register-0_62_693` (C-127…C-129, D-63, O-121/O-122); `.serial-state.yml` re-anchored to
01-08 '26 17:00 SGT.

title: v0.62.694 — Hawker: accent border on the centred card, measured card height
body:
Operator, on an iPhone 15 Pro Max screenshot at v0.62.693: *"where is the border for active card in
Hawker TMA. you see that the edge cards should be 70% glass-effect? also the card can be shorter, can
you shorten it down by 15% until the pill to 'details'"*.

All three were measured in a browser **before** anything was changed — and they needed three
different answers.

| | measured before | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **border** | all five cards identical grey `tg-border` | **real bug** |
| **height** | applied **128px**, natural content **90px** → 30 % slack | **real, but mis-estimated** (15 % asked) |
| **glass** | edge cards `rgba(…/0.6)` + `blur(12px) saturate(1.4)`; centred opaque | **not a defect** |

## 1. Border — a real bug, with a precise cause

`cardOn = activePill === \`${c.name}|card\`` (`:511`) is set only by an explicit card **tap**.
Scrolling updates `centeredIdx`, but that value never reached the card — so the card you scrolled to
wore the same grey border as the peeking ones. The question had a factual answer: there was no border
to find.

`CentreCarousel` now passes `centred = !isWide && i === centeredIdx`. A tap still adds the stronger
`ring-1 + shadow-xl + z-10`, so **"scrolled to" and "selected" stay visually distinct** (D-64) —
collapsing them would make a scroll look like a selection, which is the confusion v0.62.581 fixed in
Cuisine from the opposite direction.

Wide layouts are untouched: there is no single centred card when several are in focus at once.

## 2. Height — measured rather than nudged

15 % was asked for; the measurement found **30 %** available. Rather than swap one constant for
another, this ports v0.62.693's mechanism (D-63): read every collapsed card's natural height in a
`useLayoutEffect` and pin them all to the tallest. `height:auto` is applied momentarily during the
read, because once a height is set the content stops overflowing and `scrollHeight` would just echo it
back.

**128px → 90px, zero slack** — landing exactly on the ▸ details pill, which is what *"until the pill
to details"* asks for. `h-[8rem]`/`h-[5.5rem]` remain the first-paint fallback.

This **closes the structural half of O-109**: Cuisine and Hawker now share the mechanism, so their
card heights can no longer drift apart through constant-tuning.

## 3. Glass — working, and the "70 %" is genuinely ambiguous

The edge cards **are** glass and always were — `background: rgba(…/0.6)` with
`backdrop-filter: blur(12px) saturate(1.4)`, verified per card; the centred card is deliberately
opaque with no backdrop filter. That is the same 60 % Cuisine uses, so the two apps already match.

**"70 %" points in two opposite directions**: *more glass* (fill 60 % → 30 % opaque, more map showing
through) or *more opaque* (fill 60 % → 70 %). Left at 60 % and returned as a question rather than
guessing a visible design value — it's a one-token change once the direction is known (**O-123**).

## Verified after

| card | height | natural | border |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (centred) | **90** | 90 | **`rgb(43,194,106)`** — accent |
| 1–4 (peeking) | **90** | 90 | grey `tg-border` |

Zero slack on every card, uniform across the strip, accent on exactly one.

## Test plan

- Hawker build green; `npm test -- --run` **156 files / 3901 tests** green.
- Geometry and computed styles read from the running app before and after; probe deleted afterwards
  (`git status` shows only `package.json` + `web/hawker/src/App.jsx`).
- Device: the centred card should carry a green border, the peeking ones grey; every card should end
  just under the ▸ details pill.

## Known gaps

- The probe runs in the **dark** palette while the screenshot is light. The mechanism is
  palette-independent (alpha + `backdrop-filter` are the same rule either way), but how 60 % glass
  *looks* over a light map is not something this harness judged.
- Fixture centres, not the live NEA dataset.
- `centred` is phone-only by construction — an active border on wide layouts needs a different rule,
  since several cards are "in focus" there simultaneously.
- The measurement re-runs on `[items, isShort, basisClass]`; same late-field caveat as O-122.

## Docs

`journal-0_62_694-01_08_26-1815.md`, `register-0_62_694-01_08_26-1815.md` (C-130…C-132, D-64, O-123
opened, O-109 structurally closed); `.serial-state.yml` re-anchored to 01-08 '26 18:15 SGT.

title: v0.62.696–697 — Michelin ticks (popup, nudge, data-driven 2026) · Australia city list by state, foldable
body:
Two rounds, both from device reports.

---

# v0.62.696 — Michelin ticks

*"(1) … it should pop-up same window … Remove current showing … on the same screen. (2) By the way,
none of the '2026', '2025', 'Bib Gourmand' works. check your wiring."*

## The wiring was sound — established by testing it

**Chips → callback**, driven in a browser:

```
click 2026 mf={"year2026":false,"year2025":true,"bib":true}
click 2025 mf={"year2026":false,"year2025":false,"bib":true}
click Bib  mf={"year2026":false,"year2025":false,"bib":false}
```

**Server filter → pool**, `michYearMatches` against real data for **all 11 countries**:

| | SG | MY | TH | JP | KR | TW | VN | HK | MO | PH | CN |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all on | 140 | 69 | 180 | 587 | 117 | 219 | 83 | 147 | 34 | 34 | 475 |
| 2026 only | **0** | 9 | 43 | 359 | 46 | 61 | 11 | 77 | 21 | 9 | 129 |
| 2025 only | 41 | 7 | 33 | 70 | 9 | 52 | 9 | 18 | 8 | **0** | 20 |
| Bib only | 99 | 60 | 137 | 228 | 71 | 156 | 72 | 70 | 13 | 25 | 326 |

Every combination narrows correctly; the default returns the full pool everywhere. Stars have not
stopped appearing — all 140 SG entries carry `awardYears`.

## It was still broken — two causes, both *outside* the wiring

1. **Ticking never triggered anything.** The handler only called `setState`; nothing prompted a
   re-search. Now raises the same search hint a category-drawer close raises (your chosen convention).
2. **In Singapore 2026 could never matter** — 0 SG stars carry `'26` (2026 selection unannounced,
   ceremony 4 Aug). Toggling it there is a guaranteed no-op even after searching.

New `michelinYearsByCC` on `/api/cuisine/catalogue` drives availability from the data; an unavailable
year is **greyed + struck through with a caption saying why** rather than hidden (**D-65**). Fails
open on a null list.

Plus the popup: new `MichelinFilterDrawer.jsx`, same modal shape as `CuisineCategoryDrawer`; the
inline row is removed.

**Verified** across three data shapes — fail-open, Singapore (`'25` only → 2026 disabled), Japan-like
(both years). Inline ticks gone in all three; no page errors.

---

# v0.62.697 — Australia by state

*"expand the 'Others' for Australia with its 6 states, each state having up-to-5 cities … lite-thin
hollow line separation by state and the state now in 2 font size smaller in the middle of the hollow
line (1 character spacing before and after)"*, then *"make each state separation with ▸ for collapsed
and ▾ for expanded"*.

**9 → 33 cities**, each carrying a `state` field; mirrored into `web/menu/src/cities.js`.

| group | cities |
|---|---|
| ACT | Canberra |
| NSW | Sydney, Newcastle, Wollongong, Coffs Harbour, Ballina |
| VIC | Melbourne, Geelong, Bendigo, Mildura, Warrnambool |
| QLD | Brisbane, Gold Coast, Sunshine Coast, Cairns, Townsville |
| SA | Adelaide, Mount Gambier, Port Lincoln, Whyalla, Kingscote |
| WA | Perth, Broome, Kalgoorlie, Geraldton, Karratha |
| TAS | Hobart, Launceston, Devonport, Burnie |
| NT | Darwin, Alice Springs, Uluru |

**On "6 states" (D-67):** Australia has exactly six — and **Canberra is in none of them**. It's the
Australian Capital Territory; Darwin and Alice Springs are Northern Territory. Canberra was already
first in your list and is the national capital, so dropping it would regress the picker and filing it
under NSW would be wrong. ACT and NT are their own groups, labelled honestly.

**The divider is the control (D-66).** One row carries the hairline, the label at `text-[11px]`
against the rows' `text-[13px]` — two steps smaller — with a literal ` ` either side (one
*character*, not padding that resembles one), and **▸ / ▾**. Default every group **expanded**, so
nothing regresses; the group holding the current pick is force-open. Countries without `state` render
exactly as before.

**A bug the fold would have introduced:** `itemRefs` is positional, so a collapsed group leaves null
holes and `itemRefs.current[next]?.focus()` would have swallowed the miss and stranded arrow-key focus
mid-list. Now walks to the next ref that exists.

**Verified:** 8 group headers, all `aria-expanded=true`, 33 cities in order; collapsing QLD flips that
header alone to `▸ QLD` and removes its 5 cities (42 → 37 rows). No page errors.

attempt** (`"Wollongong" has code "WOL" which is NOT in iata-cities.js`). Good guard.

canonical table turns it green whether or not they're correct. These 15 rest on my knowledge alone

title: v0.62.698 — O-104 reproduced & fixed at the reported field; zone re-tap re-frames the zone
body:
Two device reports.

---

## 1. "it should not zoom in and make the whole TMA looks zoom in"

**This is O-104** — the oldest undecided item in the Register, open since v0.62.678 as *"the iOS
auto-zoom guard is inert in 4 TMAs"*, deliberately unfixed because *"every fix conflicts with the 14px
parity"*. It now has a device symptom, which settles it.

**The guard was never missing.** Every app's `styles.css` has it, and says so:

```css
/* … iOS auto-zooms a focused input whose font-size is below 16px …
   Force >=16px on all text inputs. */
input, textarea, select { font-size: 16px; }
```

A bare element selector is specificity **(0,0,1)**. The input carries Tailwind's `text-xs` — a class at
**(0,1,0)**. **The class wins**, the input renders at 12px, iOS zooms the page on focus. No
element-selector tinkering can ever fix that: a class outranks any number of element selectors.

**Fixed where it reaches the element** — `text-xs` → `text-[16px]` in the **shared**
`StationLocationField.jsx`, so Hawker *and* Train are both covered.

**Not** `!important` on the guard (**D-68**): that would force every input in the app to exactly 16px,
shrinking any that legitimately want to be larger — an app-wide restyle inside a one-field report.
And not `maximum-scale=1`, which suppresses the zoom by disabling pinch-zoom entirely (accessibility
regression, and Telegram's WebView may override it anyway). 16px is the platform threshold; meeting it
*is* the fix.

Verified by reading the input's **computed** `font-size` from the running app — **16px** on both phone
and desktop viewports. Reading the class list is exactly what hid this for six versions.

---

## 2. "when I click the zone again, it should zoom out to 12 in iPhone and 13 in Desktop/iPad"

All three zone-pill call sites ran `onClick={() => setActiveRegion(r.region)}`. Re-tapping the
**active** pill passed the value it already held, React bailed out of the re-render, and nothing moved.
The tap wasn't ignored by design — it had no effect at all.

New `pickRegion()`: a *different* zone switches as before; the *same* zone calls
`window.__giaHawkerFitZone(12 | 13)`. The global pans to the active zone's bounds centre and sets the
zoom **explicitly** — not `fitBounds`, which would pick its own zoom from the bounds and ignore the two
numbers that were the entire request (**D-69**).

Verified with the map global stubbed to record its argument:

| viewport | re-tap active zone | switch to another zone |
|---|---|---|
| 390×844 (iPhone) | `fitZone(12)` ✅ | no call, pill moves ✅ |
| 1280×900 (Desktop/iPad) | `fitZone(13)` ✅ | no call, pill moves ✅ |

So a switch never force-zooms; only a re-tap does.

---

## O-119 closed

Operator: *"Hawker actual works"* — it was functional before today, which supports the v0.62.692
window: `isShort` entered `renderCentreCard`'s body in v0.62.686, merged this morning in PR #1682.

## Test plan

- Hawker + Transport builds green; `npm test -- --run` **156 files / 3901 tests** green.
- Both fixes verified against the running app, not by inspection.
- Device: tapping "Search a station or road" should no longer zoom the page; re-tapping the already-
  selected zone pill should re-frame that zone.

## Known gaps

- **O-128 (new):** the zone re-tap's *actual camera movement* is unverified — Google Maps never loads
  in this sandbox (no `/maps-key`), so `__giaHawkerFitZone` early-returns on a null `mapRef`. The
  wiring is proven; the framing is not. Device check only.
- **O-104 is narrowed, not closed.** The reported field is fixed and the root cause is now proven
  rather than theorised, but the guard stays inert for **every other** sub-16px input across the TMAs.
  Closing it needs a decision — audit each input, or `!important` and accept the restyle — not a task.
- 16px is visibly larger than the 12px it replaces in that field. That's the "14px parity" cost O-104
  flagged, accepted here because the alternative is the page zooming.

title: v0.62.699 — expanded Cuisine map no longer hides the card strip and footer
body:
Operator: *"when I tap ⇲ to expand the map in Cuisine TMA, why the footer is gone and the card … the
card and footer are important despite the google map being expand"*, then *"make sure the drawer works
even when map is expanded"*.

## This is my bug, from v0.62.691

Giving Cuisine's ⇲ a real action ported Hawker's v0.62.627 overlay — and I copied the value **together
with its justification**:

> *"z-[35] … clears the carousel while staying under the footer dock (z-40), so the footer and its Map
> toggle stay reachable."*

True in Hawker. **False in Cuisine.** The two apps do not share a stack:

| | Hawker | Cuisine |
|---|---|---|
| result carousel | `z-30` | `z-30` |
| **footer dock** | **`z-40`** | **`z-30`** (`App.jsx:5582`) |

At `z-[35]` the overlay cleared the carousel *and* the footer, so both disappeared behind the expanded
map. The number was ported without re-checking the stack it landed in — and the comment I wrote
asserted something about Cuisine that had only ever been verified about Hawker (**D-70**).

## Fix

Cuisine's expanded overlay `z-[35]` → **`z-20`**. The map still fills the viewport but paints **below**
the carousel, footer and sticky header (all `z-30`).

**Hawker is deliberately untouched** — its `z-[35]` is correct for its own stack, and re-checking that
was the first thing done rather than assumed a second time.

## The drawer stays usable — measured, not asserted

"Works when expanded" is decided by which element wins `elementFromPoint`, so that's what was tested,
using the **compiled** Cuisine stylesheet and the exact class strings from source:

| tap target | `z-20` (fix) | `z-[35]` (shipped) |
|---|---|---|
| a carousel card | **card** ✅ | overlay ❌ |
| the footer | **footer** ✅ | overlay ❌ |
| above the strip | **map**, still pannable ✅ | overlay |

The drawer's wrapper is `pointer-events-none` with the inner scroll track `pointer-events-auto`, so
cards take taps and the map takes everything outside the strip.

**One honest footnote:** a fourth probe — tapping the strip's band *past* the last card — returns the
**track**, not the map, because the scroll track is `pointer-events-auto` across its full width (it has
to be, to capture horizontal swipes). So the carousel owns its whole band, not just the card
rectangles. Pre-existing and correct; recorded because the reading looks like a miss and isn't one.

## Test plan

- Cuisine build green; `npm test -- --run` **156 files / 3901 tests** green.
- `.z-20` and `.z-30` both confirmed emitted in the compiled bundle.
- Device: tap ⇲ — the map should fill the screen with the card strip and footer still on top and
  usable; ⇱ returns.

## Known gaps

- The probe reconstructs the stack from real classes and real CSS but is **not the live app** —
  Cuisine's drawer needs a completed search to render, which this sandbox can't do. An element sitting
  between z-20 and z-30 in the real tree wouldn't have been caught.
- **O-129 (new):** the expanded map now also sits below the **sticky header**. That falls out of going
  beneath the whole z-30 tier rather than being a decision about the header; you asked only about the
  card and footer. Covering the header while keeping those two needs the header to have its own z — a
  bigger change to the stack.
- **O-130 (new):** the z-stack is **undocumented and app-specific**. Cuisine and Hawker disagree on the
  footer's layer with nothing recording that they differ, which is exactly how this port went wrong. A
  short per-TMA tier table (header / map / carousel / footer / dialogs) would make the next port
  checkable instead of assumed.

## Docs

`journal-0_62_699-01_08_26-2045.md`, `register-0_62_699-01_08_26-2045.md` (C-144/C-145, D-70,
O-129/O-130 opened); `.serial-state.yml` re-anchored to 01-08 '26 20:45 SGT.

title: v0.62.700 — O-124: the Michelin edition ticks become data-driven
body:
_(№ 1,204 - 02-08 '26 15:00 SGT)_

> Operator: *"O-124 - yes, make it data-driven"*

## What O-124 actually was

Not a defect — a **latent** one. v0.62.676 shipped the Michelin edition filter as a hardcoded 2026/2025 pair. That is correct for today's data and silently wrong the day a `'27` edition lands: a venue awarded only in `'27` matches neither arm and vanishes from results, with a green suite, a normal-looking UI and nothing in the logs. The ticks would still toggle — they would just be filtering against a year universe that no longer described the data.

## Six sites, not one

| # | Site | What it hardcoded |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `index.js` (search handler) | `years.includes("'26") \|\| years.includes("'25")` |
| 2 | `index.js` (walk hash) | a fixed 3-bit string `"110"` — cannot describe a third edition |
| 3 | `MichelinFilterDrawer.jsx` | `KEYS = [2026, 2025, bib]` |
| 4 | `state.js` (default) | `{ year2026: true, year2025: true, bib: true }` |
| 5 | `state.js` (hash) | one param per year — `michY26` / `michY25` |
| 6 | **`michelin-sort.js`** | `YEAR_RANK = { "'26": 2, "'25": 1 }` |

**Site 6 was found during the work, not before it**, and it is the worst of the six: a `'27` entry scores 0 there and sorts **below** `'25` — newest-last, with no visible cause. O-124 named "the ticks"; the sort was carrying the same constant one file away.

## The rule that replaces them

One convention, both halves: **only OFF is ever transmitted.** A year nobody has mentioned is ON. That inversion is what makes it data-driven — "everything not switched off" already contains editions that do not exist yet, so a new one needs no new key, no server change and no client deploy.

## Changes

- **`michelin-year-filter.js`** (NEW, root, CJS) — `yearsOffFromFilter()`, `yearUniverse()`, `makeMichelinYearMatcher()`. Extracted out of a ~400-line route so the rule is testable; it could previously only be checked by reading it.
- **`web/cuisine/src/v2/lib/michelin-years.js`** (NEW) — the client half (`yearOfToken`, `buildMichelinKeys`, `tickTokens`, `unionYears`), lifted out of the component for the same reason: with no React render harness (O-93), logic inside a component is verified by eye.
- **`index.js`** — handler uses the matcher; `michSelectedYears` derives from the country's own editions minus what the client switched off; walk hash `110` → `'26,'25|1`.
- **`michelin-sort.js`** — `yearRank(token)` returns **the year itself**. Newest-first is a property of the number, not of a lookup table. `YEAR_RANK` stays exported, now computed.
- **`MichelinFilterDrawer.jsx` / `CuisineDrawer.jsx` / `App.jsx`** — tick list built from data, via a new `allYears` prop.
- **`state.js`** — default `michelinFilter` is `{}`; hash years travel as one `michYoff=2026,2025` list. Links shared while v0.62.676–699 were live are still **read**, so an old link keeps meaning what it meant.

### Why two year lists and not one

The obvious build — drive the ticks from the country's own editions — would have **deleted a feature**. Singapore's 2026 star list is unannounced, so its per-country list is `["'25"]`; a list built from that alone makes the 2026 tick silently disappear. v0.62.696 (D-65) deliberately *shows* it, greyed, with a reason. So **which ticks exist** comes from the cross-country union and **which are live** from the per-country list. Two questions, two inputs.

## Verification

- **Old vs new over the real datasets.** The pre-v0.62.700 predicate was transcribed verbatim from `index.js@c982ba6` and run beside the new matcher across **12 countries / 2,114 venues × all 8 tick combinations = 96 comparisons**. **94 identical.**
- **50 new tests** — `michelin-year-filter.test.js` (17), `cuisine-michelin-hash.test.js` (13, incl. legacy-link reads), `cuisine-michelin-years.test.js` (15), +5 appended to `michelin-sort.test.js` for `'27` ordering.
- Full suite **159 files / 3,951 tests** green (was 156/3,901). Cuisine build green.
- Tick classes re-checked as **emitted** in the compiled stylesheet (D-22…D-28 Tailwind silent-drop check), run because the class list's *shape* changed even though no class string did.

## The two differences — a live zero-results path this comparison uncovered

Both are the same shape, and both are in the only two **single-edition** countries:

| | star editions | reachable state | on main today | with this change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SG** | `'25` only | untick 2025 + Bib (2026 is greyed) | **0 results** | 140 (fail-open) |
| **PH** | `'26` only | untick 2026 + Bib | **0 results** | 34 (fail-open) |

The fail-open guard's own comment says it exists so a tick combination *"fails OPEN rather than silently returning zero"*. The hardcoded version measured "all ticks off" against the **literal pair**, so with 2026 nominally ON — even though it can match nothing in SG — it judged "not all off" and returned nothing.

**This is a behaviour change, in Singapore, reachable by tapping two ticks.** It ships because it is what the guard was written to do, but it is filed as **O-131** rather than declared correct: fail-open makes the last untick *appear to do nothing*, which is the exact complaint D-69 was written about. Returning empty with a "no results for this filter" message is defensible and is the operator's call.

## Test on device

In Cuisine → *Cuisine & Filters* → **Michelin · Bib Gourmand**, the popup should look **exactly as before** — 2026, 2025, Bib Gourmand, with 2026 greyed and explained in Singapore. Nothing here is meant to be visible today; that is the point. The proof it worked is that a `'27` edition would need **no code change** to appear.

## Known gaps

- **Never seen with a real third edition**, because none exists — the `'27` behaviour rests on tests and the 96-combination comparison, not on data (**O-132**).
- The popup is **unverified on a device** at this version; wiring is unchanged from v0.62.696 but the tick list is now computed (**O-133**).
- O-131 above is a shipped behaviour change awaiting a ruling.
- `michelinYearsByCC` is still recomputed per catalogue request (**O-125**, untouched).

## Docs

`doc/Journal/journal-0_62_700-02_08_26-1500.md` (№ 1,039) and `doc/Register/register-0_62_700-02_08_26-1500.md` (№ 175) — C-146…C-150, D-71…D-73, O-131…O-133, **O-124 closed**. `doc/.serial-state.yml` counters bumped and re-anchored to 02-08 '26 15:00 SGT from a live `data.gov.sg` fetch (TF-6/TF-9).

## Confirmation gates

| Gate | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | ✅ | PATCH bump 0.62.699 → 0.62.700; build green, 159/3,951 tests green, old-vs-new compared across 96 combinations |
| G2 | ➖ | no deletions — `YEAR_RANK` still exported (computed), legacy hash params still read, D-65's greyed-year behaviour preserved by design |
| G3 | ✅ | **D-71** a constant that describes the data belongs to the data · **D-72** a fail-open guard must be measured against what is actually reachable · **D-73** two questions need two inputs |
| G4 | ➖ | no external paid API call (TF-6 anchor is the free `data.gov.sg` sovereign source) |

title: v0.62.701–703 — settle O-131/SG-JB/O-104, then O-130 (z-stack registry), then O-120+O-93 (render smoke in CI)
body:
_(№ 1,208 - 03-08 '26 09:45 SGT)_

Three versions on one branch.

| version | driven by | closes |
|---|---|---|
| **v0.62.701** | *"Settle: O-131 / SG/JB: 2. Johor Bahru as a Malaysia City / O-104"* | O-131, SG/JB, **O-104** |
| **v0.62.702** | *"do next work"* | **O-130** |
| **v0.62.703** | *"do next work"* | **O-120**, **O-93**, **O-140** |

---

# v0.62.703 — O-120 + O-93: the render harness stops being thrown away

A render harness has been hand-built and deleted **nine times** this session. This is the tenth, and it is committed and wired into CI.

`scripts/render-smoke.mjs` boots all six built TMAs in headless Chromium, stubs the Telegram bridge, serves the app from disk and the API from fixtures, waits for the render to **settle**, and asserts the app painted.

**No static server.** Each app builds with base `/app//` but ships to `public//`, so the paths don't line up on disk. Every request is intercepted and fulfilled instead — one handler dispatching internally, which also sidesteps Playwright's last-handler-wins route precedence that produced a false all-clear earlier in this session.

## Does it catch what it exists for?

The v0.62.692 crash was reintroduced verbatim — `isShort` dropped from `renderCentreCard`'s signature while still used in its body:

| check | with the bug present |
|---|---|
| `vite build` | **green** |
| `npx vitest run` (161 files / 3,964 tests) | **green** |
| **`npm run test:render`** | **❌ hawker — `isShort is not defined`** |

That's the whole case for the file, in three lines. Restored, rebuilt, green again.

## Two false greens it produced on itself

Both found before committing:

1. **It failed two apps for requests it was itself refusing to answer.** Same-origin non-asset paths (`/maps-key`, unmatched `/api/…`) fell through to the disk lookup and 404'd, surfacing as console errors. Now only `/app//…` is served from disk; everything else same-origin gets a JSON stub.
2. **Worse — it was smoke-testing the lockout screen.** The stub left `initData` empty, and every app boots through a `hasInitData()` guard that renders *"reopen from Telegram"* when it's blank. Cuisine painted **4** nodes, Clipboard **5**, and the run reported six passes. On that path the component that crashed in v0.62.692 **never mounts**, so the harness would have sat in CI looking like protection while being green through the exact bug it was written for.

Fixed with a non-empty `initData`, plus **settle-then-count** and **per-app node floors** (cuisine 40 / hawker 32 / transport 45 / menu 30 / oversight 18 / clipboard 32 against observed 95 / 76 / 106 / 71 / 40 / 77), so *"something painted"* now means *"the app painted"*.

## It works on the runner — O-140 closed

This was the one part that couldn't be verified from the sandbox. **This PR's own build job settled it:**

```
> soleat@0.62.703 test:render
  ✅ cuisine 99 · hawker 76 · transport 106 · menu 71 · oversight 40 · clipboard 77
All 6 apps rendered.
```

`channel: 'chrome'` resolved on `ubuntu-latest`, six apps in **6.4 s**, and the build job's total went **75 s → 72 s** — the step costs nothing measurable. Cuisine reads **99** on the runner against 95 locally, which is exactly why the floors sit well below observed (O-142).

## One correction to O-120 as filed

The item said it *"needs no new dependency beyond what this repo already has available headlessly"*. **That was wrong, and it was mine** — Playwright is supplied by the sandbox *environment*, not by this repo, so CI would have had nothing to drive.

- **`playwright-core`** added as a devDependency — chosen over `playwright` because core downloads no browsers; it drives the Chrome `ubuntu-latest` already ships.
- **`package-lock.json` regenerated.** Not optional: `ci.yml` uses `npm install`, but four other workflows use `npm ci`, which fails outright on a package.json/lock mismatch.

Also included, **unrelated to O-120**: `web/clipboard/package-lock.json`, which had never been committed while its six siblings all are. The build generated it; tracking it matches the other TMAs.

---

# v0.62.702 — O-130: the z-stack registry, and the bug writing it down exposed

Filed as documentation. **It produced a user-facing fix.**

| role | cuisine | hawker | transport | clipboard |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **footer dock** | **`z-30`** | **`z-40`** | **`z-40`** | **`z-20`** |
| expanded map | **`z-20`** | **`z-[35]`** | **`z-[35]`** | — |

Cuisine had two dialogs at `z-30` — the **same tier as its own footer dock**, which renders later in the DOM (5591 > 4592). At equal z, document order decides: the footer painted over dialogs declaring `aria-modal="true"` and stayed tappable. `CuisineCategoryDrawer` was worse — its root is `fixed` *with* a z-index, so its nested dish pop-up (`z-40`) and dish detail (`z-50`) were clamped to `z-30` too. Three layers, one root.

Measured by hit-test against the compiled stylesheet: at `z-30` a tap on the footer band returns the footer chips; at `z-40` it returns the dialog scrim. Both roots raised to `z-40`, re-derived against Cuisine's own neighbours (D-70).

**Two silent scanning failures, both mine:** the enumeration regex ended `\|auto)\b` — a `\b` after `]` can never match, so every arbitrary `z-[NN]` was dropped and the first table omitted 17 sites. Then the new guard **passed a mutation it should have caught**, because it stripped comments *after* extracting the opening tag and the comment explaining this fix contains `(5591 > 4592)`.

Added: `doc/Technical/technical-0_62_702` (№ 70) and `__tests__/z-stack-registry.test.js`.

---

# v0.62.701 — O-131, SG/JB, O-104

**O-131** — neither filed option. Re-reading showed the item was wrong about its own scope: unticking everything returned everything in **all twelve countries**, not just SG/PH. So the state is made **unreachable** — `soleCheckedKey()` locks the last checked tick, counting **live** ticks only (in SG, unticking 2025 locks Bib, not the greyed 2026). The server's fail-open guard is untouched and is now genuinely a backstop.

**SG/JB** — Johor Bahru added to `MY` in both cities files, above the untouched *Johor state* row. A device in JB via the OTHER path previously landed on the state centroid ~50 km north. `JHB` already existed in the vetted IATA table.

**O-104** — audit over `!important` (D-68 stands). 11 sub-16px text-entry inputs swept to `text-[16px]`. The closure is `__tests__/ios-input-zoom-guard.test.js`, which **caught a hole in my own sweep** (`web/_shared/` isn't under `web/*/src`), then failed on the comment *explaining O-104*.

---

## Verification

- All six TMAs build **and paint**, locally and on the runner; full suite **161 files / 3,964 tests** green.
- Every new guard **mutation-checked** — made to fail on purpose before its silence was trusted.
- Compiled-stylesheet emission confirmed for all new classes (D-22…D-28).

## Known gaps

- **O-141 — first screen only.** No search, no drawer, no map. A crash needing a completed search still ships silently.
- **O-142 / O-143** — node floors and fixtures are hand-maintained.
- **O-134** — 11 inputs are visibly larger; `text-[10px]` → 16px in Clipboard's `DrawerRow` is the biggest jump.
- **O-138** — `_shared/FooterNav.jsx` at `z-50` sits above Cuisine's dialog tier: same defect class as v0.62.702's fix, one tier up, needs its own decision.

## Test on device

- Cuisine → **Michelin · Bib Gourmand**, and a cuisine **category** drawer: the footer should now be behind the dim scrim and untappable.
- In the Michelin popup, untick to one — the survivor stays on, dims and explains. In SG, unticking 2025 locks **Bib**.
- **Other → Malaysia**: *Johor Bahru* above *Johor state*.
- Any search/filter text field in Cuisine, Menu or Clipboard — no page zoom.

## Docs

Journals № 1,040–1,042 · Registers № 176–178 · Technical № 70. **O-104, O-131, SG/JB, O-130, O-120, O-93 and O-140 all closed**; C-151…C-164, D-74…D-79, O-134…O-143 recorded.

## Confirmation gates

| Gate | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | ✅ | PATCH bumps 0.62.700 → 0.62.703; builds green, 161/3,964 green, every guard mutation-checked |
| G2 | ➖ | no deletions; one devDependency **added** (`playwright-core`) and named, since O-120 claimed none would be needed |
| G3 | ✅ | **D-74** make a bad state unreachable · **D-75** a sweep without a guard is a fix, not a closure · **D-76** writing the invariant down is how you find it violated · **D-77** a scan's own escape hatches are part of its logic · **D-78** a harness rebuilt nine times is infrastructure · **D-79** a probe must be pointed at the real screen and proved against a real bug |
| G4 | ➖ | no external paid API call (TF-6 anchors are the free `data.gov.sg` sovereign source) |

title: v0.62.704 — Sketchbook itinerary map: live Google map, M3 layer panel, per-drawer pins
body:
Gives a Sketchbook cabinet an itinerary map. Every filed card carrying coordinates becomes a numbered, drawer-coloured pin on a **live Google map**, inside a pull-out sheet with the same physics as the Cuisine / Hawker / Transport drawers. Alongside it, a printable, copyable stop list separated by drawer, and travel legs **between** drawers.

Spec written first and committed: `instr/GIA_Sketchbook_Itinerary_Map_AI_Prompt.md`.

## Google Maps on screen, SVG for print

The design mockup drew an SVG, because a mockup needs no API key. Shipping that would have made Clipboard the only TMA whose map cannot zoom or pan and has no basemap. Screen rendering now uses the same loader, the same `AdvancedMarkerElement` pins and the same map options as the other three.

The SVG survives for **print only**. A live map is a WebGL canvas of raster tiles: browsers print it blank or grey, and Google's terms restrict reuse of captured tiles. There was no print path anywhere in this repo before now. Both renderers draw from `lib/itinerary.js`, so the printed page cannot drift from the screen.

|  | screen | print / PDF |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| renderer | Google Maps JS | inline SVG |
| zoom / pan | yes | no — fixed fit |
| basemap | Google tiles | none; 1 km scale bar |
| offline | `nokey` placeholder | always works |

## One colour per drawer, not per day-part

Colouring pins by `segments.js`'s day-part would render `teaBreak`, `earlyDinner` and `dinner` identically — all three are `evening` — and "which drawer is this pin" is the only question the colour answers. The **family** is now the day-part; the **shade** is the drawer's ordinal within it.

## The layer panel is the day

> "checkbox's alignment and groupings lacking and not following realistic drawer's purpose. i am not looking for general purpose checkbox."

A drawer *is* a time slot, so the control is the day itself: drawers in clock order, nested under their day-part, each part with its own parent tick and a real **indeterminate** state — a half-ticked Evening must not read as "Evening is off". Empty parts are not rendered. Each part's span is computed from its members. `wholeDay` reads "Anytime", so it gets its own trailing section instead of pretending to be an evening.

Checkboxes are Material 3 to spec, not `accent-color`: 18×18 / 2dp radius / 2dp outline, a **drawn** checkmark, a 40dp state layer, and every box in its own 40px column so parents, children and map layers share vertical centrelines.

## Mappable stops only, counted out loud

Coordinates reach a card only via the structured `venue`. Copy-all pushes, blank cards and anything filed before v0.62.429 have none. Those stay in the list, greyed, and the count says so out loud. The 📍 badge counts only what can be pinned, and is absent entirely at zero.

## Z-index

`BottomSheet`'s hardcoded `z-30` becomes a prop **defaulting to `z-30`**, so Cuisine / Hawker / Transport are unchanged. Clipboard passes a tier below its `z-20` footer nav — the same relationship this component already has to Hawker's and Transport's `z-40` footers. Porting a z-index without re-deriving it against that app's own chrome is a mistake already documented in `cuisine/MapPanel.jsx`.

## Verification

- **23 new unit tests** on the pure geometry/grouping module — and **mutation-checked**, because they passed first try: colouring by day-part alone fails 2 of them, computing legs over hidden drawers fails 1, both green again on restore.
- Full suite **162 files / 3,987 tests** green.
- `npm run build` green; `npm run test:render` green — all six apps paint, clipboard 77 nodes.
- Compiled-CSS grep for every new class, including the 340px responsive grid.
- M3 geometry measured in headless Chromium **against the built stylesheet**: box 18×18, radius 2px, border 2px, checked fill `rgb(43,89,201)` with tick offset 0, indeterminate fill filled with bar at 0 and tick hidden at 18, 40×40 hit column, parent centreline 20px vs child 51px, rows 40/48.

## Known gaps

- Render smoke covers the **first screen only** (O-141) — the sheet needs interaction, so CI does not exercise it.
- Nothing here is verified on a device.
- The three existing panels still carry their own loader copies; the shared module ships with one consumer.
- **Found, not fixed:** `clip-store.js` truncates the venue with `JSON.stringify(...).slice(0, 6000)`, which cuts the *string*, not the object. A large venue is stored as invalid JSON and silently reads back as `undefined`, so a stop that *had* coordinates is counted as unmappable. The fix belongs in the store with its own test — filed rather than smuggled in here.

title: v0.62.705–706 — footer cabinet switch, then three device fixes on the itinerary map
body:
Two versions on one branch.

---

# v0.62.706 — the 0px drag handle, and the map's missing controls

> *"the drawer for the cabinet map doesnt have handle like the other TMA. and is block at half layout the map / where are the embedded quick buttons and navigation cluster buttons in the map"*

Three reports. The first two were **one build bug**.

## Reports 1 + 2 — a Tailwind content glob, provable from the compiled CSS

`web/clipboard/tailwind.config.js` was the **only** TMA without `'../_shared/**/*.{js,jsx}'` — and v0.62.704 had just made Clipboard a consumer of the shared `BottomSheet`. Tailwind never scanned that file, so every utility unique to it was absent from Clipboard's stylesheet:

| class | clipboard | hawker | what it does |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `h-1.5` | **0** | 1 | the drag pill's **height** |
| `touch-none` | **0** | 1 | `touch-action: none` on the drag band |
| `cursor-grab` | **0** | 1 | the grab affordance |
| `fixed`, `w-12`, `rounded-t-2xl` | 1 | 1 | coincidentally used elsewhere in `clipboard/src` |

So the grabber rendered **48px wide and 0px tall** — "doesnt have handle" — and the band never set `touch-action: none`, so the WebView claimed the drag as a page scroll — "block at half". Two symptoms, one line of config. The partial hits are why it looked *nearly* right.

## A guard — which found a second case, then turned out to be wrong about it

`__tests__/tailwind-shared-content-guard.test.js` walks each app's import graph into `_shared` and fails if a reached file carries `className` while that app's `content` omits `../_shared`.

Its first version asked only *"does the app mention `_shared`?"* and immediately failed **`oversight`** — which imports exactly one thing, `_shared/lib/safe-area.js`, a pure module with no markup. **The guard was wrong, not `oversight`**; adding a glob there would have protected nothing and left the rule permanently over-strict. Narrowed to "reaches a shared file containing class strings".

## Report 3 — two separate mistakes, both mine

1. **The map was a 240px box inside the sheet's scrolling content.** Every other TMA puts it full-bleed *behind* and floats the sheet over it — the only arrangement in which the sheet's snaps mean anything. Now `fixed inset-x-0 top-0 bottom-14` at `z-[14]`, under the sheet's `z-[15]`; `inset-0 z-[16]` when expanded.
2. **Neither control cluster existed.** Added both, matching the other three verbatim: the left nav cluster (zoom-readout/Reset · ＋ · ↹ · － · ⇲) and the shared `MapControls` row + ⋮ overflow.

One deliberate difference: **Reset returns to the itinerary's own fitted bounds**, not `SG_CENTROID`. Their map is "Singapore"; this one is "your day".

## Verification

Driven in the real built app (Playwright over `public/clipboard/`, plus a minimal `google.maps` stub so the panel's actual draw effect runs):

| measurement | before | after |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| handle band height | 0 | **44px** |
| drag pill | 48 × **0** | **51 × 6** |
| `touch-action` on the band | inherited | **`none`** |
| nav-cluster buttons | 0 | **5** |
| Layers control | 0 | **1** |
| console errors | — | none |

---

# v0.62.705 — footer tab 2: long-press to switch cabinet

> *"the second button in the footer which shows default cabinet should be switchable"*

Changing which cabinet the tab points at required Cabinets → open → ★: three screens from the button it controls. Long-press now opens a picker; choosing a cabinet **sets the default** (the same write ★ makes) and navigates there. Both the interaction and the semantics were asked before building, since "switchable" could have meant navigate-only — which would let the tab's label and its destination disagree.

A hold is touch-only, so the same picker also opens on **right-click** and on **ArrowUp** when the tab has focus.

Two things that would have bitten on a device, both tested and both mutation-checked:
- **A press that drifts is a scroll** — drift measured from the *origin*, not the previous move, or a slow 4px crawl never trips the tolerance.
- **The click after a hold is swallowed** — otherwise one hold opens the picker *and* navigates.

Probe: plain tap opens no sheet; a 750 ms hold does; picking issues exactly one `setDefaultCabinet`; the label goes `🇸🇬 Singapore Trip` → `🗼 Tokyo 2027`; hold-while-dragging opens nothing.

---

## Combined verification

- **165 files / 4,026 tests** green; six apps build and paint (clipboard 77 nodes).
- Compiled-CSS checked before and after for every affected class.
- Both features driven end-to-end in the built app.

## Known gaps

- **Neither version is verified on hardware.** The probes are real browsers driving real built output — a genuine step up from the render smoke — but the bug they fix was found on a device, and they stub `google.maps`.
- The new guard checks **configuration, not emitted output**; the opacity-modifier silent-drop of v0.62.648 would still pass it.
- `bottom-14` is a hardcoded footer clearance tied to nothing.
- 500 ms for the hold is inherited from Cuisine's map gesture, not measured.

title: v0.62.707 — card drag: a movement guard, and friction on the scroll
body:
> *"if I want to move the card by holding on it / can it hard-friction the scroll bar. currently is too smooth to move around"*

Two causes, and the first wasn't what was asked about.

## 1. `dnd.js` had no movement guard

`dragHandle` armed a 280 ms timer and nothing cancelled it — there was **no `onPointerMove` at all**. So an ordinary scroll that happened to start on a card *also* began a drag 280 ms in: the list sliding under the finger with a ghost attached. That's a plain bug, not a tuning question, and it's half of "too smooth to move around".

Fixed by reusing **`createLongPress`** — written three versions ago for the footer tab, already tested, already carrying the drift-cancels-the-press rule. 8 px tolerance here vs the footer's 10: a card sits inside a scrolling list, and a false drag costs more than a false scroll.

## 2. There was no scroll model

The list kept its ordinary touch scrolling for the whole drag, so the finger moved the card *and* the list at once.

**What "hard friction" was taken to mean** — not a slower constant speed. Free scrolling is taken away for the duration and replaced with scrolling you have to ask for:

- a **rest band** through the middle where nothing moves;
- **72 px edge zones** top and bottom;
- a **quadratic ramp** inside them — 25 % speed at the halfway point, full speed only at the very edge. A linear ramp would pull the instant you crossed the boundary, which is precisely the "smooth" being complained about.

Measured: **3 px** in 500 ms held just inside the boundary, **397 px** at the edge. ~130:1 between a nudge and a commitment.

**Why the lock can only be applied at drag start:** `touch-action` is read when the browser decides what a gesture *is*. The long press needs 280 ms of stillness, so at that moment the browser hasn't committed to a scroll and the lock still takes effect. Earlier would break ordinary scrolling; later is too late.

## The probe found a defect the unit tests could not

Driving a real drag reported **0 px scrolled in 500 ms** at the zone boundary, where the model says it should creep.

`scrollTop` quantises to whole pixels. A 0.1 px/frame delta assigned `before + 0.1`, landed back on `before`, and the fraction was discarded — every frame, forever. Anything under ~0.5 px/frame was dead, silently pushing the rest band ~14 px past its designed end and making the shipped feel disagree with the tested one.

Fixed with `createScrollDriver()`, which carries the remainder between frames and drops it at an end so a built-up carry can't burst on reversal. **No test of the pure function could have found this** — the function was right; the loss was where the model met the DOM.

## Verification

- **166 files / 4,050 tests** green; six apps build and paint.
- 24 new tests, **mutation-checked**: `RAMP_CURVE` 2→1 fails 2, an unclamped zone fails 1, both green on restore.
- Five drag behaviours driven in the real built app:

| check | result |
| :-- | :-- |
| scroll gesture starting on a card | **no ghost** (was: ghost after 280 ms regardless) |
| still hold | ghost appears; scroller `touch-action: none`, `overscroll-behavior: contain` |
| held mid-list, 500 ms | **0 px** |
| held at the bottom edge, 500 ms | **397 px** |
| held just inside the boundary, 500 ms | **3 px** (was **0** before the carry fix) |
| after drop | ghost gone, `touch-action` restored |
| console errors | none |

## Known gaps

- **Unproven on touch, which is the only place it matters.** The probe drives a synthetic **mouse**, and mouse pointers never trigger the native touch-scroll arbitration this entire design turns on. Whether the mid-gesture lock holds in Telegram's iOS WebView is exactly what hasn't been tested.
- 72 px / 14 px-per-frame / curve 2 are **chosen, not measured**.
- `scrollParent` returns `null` for a list that isn't overflowing, so behaviour changes as content grows.
- The horizontal catch-all strip is untouched; this model is vertical only.

title: v0.62.708 — fix O-144: clip-store.js venue JSON truncation
body:
## Summary

- `clip-store.js`'s `normaliseRecord()` capped a structured venue by slicing the **stringified** JSON at 6000 chars — a truncation that can land mid-token and write syntactically invalid JSON. `denormaliseRecord()`'s `JSON.parse` then failed silently, degrading to `undefined` with no trace (indistinguishable from "no venue was ever attached").
- Fixed by validating the full stringified length *before* deciding what to write: if it fits, write it whole; if not, drop venue entirely (same `''` path already taken when `record.venue` is absent) rather than persist a corrupt fragment. Cap raised 6000 → 10000 for headroom.
- The venue `JSON.parse` catch block now logs via `console.warn('[Clip-Store] ...failed:', ...)`, matching every other catch in this file (it was previously the one silent catch).
- Closes Register item O-144.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --check` on both changed files
- [x] `npx vitest run __tests__/clip-store.test.js` — 46/46 (42 pre-existing + 4 new venue-field tests: normal round-trip, oversized-degrades-cleanly, corrupt-on-read-warns-and-degrades, existing no-venue cases unaffected)
- [x] Full `npm test -- --run` — 166 files / 4,062 tests green
- [x] Both new code paths mutation-checked (cap-removal and warn-removal each independently fail a test, confirmed restored to green)
- [x] No `web/` files touched — every downstream reader already null-guards on `typeof card.venue === 'object'`, so no build gate applies

title: v0.62.710 — GEMINI_MODEL now overrides every Gemini call site
body:
## Summary

- `GEMINI_MODEL` was documented as a general override ("GEMINI_MODEL env var still overrides") but only fed one constant, `DEFAULT_MODEL`, which only one function (`generateGroundedHiddenGems`, the `/hidden` command) actually read.
- The other four Gemini call sites — `validateAuthenticity`, `classifySearchIntent`, `describeCookingMethod`, and `extractDishesFromReviews` — each had an independent hardcoded `model = 'gemini-flash-latest'` default, silently ignoring the env var. Confirmed via `cuisine-enrich.js:253`'s call to `extractDishesFromReviews`, which never passes a `model` override.
- Fixed by changing all four defaults to `DEFAULT_MODEL`, matching the pattern already used by `generateGroundedHiddenGems`. Each function's own fallback chain (`SEARCH_INTENT_MODEL_CHAIN` / `FALLBACK_CHAIN`) is left untouched — those are deliberate retry lists for when the *primary* model fails, not the primary choice itself.
- Surfaced while investigating a deploy log after a Google API credential change; some pasted external "advice" about a related timeout was checked against the actual code and found not to match (wrong constant name, an unreferenced model, a different SDK's call shape) — none of it was applied.

## Test plan
