title: v0.62.712 — location picker: region-grouping for Malaysia + China (O-127)
body:
## Summary

Third and final item of the operator's original "next build" message. Extends Australia's state-grouped disclosure-triangle city picker to a **Malaysia + China pilot**, with France data-prepped only.

- **Generalized mechanism**: `state` renamed to `region` throughout `cities.js` (both apps); new `REGION_LABEL_BY_COUNTRY`, `CN_POPULAR_PROVINCES`, `defaultCollapsedRegions()` manifests; the disclosure-triangle grouping logic extracted into one pure `computeGroupedRows()` function shared by Cuisine's `CityDropdown` and Menu's `CityDropdownMenu` — previously two independently-maintained implementations (Menu actually had **zero** grouping — flat list, naive wraparound keyboard nav).
- **Malaysia**: 16 flat rows → 16 region groups (13 states + 3 Federal Territories), 62 rows total, capital-first. Every new code reuses an already-vetted IATA code (confirmed via the pre-existing `iata-cities.test.js` "non-inventive" invariant, unchanged pass). "Johor state" keeps its exact position and 120 km whole-state radius — given no `region` field so it stays an always-visible row outside any group's fold.
- **China**: 16 rows → 31 region groups (22 provinces + 4 municipalities + **5** autonomous regions — the operator's original spec said "3", real China has 5; used the complete correct set on delegated authority), 78 rows total. 6-province "Popular" lead section (Beijing/Guangdong/Shanghai/Zhejiang/Jiangsu/Sichuan) expanded by default, the other 25 collapsed.
- **France**: `region` (French région) added to the existing 12 rows, data-prep only — the picker entry stays disabled, zero visible effect.

**Two real bugs caught before shipping**, not after:
1. `App.jsx`'s boot-anchor fallback reads `CITIES_BY_COUNTRY[cc][0]` as the country's national-capital default with no GPS. A plan-literal "Popular provinces in listed order" would have silently moved China's `[0]` from Beijing to Guangzhou — fixed by reordering the Popular manifest (Beijing first) rather than touching the `[0]`-dependent code.
2. The collapsed-region `Set` never reseeded on a `countryCode` prop change (the picker component isn't remounted on a country switch) — harmless while only AU carried a `region` field, but would have silently broken China's "non-Popular starts collapsed" seeding on the very next country switch. Fixed with a `useEffect` reseed.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --check` on all changed `.js`/`.jsx` files
- [x] `npx vitest run __tests__/location-grouping.test.js` — 21/21 new tests (dividers, folding, force-open on selection, zero-cost when unused, real-data invariants)
- [x] `npx vitest run __tests__/iata-cities.test.js` — 30/30 unchanged, confirming every new MY/CN code is a real, already-vetted IATA code
- [x] Full `npm test -- --run` — 167 files / 4,094 tests green
- [x] `npx vite build` for both `web/cuisine` and `web/menu` — clean
- [x] `npm run test:render` — all 6 apps painted
- [x] Simulated a fresh picker open in a Node REPL: MY opens 62 cities across 16 expanded groups; CN opens with only its 6 Popular provinces' cities visible, the other 25 folded behind their dividers
- [x] 3 mutations checked (disable folding / disable CN collapse seeding / remove force-open-on-selection) — each confirmed to fail its matching test, then restored to green

title: v0.62.713–716 — Cost audit: instrumentation, leak fix, spend circuit breaker, per-user caps
body:
## Summary

From the operator's concern: *"serious concern over the use of tokens, i would like to know like how many request… And firing model, per user and if there are leaks."*

An audit found `/cost`'s tracker was nearly blind, one confirmed spend leak, no spend cap of any kind, and no per-user cap on any bot command. **This PR carries all four phases of the approved remediation plan.**

### Phase A (v0.62.713) — instrument the blind tracker
**0 of ~10 Gemini call sites** and **~2 of ~25 Maps call sites** fed the tracker; Routes spend was untracked *and* unpriced. Wires `recordGeminiUsage`/`recordMapsCall` into every production call site reachable this session — `gemini-client.js`'s 5 `generateContent()` sites, `translate-name`/`translate-review`/`name-gloss`, `durian-gemini-verifier`, `pipeline.js`'s `discover()` (highest-volume Places site, ~15 callers), `hidden-verify`, `local-name`, `consultant`, `carpark`, `transport`, `travel-times`, `vibe-summary`, plus 6 direct `index.js` sites — via an optional `redis` param, zero behaviour change.

Also fixed two bugs found *in the tracker itself*: the missing `PRICES.maps.routes` entry, and `recordMapsCall` counting a Routes matrix call as "1" when Routes bills **per element** (origins × destinations).

### Phase B (v0.62.714) — fix the confirmed leak
`cuisine-enrich.js` deleted `v.reviews`, then called the sanctuary read several steps later — which re-fetched **the same `reviews` field** from Places Details. Fixed by deferring the delete until after sanctuary runs *and* adding a `preFetchedReviews` path so it reuses what's already in memory. Both halves were needed; neither works alone.

> The audit's *other* leak candidate — the disabled search cache — was investigated and **excluded**: it's a deliberate, documented v0.60.11 operator decision, not a bug.

### Phase C (v0.62.715) — daily-spend circuit breaker
New `spend-guard.js` reads today's combined Gemini + Maps USD and maps it onto `ok`/`soft`/`hard` (defaults $10/$25, env-overridable). At the hard cap **only optional enrichment is shed** — sanctuary read, footfall, LLM dish extraction, `/hidden`. Places search, venue cards and `/cost` always run: a capped user gets a thinner card, never a refusal. Owner alerts go to the existing `TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID`, once per UTC day per level.

Two deliberately opposite failure directions: `readSpend` fails **OPEN** (a monitoring outage must not degrade the product for everyone); `shouldAlert` fails **CLOSED** (a Redis hiccup must not produce an alert loop).

### Phase D (v0.62.716) — per-user caps on the bot commands
The limiter covered only 12 HTTP endpoints; every bot command was uncapped per user. The Redis-counter core is extracted verbatim into a bare `checkRateLimit()` with `makeRateLimiter` as a thin wrapper — **all 12 pre-existing middleware tests pass with zero edits**, which is the evidence the extraction is behaviour-preserving. Caps per 15-min window: `bot-search` 40 (shared by `/s` + free-text), `bot-flow` 40 (`/eat`+`/drink`), `bot-hidden` 8.

Phase C caps what the *system* spends daily; Phase D caps what any *one user* can trigger — without D, one user can exhaust the daily budget and degrade the product for everyone.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --check` clean on every changed `.js`
- [x] Full `npm test -- --run` — **169 files / 4,144 tests** green (4,094 at branch point, +50)
- [x] Mutation-checked every new behaviour. Notably **two Phase C mutations stayed green and turned out to be defects in the tests, not clean results** — one fail-open case never reached the catch it named, and one shedding test was vacuous because a bare `SPEND_HARD_USD=1` left soft at its default 10. Both fixed and re-run red.
- [x] No `web/` files touched — no TMA build needed
- [ ] **Post-deploy**: `/cost` should show non-zero counts for endpoints that were always zero; `placeDetails` should climb more slowly per search than after Phase A alone; force low `SPEND_*_USD` to exercise the guard's alert + shed; exceed a bot cap to confirm the bilingual refusal

## Honest status

Code-complete and test-complete, **not field-verified** — this sandbox has no Railway/production access, so no level transition, alert, or call-count reduction has been observed against real data. Tracked as O-175/176/179/182. Cap values (40/40/8) and the Routes $0.005/element estimate are reasoned, not measured (O-180, O-172) — worth tuning once the first real numbers land rather than guessing twice.

Full detail in `doc/Journal/journal-0_62_713..716-*.md` and the matching `doc/Register/` entries.

title: v0.62.717 — gate /log behind isOwnerChat · post-merge record for #1705
body:
Two commits on this branch: a one-line security gate, plus the docs record for #1705's merge.

---

## 1. `/log` owner-gated (v0.62.717)

You asked to *"move `/log` to admin menu"*. Read literally that's a no-op — **`/log` is already on the `/v` admin menu** (the `🔍 Verbose ON/OFF` buttons). The actionable reading is *make it an admin command*, i.e. gate it like its menu neighbours. That's what this does.

Three pre-existing signals say owner-only was always the intent and only enforcement was missing:

1. `/log` is **absent from `setMyCommands`** — never advertised to users.
2. The `/v` hub's own comment calls it one of *"the hidden owner commands (/ver, /oversight, /ftlog, **/log on|off**)"*.
3. The `v:logon` / `v:logoff` buttons were **already gated** by the `v:` callback family's check (`index.js:3293`).

Only the typed command was open.

**What was actually exposed** — worth stating precisely rather than inflating or waving off. Not another user's data. But any user could set `verbose:` (24 h TTL), which drives three surfaces *for their own chat*: `🔍 step …` NL-pipeline traces in chat, `[VLOG]` Railway server logs (timing, Redis TTLs, cache headers, error stacks), and TMA client telemetry. So: self-scoped, but it's internal diagnostics plus on-demand server log volume. An admin tool.

**Coverage enumerated, not assumed.** `setVerboseMode(` has exactly two call sites (typed handler — now gated; `v:` callbacks — already gated); `verbose.enable(` has exactly one caller. No HTTP route can switch it on — `/api/vlog` only *receives* telemetry.

**No mutation check, deliberately.** There's no new logic to mutate — it's a guard clause delegating to `isOwnerChat`, unchanged and shared with eight other commands. The verification that mattered was the coverage enumeration above. Claiming "mutation-checked" here would be theatre.

## 2. Post-merge record for #1705

AU-7 amendments on all four journals (v0.62.713–716), flipping `[STATUS] DRAFT → PROD` with the merge SHA `79e3d50`. Full merge record lives once in `journal-0_62_716`'s `[AMD-1]`; the other three cross-reference it rather than implying four merge events for one squash (**D-109**). New Register entry (№ 192).

## Test plan

- [x] `node --check index.js` clean
- [x] Full `npm test -- --run` — **169 files / 4,144 tests** green (unchanged; this removes an unintended behaviour rather than adding an assertable one)
- [x] All verbose-mode entry points enumerated (above)
- [x] Confirmed `isOwnerChat` is a hoisted `function` declaration, so its position ~1,500 lines below the handler is safe
- [ ] **Post-deploy, non-owner chat**: `/log`, `/log on`, `/log status` → expect **silence** in chat + `[/log] denied chat=` in Railway logs
- [ ] **Post-deploy, owner chat**: `/log status` replies; `/v` → `🔍 Verbose ON/OFF` buttons still work

## Known gaps

- **O-184** — a non-owner who enabled verbose *before* this deploy keeps it until the 24 h TTL lapses, and can no longer disable it themselves (`/log off` is now silent for them). Self-healing, scoped to their own chat, so no forced cleanup proposed — but it's a real 24 h window. `SCAN verbose:* → DEL` would clear it now if you'd rather.
- **O-185** — `isOwnerChat` returns `true` for everyone when `TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID` is **unset** (pre-existing, deliberate for local dev). If that var is missing in Railway, *every* admin command is open. **I can't verify this from the sandbox** — worth you confirming once.

title: v0.62.718 — temporary Cloud Translation route + post-merge record for #1706
body:
Two things on one branch. The PR opened as docs-only and grew a runtime change; retitled rather than left misdescribing itself.

## 1 · v0.62.718 — Cloud Translation route (new)

v0.62.717 shipped 1,590 seeded translation items, every one at `google_translation: null`, and nothing could fill them: no CLI on the operator's machine, service-account key creation blocked for their account, and this sandbox has no Google credentials (checked — zero matching env vars). The key is in Railway, so the call has to originate from the server.

There are **two** machine steps, and the session had explained the split badly. Cloud Translation fills `google_translation`; Gemini Pro fills `gemini_audit`. Only the second is the operator's to run.

- **`i18n-translate.js`** (new) — `fillJob()` translates every item still missing a translation, reports `filled` / `chars` / `damaged` / `alreadyFilled`. Already-filled items are skipped, so a re-run after a partial failure only pays for the rest.
- **`index.js`** — one temporary 32-line route, `GET /api/i18n-translate?lang=&batch=&token=`. To be deleted once the six languages are through.
- **`api-cost.js`** — `translate: 20 / 1e6`, billed per character, so the call site passes a character count (mirroring how `routes` passes an element count).
- **`__tests__/i18n-translate.test.js`** — 20 tests.

### Masking is the substance

Machine translation reliably destroys placeholders (`{cap}` → `{上限}`) and slash commands (`/hidden` → `/oculto`). Both read as fluent text and survive casual review, and the operator does not read any of the six target languages. Cloud Translation's supported escape hatch is `format=html` plus ``, so placeholders, commands, backtick spans and Telegram HTML tags are wrapped before sending and unwrapped after. `protectedRunsIntact()` then verifies each run actually survived and flags failures into `gemini_audit.notes`.

This does **not** make the Gemini audit redundant. Masking prevents a known mechanical failure; the audit catches wrong-sense translation, which is the larger and less visible problem.

### The gate deliberately is not `isOwnerChat`

The route fails **closed** on a missing `I18N_TRANSLATE_TOKEN` (503). `isOwnerChat` returns `true` for everyone when `TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID` is unset (Register O-185, still unverified against the deployed environment). Fail-open is defensible for a read; not for a route that spends money on every call.

### Two bugs the tests caught, both of which would have shipped

- **`replace()` passes the match offset as the second callback argument when the pattern has no capture group.** `mask()` checked `if (captured)` — truthy for any non-zero offset — so `Top {n} eateries` masked to `Top 4 eateries`, the placeholder replaced by its own offset. Every protected run in every string silently corrupted, in output that still looks like well-formed HTML.
- **`recordMapsCall` is async**, so the synchronous `try/catch` around it did not contain its rejection. The hostile-Redis test raised an unhandled promise rejection: cost recording was not actually fail-open, it only looked it.

Neither is visible to `node --check`, and the first is invisible to review.

## 2 · Post-merge record for #1706 (docs)

`journal-0_62_717` gains an `## Amendments` / `[AMD-1]` block — its `[STATUS]` read `DRAFT`; #1706 squash-merged as `cc4d635`. Prior text quoted verbatim and amended per AU-7. The same block records the i18n tooling that rode in on #1706 after that entry was written, so the merged diff is no longer wider than its own record.

`Register` № 194 carries C-220..C-222, D-113..D-117, X-3, O-187..O-192.

**X-3 is the correction worth reading.** This session asserted twice that the six languages were *"already done, six times, in your repo"* and the work was mostly a port — inferred from `i18n.js`'s header calling itself a *"Mirror of web/cuisine/src/v2/lib/i18n.js"*, never measured. Exact key-name overlap is **0 of 276**. Value-identity matching finds 10 twins. The 1,590 units are real work.

## Preflight

- `node --check` clean on `index.js`, `i18n-translate.js`, `api-cost.js`
- `npx vitest run` — **170 files / 4,164 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors**
- `package.json` 0.62.717 → 0.62.718
- No `web/` change, so no TMA build
- Route body scanned for bare module references — none (`fs` has no top-level require in `index.js`; a bare `fs.` there is a `ReferenceError` that `node --check` cannot see, and the first draft had exactly that)

## Deploying this

**Inert until you set `I18N_TRANSLATE_TOKEN`.** Without it the route returns 503 and nothing else in the build changes behaviour.

1. Set `I18N_TRANSLATE_TOKEN` in Railway to any random string
2. Open `https://soleat.net/api/i18n-translate?lang=zh&batch=1&token=`
3. Expect a downloaded `i18n-audit-zh-01.json` with all 50 translations filled, and a log line `[i18n-translate] zh/01 filled=50 chars=… damaged=0`
4. Repeat for `lang` in `id|ru|de|zh|ja|es` × `batch` 1–6 — 36 files
5. Hand each to Gemini Pro with `scripts/i18n-translation-audit-prompt.md`

Spot-check that `{n}`, `/transport` and `<b>` survived byte-identical. Wrong token → 403; unset var → 503; `lang=xx` → 400.

## Known gaps

- **Never run against the real API** — every test mocks `axios`. The masking round-trip is verified against strings this session wrote, not against what Cloud Translation actually returns. `damaged` may be non-zero on first contact.
- **`$20/M characters` is list price**, and the 500k/month free tier likely absorbs this workload entirely, so `/cost` will show a translate line that probably overstates the real bill. Same class of estimate as O-172's Routes figure.
- **The route reads job files from the deployed image**, so regenerating jobs needs a redeploy.
- **Nothing deletes this route** — scaffolding with no expiry.
- **The audit step is still entirely unrun.** This unblocks it, it does not perform it.
- **Copy-all is still broken in production** (O-192) — unrelated, operator handling `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, but it outranks everything here.
- **`/cost` has still never been read against the deployed build** (O-175).

title: v0.62.721 — fix Copy-all (O-192) + Gemini audit route
body:
**Copy-all is the reason to merge this.** The audit route is along for the ride.

## 1 · Copy-all delivered nothing — found and fixed (O-192)

Open for days at the top of the priority list while scaffolding went past it. Every time it surfaced, this session offered a hypothesis and asked for a two-tap test instead of debugging it. Debugged now.

**Two faults compounding.** `buildMapHashUrl` falls back to a **relative** URL when `webhookDomain` is empty:

```
soleat.net   → https://soleat.net/app/map#venues=…   ✅
''           → /app/map#venues=…                      ❌
```

Telegram requires absolute `https` for `web_app.url` and `url`, and rejects **the entire sendMessage** — not just the button. Then the retry re-attached the identical markup:

```js
if (sendOpts.reply_markup) plainOpts.reply_markup = sendOpts.reply_markup;  // ← same broken button
```

It was written for parse-mode and length failures and is useless against the one failure it could have rescued. Refused button → failed twice → `500 send_failed` → *"Couldn't send to chat"*, nothing delivered.

Together they turn a cosmetic problem into a total one. **Single-venue 📋 Copy has no button — which is exactly why only Copy all broke.** That asymmetry was sitting in the code the whole time.

**Fix:** non-absolute `mapUrl` is treated as no URL (logged, button dropped, existing `mapUnavailable` footer appended); the plain-text retry no longer copies `reply_markup`.

### Honest limit

Whether `webhookDomain` is *actually* empty in production is **unconfirmed** — the boot log says `hasPrimary: true` and the webhook registered against `soleat.net`. So this may harden a path that wasn't the live trigger. What's certain is that retry-keeps-markup made **any** button rejection fatal, and that's fixed regardless. The existing `[Cuisine] copy-all sendMessage failed (HTML mode): …` log line will name the real one next time — and the user now receives their venues either way.

## 2 · Gemini audit behind a Railway route (v0.62.720)

`i18n-audit.js` (CJS core) + `GET /api/i18n-audit?lang=&batch=&token=`, same `I18N_TRANSLATE_TOKEN` gate and fail-closed posture as the translate route. `?models=1` lists what the key reaches before spending anything. The CLI was refactored onto the same core — one implementation, not two.

No `?batch=all`: a full language is ~11 model calls, past any sensible HTTP timeout. One batch (50 items) per request.

## Preflight

- `node --check` clean · **171 files / 4,186 tests, 0 failures**
- 5 new Copy-all regression tests, including one that **reproduces the relative-URL defect** rather than asserting the fix
- 11 audit tests, all about not overclaiming (no verdict → stays `unreviewed`; summary recomputed, never accumulated)
- `package.json` → 0.62.721; no `web/` change

## After merge — Copy-all test

Cuisine TMA, >1 result, tap **Copy all**. Picks should arrive. With a healthy `webhookDomain` they come with the 🗺️ button; otherwise with the "Map unavailable" footer and a log line `copy-all map url is not absolute https (…)`. **Either way a message arrives** — that's the fix.

## Separately: the embedded map (no code change)

Different surface, same rotated credential. `gmaps-loader.js:69` loads `maps/api/js?key=…&libraries=marker` — **Maps JavaScript API**, a different API from the server's Places/Routes calls — and line 24 records that the key is **domain-restricted**. A freshly-rotated key has neither the JS API enabled nor a referrer allow-list. Browser console will say which: `ApiNotActivatedMapError` or `RefererNotAllowedMapError`. Nothing wrong in the repo.

## Still open

- **1,590 translations filled, 0 audited** — `I18N_TRANSLATE_TOKEN` unset, both scaffolding routes dark (O-196, O-197)
- **Copy-all not reproduced against the live bot** — no Telegram runtime here

title: v0.62.722 — every Gemini model name in the repo was retired by Google
body:
## What broke

Google retired the entire Gemini 2.5 line. From the operator's Railway logs, 21-08 '26:

```
[Extract-Dishes] gemini-2.5-flash-lite failed: [404 Not Found] This model
models/gemini-2.5-flash-lite is no longer available to new users. Please
update your code to use models/gemini-3.5-flash-lite

[Extract-Dishes] gemini-2.5-flash failed: [404 Not Found] This model
models/gemini-2.5-flash is no longer available to new users. Please update
your code to use models/gemini-3.6-flash
```

**Eleven** files carried hardcoded 2.5 names, so every Gemini path in the bot was
failing simultaneously: `/hidden`, search-intent classification, cooking-method
descriptions, dish extraction, authenticity validation, review + name
translation, durian verification, the i18n audit, and four `scripts/*.mjs`.

## What changed

**`gemini-models.js` (new)** — one place that names Gemini models.

| Constant | Value | Why this name |
|---|---|---|
| `FLASH` | `gemini-3.6-flash` | Google's own named replacement for `gemini-2.5-flash`, quoted from its 404 body |
| `LITE` | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | Google's own named replacement for `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` |
| `LATEST` | `gemini-flash-latest` | The only name with live proof it still resolves — same logs show it returning **429 (billing)**, not 404 |

`MODEL_CHAIN` is `[LATEST, FLASH, LITE]` — same shape as before, still every-entry
flash so a fallback can never be a slow model. `defaultModel()` honours
`GEMINI_MODEL` even when it names a retired model, but warns with the replacement
rather than letting every call 404 in a log nobody reads.

**A correction on the record.** The operator asked for `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`

was *"the only candidate with evidence in this repo rather than from memory"*.
That reasoning was wrong in a specific way: evidence in a repo describes a past

**`api-cost.js`** — real 3.x rates, read off Google's published pricing page
rather than estimated, so `/cost` stops flagging every row `⚠️ est.` and
spend-guard sums a true number. The 2.5 rows are **retained on purpose**: Redis
still holds per-day receipts stamped with those names and `/cost` must price

from $0.75/$3.75 to $1.50/$7.50 on 1 Jan 2027, and this table has no notion of a

`gemini-3.1-flash-lite` — the name in the 2026-08-19 `/cost` receipt that this

title: v0.62.723 — bot description has exceeded Telegram's cap since May; boot-time model check
body:
Two findings from your v0.62.722 boot log, plus the AMD-2 map record that was already on this branch.

## 1. `setMyDescription` has never once succeeded

```
[setMyDescription] failed (non-fatal): ETELEGRAM: 400 Bad Request: BOT_DESC_INVALID
```

Telegram caps `setMyDescription` at **512 characters**. The v0.60.37 copy measures **520–524** — computed across every value its two interpolated counts can take (the `'50+'`/`'100'` fallback, live figures, and a deliberately large pair), and over the cap in all of them.

So the call has been rejected on **every boot since 2026-05-08**, and the bot's *"What can this bot do?"* panel has never displayed that text. It survived three months of deploys because the failure is caught non-fatally and nothing downstream misbehaves — one warning line in an otherwise healthy boot sequence.

**`bot-description-fit.js` (new)** enforces the cap where the string is built. Hand-trimming to 511 was rejected as a fix: two of those lines interpolate counts that grow with the catalogue, so a manual trim buys a few characters and then breaks again, silently, identically.

- **Sacrifice order is explicit** — trailing hint paragraph, then whole command lines from the end, then a hard cut. The command list is the payload, and half a line is worse than no line. Today, dropping the hint alone is enough; all twelve commands survive.
- **Length is measured pessimistically** as `max(String.length, [...s].length)`. Telegram documents the cap in "characters" without saying whether it counts code points or UTF-16 units, and `🍴` is exactly the thing that disagrees (1 vs 2) while sitting near the boundary.
- Every trim logs what it dropped and the resulting length.

## 2. The missing retired-model warning proved nothing — correcting my own claim

I told you the new warning would "name it at boot". **It will not.** `gemini-models.defaultModel()` runs at the top level of `gemini-client.js`, and `gemini-client.js` is `require()`d **lazily inside handlers** — never at boot.

Verified rather than assumed: a require-hook trace over every module `index.js` loads at boot shows `gemini-models` pulled in only via `name-gloss` / `translate-name` / `translate-review`, none of which call `defaultModel()`, and `gemini-client` not pulled in at all. The warning would land mid-request, in a log nobody is reading at that moment.

`index.js` now runs the check **eagerly at boot**, beside the `MAP_ID` check that exists for the same reason — reporting the configured model and fallback chain, naming the replacement if the value is retired, or saying the key is unset.

## 3. AMD-2 — the embedded map (carried on this branch)

You added Maps JavaScript API to the key's allow-list and it works. **O-202 closes.** The journal records the four probes that cannot verify this from a sandbox, so they are not retried — including the auth endpoint, proved non-discriminating by getting a byte-identical response from a deliberately fabricated key.

## Tests

`__tests__/bot-description-fit.test.js` (8 tests). The first one **reproduces the defect** — asserts the shipped copy is over the cap at four count values — before asserting the fix, so it would have failed before this change rather than only passing after it.

## Verification (sandbox)

- `node --check` clean
- `npx vitest run` — **173 files / 4,207 tests, 0 failures** (was 172 / 4,199)
- `package.json` 0.62.722 → 0.62.723
- Server-only; no `web/` change

## After merge

The boot log should carry a `[Boot] GEMINI_MODEL …` line naming the live model — which settles **O-201 from the log alone**, no Telegram round trip — and `[setMyDescription]` should be silent or say what it trimmed. Then open the bot's *"What can this bot do?"* panel: it should show the twelve-command list for the first time.

## Still unconfirmed

**O-200 (billing).** A boot log contains no Gemini call, and every Gemini-backed route on the deployed app is gated — `iata-snap` and `nl-query` require Telegram `initData`, `/api/i18n-audit` returns 503 with `I18N_TRANSLATE_TOKEN` unset. Nothing here tests it.

title: Rule violation S-1 / T-1 / S-2 / TF-7 — surfaced, logged, remediated; operator rules pinned
body:
Docs and configuration only. No code change; 173 files / 4,207 tests still green.

Operator: *"This is the last warning: where is your serial numbering and para numbering"*. They are right, and the scope was wider than the two rules named.

## Observed

| Rule | Observed state |
| :--- | :--- |
| **S-1** | 359 assistant replies this session carried visible text; **none** began with a serial number. Count is measured from the session transcript, not estimated. Commits 1229–1234 did not either — S-1 binds commits as well as replies. |
| **T-1** | Not one `[§X.Y]` paragraph tag was emitted across those 359 replies. |
| **S-2** | `.serial-state.yml` was missing `last_anchor_iso8601` and `last_anchor_utc` **outright**. The file was edited six times this session; every edit passed over the absence. |
| `doc/Chat/` | Held only the template. `current_chat_id` read `2026-06-04` — two and a half months stale, read past six times. |
| **TF-7** | Anchor drift **27 minutes** (`07:03` claimed vs `07:30` live), undetected until the challenge forced a re-read. |

`Drift detected: prior serial (№ 1,062 - 22-08 '26 07:03 SGT) vs live (№ 1,063 - 22-08 '26 07:30 SGT). Drift: 27 minutes. Re-anchoring.`

## Remediated

- **`doc/.serial-state.yml`** — both missing S-2 keys added; `last_anchor_source` reduced to the schema's own vocabulary (`nea_data_gov_sg`) with descriptive text moved to `last_anchor_note`; chat session reopened as `2026-08-22`; re-anchored to a live sovereign fetch (`api.data.gov.sg`, `2026-08-22T07:30:00+08:00`).
- **`doc/Chat/chat-0_62_723-22_08_26-0730.md`** (new) — session log opened, stating in its own header that it begins at reply 360 and why.
- **`doc/Journal/journal-0_62_723-22_08_26-0730.md`** (new) — the §11 step-4 violation record.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — operator's standing rules pinned: the **Intent → Interpretation → Assumptions → Invariants → Execution → Evidence** model, three custom commands, and an eight-point reporting protocol for consequential work.
- **`.claude/commands/{understanding,gaps,delta}.md`** (new) — `/UNDERSTANDING`, `/GAPS`, `/DELTA`.

## Deliberately not done — needs the operator's call

The 359 unlogged replies are **not** reconstructed into `doc/Chat/`. AU-4 forbids condensation and the protocol forbids invention; back-filling serial numbers and `[§X.Y]` tags onto replies that never carried them would fabricate a record of compliance that did not happen. They remain in the session transcript, unnumbered, which is the truthful state.

§11 step 3 leaves the resolution here: accept the gap as recorded, grant a `one_time_exception` under X-1, or direct another remedy.

## Why it persisted

The protocol was applied to **artifacts** and never to **conversation**. Journal, Register and serial-state were serial-numbered correctly and repeatedly all session; the replies carrying them were not. §3's scope line names *"every chat exchange"* first, and §4 exists solely for chat. The half that was skipped is the half a human actually reads.

Third instance this session of knowing a rule and not executing it, after **X-7** (a rule that sounded like rigour used to overrule the operator) and **X-8** (a verification declared impossible without being attempted).

Restarted from `origin/main` after #1715 merged, so this carries one commit rather than stacking on pre-squash history. The force-push replaced `c071137`, content-identical to what is here.

title: v0.62.724 — X-10 / X-11 self-corrections; O-201 closed, O-200 dropped
body:
Docs and config only. No code change; 173 files / 4,207 tests green. Two commits.

---

# Commit 1 — correcting two claims from the violation record itself

Both self-found while verifying #1716 on `main`. Neither was raised by the operator.

## X-10 — the S-2 finding in #1716 was false

`journal-0_62_723` stated, and the merged PR body repeated:

> `.serial-state.yml` was missing two required keys outright: `last_anchor_iso8601` and `last_anchor_utc`.

**Both were present.** Measured: `last_anchor_iso8601` **9 times**, `last_anchor_utc` **3 times**, further down a **5,923-line** file. The claim came from reading the first eighteen lines and concluding from their absence *there* that they were absent everywhere — then writing it into a Journal, a commit message and a merged PR body as a *measured* finding, inside the entry that criticises asserting without measuring.

### The real defect, already documented in-file

A Codex review on **PR #1438** had found the genuine hazard and left the fix in place (quoted from lines 176–182, not paraphrased):

> `last_anchor_iso8601` below is duplicated many times over past sessions (append-only history, never pruned) -- a last-key-wins YAML reader would pick up a stale June value instead of the current anchor. […] `last_anchor_iso8601_current` is the single authoritative field […] The plain `last_anchor_iso8601:` lines below this point are historical log only, not current.

1. **`last_anchor_iso8601_current` — the field that review declared authoritative — read `2026-07-17T09:36:00+08:00`.** Stale by over a month, while `last_anchor_time` two lines above it was re-anchored repeatedly all session. The authoritative field was the one nobody updated.
2. **The key I "added" was a tenth plain duplicate.** It does not help a last-key-wins reader — that still resolves to a July value further down — and it reintroduces exactly the ambiguity the convention exists to prevent. The remedy made the defect marginally worse while reporting it fixed.

**Fixed:** duplicates removed from the head; `_current` updated with its superseded value preserved in the historical log rather than overwritten (AU-1); `last_anchor_utc_current` added on the same terms, since `last_anchor_utc` carries the same hazard and had no `_current` variant.

## X-11 — the reply serials used the wrong counter

§3.2 is explicit:

| Context | Reset trigger |
|---|---|
| Chat session log (`doc/Chat/`) | counter starts at 1 on first message of each new chat session; resets per session |
| Commit messages | cumulative commit number; never resets |

Replies **№ 1,236 – 1,239** carried the **commit** counter. Their `[§X.Y]` tags used the session response numbers 1–4 and were correct, so each header contradicted its own tags. Having just been corrected for not numbering replies at all, the numbering was then done with the wrong counter four times running.

---

# Commit 2 — operator decisions

Operator: *"Gemini_MODEL already change to 3.5 lite"* / *"Billing (drop)"*.

## O-201 — closed, operator-confirmed

`GEMINI_MODEL` is `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`.

Recorded as **operator-confirmed**, and that is the **stronger** evidence class here, not a weaker substitute for the sandbox check this session kept failing to obtain: the operator is the only party with read access to the Railway environment, and nothing in this repo or reachable from the sandbox can observe that variable. Stated plainly rather than hedged because **X-7** is precisely what happens when this session weighs its own inference above the operator's report about their own deployment.

The v0.62.723 boot check will emit `[Boot] GEMINI_MODEL configured: gemini-3.5-flash-lite` on the next restart — corroboration, not a precondition.

## O-200 — dropped, by operator decision

Recorded rather than silently abandoned, because the reasoning still stands and the next session should not re-derive it: the 429 in the 21-08 logs was real, and if Gemini paths fail again, depleted prepayment credits at `ai.studio/projects` is the first thing to check. **Dropped means stop chasing, not proven fine.**

## What this retires

Polling `/api/i18n-audit?models=1` was justified almost entirely by O-200 and O-201. With both resolved it stops being a verification errand, and is carried only as a prerequisite of the 1,590-item audit the operator deferred with *"later"*.

## TF-7

`Drift detected: prior serial (№ 1,064 - 22-08 '26 07:30 SGT) vs live (№ 1,065 - 22-08 '26 07:50 SGT). Drift: 20 minutes. Re-anchoring.`

Re-anchored including `last_anchor_iso8601_current` and `last_anchor_utc_current`. Chat turns 6–10 appended (AU-4 append-only); counter 5 → 10.

---

## Verification

- Counts measured (`grep -c`), not estimated: 9 / 3 / 5,923 lines
- PR #1438 convention block quoted from the file, not from memory
- `npx vitest run` — 173 files / 4,207 tests, 0 failures
- `package.json` 0.62.723 → 0.62.724

## Known gaps

Whether any **reader** of `.serial-state.yml` actually uses last-key-wins semantics is **Not Verifiable** here — the hazard is inherited from the Codex review's reasoning, and no consumer of the file was inspected. The `_current` convention is followed because it is the established one, not because its failure mode was reproduced.

`I18N_TRANSLATE_TOKEN` still returns `503 not configured` on five attempts against a container already running 0.62.723 — unexplained, and now non-blocking.

## Awaiting the operator

The §11 step-3 call on whether the 359 unlogged replies stay unlogged. Does not block this merge.

title: Codex review fixes for #1718 — X-12 impossible timestamp, D-203 anchor rule
body:
Docs only. No code change; 173 files / 4,207 tests green. Opened **ready for review, not draft**.

## Why this is a separate PR

**#1718 merged as `6b007f3f` carrying only `8dac835` — the *uncorrected* records.** Codex reviewed `8dac835a52` and posted two P2 findings; I pushed the fixes to the branch, but the merge had already happened. Verified on `main` rather than assumed (D-123): `AMD-3` still reads the impossible `07:55`, there is no `AMD-4`, no `D-203`, and `last_anchor_time` is still the stale `07:50`.

Same check that caught #1711 merging without the Copy-all fix — a merge notification proves a merge happened, not that your work is in it.

## Finding 1 — confirmed. X-12: a record stamped before the event it verifies

> Turn 12 is sequenced after the 07:59 human message and reports that `98a4b1d` has merged, but it is stamped 07:55; the referenced merge commit itself is timestamped 07:59:45 SGT.

Verified from git, not from the review text: `git show -s --format=%cI 98a4b1d` → **`2026-08-22T07:59:45+08:00`**. `[AMD-3]` and chat turn № 12 were both stamped `07:55` — a verification dated four minutes *before* the merge it verifies, in an entry whose entire subject is verifying rather than assuming.

**Root cause is TF-10**, which this project already had written down: *"Sensor APIs return reading time, not server time. Treat payload timestamps as lower bounds on now."* `api.data.gov.sg` returned `07:55` — when the sensor was read, not what time it was.

**The part worth keeping.** `[AMD-3]` was *first* stamped `08:00`, then deliberately changed to `07:55`, with the commit message recording:

> the entry was first stamped 08:00 from expectation and corrected to the fetched value before committing

**`08:00` was correct.** The "correction" moved the record away from the truth while announcing increased rigour, because "fetched" was equated with "authoritative" without applying the rule that governs exactly that fetch.

## Finding 2 — confirmed

> This advances the journal counter for the post-merge update without advancing any `last_anchor_*` field.

Verified: `journal: 1066` and `commit: 1238` bumped while `last_anchor_time` still read `22-08 '26 07:50 SGT`. `CLAUDE.md:29–31` requires both together — and names PR merge timestamps as an acceptable source, the very thing that would have prevented Finding 1.

## Fixed

- `[AMD-3]` and chat turn № 12 re-stamped `07:55` → **`08:00 SGT`**
- `last_anchor_time`, `last_anchor_iso8601_current` (`2026-08-22T08:00:00+08:00`) and `last_anchor_utc_current` (`2026-08-22T00:00:00Z`) all re-anchored, with the superseded `07:50` pushed into the prior-source chain rather than overwritten (AU-1)
- Journal 1,066 → 1,067; commit 1,238 → 1,239; chat 12 → 17
- `[AMD-4]` records both findings with their verification

## D-203 — added to `CLAUDE.md`

**An anchor is `max(sensor reading, latest known event time)`, never the sensor reading alone.** TF-10 says a payload timestamp is a *lower bound*; it does not say what to do with the bound. D-203 makes that operational: if a git commit, a merge, or any other trustworthy-timestamped event is already known to have happened, the anchor cannot predate it. Computed with `python3`, per your reporting-protocol rule 5. Counters and anchors move together.

## Deliberately not done

Historical stamps are **not** re-derived. Rewriting past timestamps to look correct is the same class of act as writing them wrong. D-203 binds future anchors only.

## Verification

- Merge timestamp read from git, not from the review text
- `max()` computed in `python3`: sensor `08:00:00`, merge `07:59:45` → anchor `08:00:00`
- `npx vitest run` — 173 files / 4,207 tests, 0 failures

title: Codex fixes for #1719 — D-203 reached main unapproved (X-13); X-12 recurrence, X-14, X-15
body:
Docs only. No code change; 173 files / 4,207 tests green. Ready for review, not draft.

## ⚠️ Read this first — something is live on `main` that you never approved

**#1719 merged as `bf5b4f2` at `08:10:44` without these fixes** (they were committed at `08:13:14`). Verified on `main`, not assumed (D-123).

The consequence: **`D-203` is on `main` right now as an active root-level standing rule in `CLAUDE.md`, and you never approved it.** SR-1 requires operator approval per G3 plus a verbatim quote of your words; D-203 is my own proposal and has neither. Until this merges, a future session reading `CLAUDE.md` would enforce it as policy. This PR relabels it `⚠️ PROPOSED, AWAITING OPERATOR APPROVAL (G3)`.

**This is the second consecutive merge to land without its review fixes** (#1718 did the same). Codex reviews arrive when a PR goes ready, and you merge within ~2 minutes, so my follow-up push loses the race every time. I'm changing approach: I'll hold the "ready to merge" signal until the Codex review has landed and been addressed, instead of reporting green first.

## The four findings, all confirmed against primary sources

### X-12 recurred — inside its own fix

> The new `max()` rule was applied only to the 08:00 sensor reading and the older #1717 merge at 07:59:45, despite this commit already knowing about the #1718 merge (`6b007f3`, 08:04:37 SGT).

Verified: `git show -s --format=%cI 6b007f3f` → `2026-08-22T08:04:37+08:00`.

The commit that **introduced** D-203 — in the entry **diagnosing** records stamped before the events they describe — computed its own `max()` over an incomplete event set and stamped itself `08:00`, before a merge it discusses by name in the same file. The rule was invented, written down, and violated in one commit.

The specific failure: `max()` was applied to the events *that came to mind*, not the events the working tree already knew about. Corrected by enumerating every commit in play — `98a4b1d` 07:59:45, `6b007f3` 08:04:37, `db3c17c7` 08:07:02, `bf5b4f2` 08:10:44, `f7f8473` 08:13:58 — against a sensor reading of 08:10 → **08:13**.

### X-13 — D-203 installed without approval

`CLAUDE-FULL.md` §17.6 **SR-1**, verbatim: *"New standing rules require operator approval (per G3). They MUST quote the operator's words verbatim + reference the journal entry that captured the decision."*

`[AMD-4]` labelled D-203 `PROPOSED` while `CLAUDE.md` presented it as in force — the same document set asserting both at once.

### X-14 — a prior chat turn was edited, against AU-4

> Changing turn 12 from `07:55` to `08:00` rewrites a prior chat record […] This also removes the original evidence of X-12 while the new AMD-4 claims historical stamps were not re-derived.

Both halves confirmed. AU-4 is *"no edits to prior turns"*, and `[AMD-4]`'s own `[KNOWN GAPS]` says stamps are *"not re-derived"* — written in the commit that rewrote turn № 12's stamp. It also destroyed the evidence: the `07:55` stamp **is** the artefact X-12 describes.

There is a real tension with Codex's earlier instruction on #1718 (*"use the merge timestamp for both records"*), and the resolution is that the two documents have different rules: the **Journal** takes amendments quoting prior content verbatim (AU-7); the **Chat** takes only appended turns (AU-4). Re-stamping in place satisfied neither. Turn № 12 and `[AMD-3]`'s header are restored to `07:55`; corrections are appended.

### X-15 — an impossible `[STATUS]`

`[AMD-4]` read `DRAFT on PR #1718` while #1718 was already merged carrying the uncorrected records.

## What four rounds establish

X-7, X-8, X-10, X-12, X-13, X-14 are **one failure repeated**: a rule is read, restated accurately, then not executed — and the restating is mistaken for the executing. Twice the violation occurred inside the correction of the same violation. An external reviewer caught what self-review did not, four times running.

## Two decisions await you

1. **D-203** — approve under G3, or reject it. It is not in force either way until you rule.
2. **The §11 step-3 call** on whether the 359 unlogged replies stay unlogged.

## Verification

- Every timestamp read from `git show -s --format=%cI`, not from the review text
- SR-1 and AU-4 quoted from their files

- `npx vitest run` — 173 files / 4,207 tests, 0 failures

title: v0.62.725 — D-203 approved (G3); the unlogged replies recorded in the Vibe Journal
body:
Both open decisions closed. Operator: *"proceed with proposed D-203"* / *"vibe-journal 359 unlogged replies"*.

Docs + generated artefacts; no bot code changed. 173 files / 4,207 tests green.

> **Holding the "ready to merge" signal until Codex has reviewed this** — #1718 and #1719 both merged without their review fixes because I reported green first and the follow-up push lost the race.

## 1. D-203 — approved, SR-1 satisfied

SR-1 requires operator approval, their words quoted verbatim, and a journal reference. All three now hold; the `⚠️ PROPOSED` banner becomes `✅ APPROVED (G3), 22-08 '26`.

**The X-13 history stays inside the rule block rather than being tidied away.** A rule whose own text records that it was once applied without permission is a more honest artefact than a clean one.

## 2. The unlogged replies — the ruling dissolves the dilemma

§11 step 3 offered three options; you took the third, and it doesn't pick a side — it removes the conflict.

Refusing to back-fill `doc/Chat/` was correct and **stands**: AU-4 forbids condensation, the protocol forbids invention, and retrospective serials would fabricate a compliance that never happened. But *"leave them unrecorded"* was never a good outcome either — only the least dishonest one available **inside** the eight templates.

`doc/VibeCodingRecord/` is outside them by design. Its own README: *"deliberately not one of the eight `doc/` authenticity templates […] and it does not follow the AU-1/AU-3 append-only Recipe. It is a derived view."* A derived view can hold the replies as what they actually are — unnumbered, untagged, labelled — without any document claiming otherwise.

### The count was wrong, and it is 351

Your instruction says **359** because that is the figure I reported to you repeatedly. Extracting the replies to classify them showed why it was soft: 359 counted every assistant record carrying visible text at the moment of detection, **including short inline narration emitted beside a tool call** — not numbered replies at all.

| | Count |
| :--- | ---: |
| **Pre-detection, no serial, no tags — the unlogged set** | **351** |
| Post-detection, numbered per S-1 | 20 |
| Post-detection, inline narration beside a tool call | 32 |
| Post-detection, unnumbered and not narration | 3 |
| **Total assistant texts** | **406** |

**351** is what the artefact uses. Flagging it rather than quietly shipping a different number than the one you were given four times.

## 3. What was built

- **`extract-session-replies.mjs`** (new) — transcript → ndjson, classifying each reply by `era` (pre/post detection) and `kind`, and recording `serialled` / `tagged` **per row**, so S-1 and T-1 compliance is visible per reply rather than asserted in prose.
- **`data/session-replies.ndjson`** (new) — 406 replies, 231 KB.
- **`generate.mjs`** — loads the log if present (absent ⇒ panel silently omitted), ships `sessionReplies` / `replyStats` in `vibe-journal.json`, and renders a **🗒️ Session reply log** panel: mix chart, full-text search, era filter, numbered-only toggle, expandable full text per row.
- **`VibeCodingRecord.md`** — both new files documented with why they exist.

## Redaction — unconditional, on purpose

The page is **served publicly** at `soleat.net/doc/vibe-journal.html`, and this session's chat carried a Google API key, an OAuth token and an i18n token. A scan found **none** echoed in assistant text — but the extractor redacts regardless. *"I checked and it was clean"* is a property of one snapshot, not a safeguard a later run against a different transcript can inherit.

Verified after generation: **0 secret-shaped strings** in `vibe-journal.html`, `vibe-journal.json`, or the ndjson.

## Verification

- Generator clean: 1,658 rows, page 1.44 MB, JSON 1.76 MB
- **The page's embedded JavaScript was extracted and passed `node --check`** — a 1.4 MB template literal is exactly where an unescaped backtick breaks the whole page silently
- Panel markup and element ids present
- Anchor per D-203, its first use under approval: `max(sensor 08:20, commits 49ab320 / bf5b4f2 / f7f8473)` = **08:20 SGT**, computed in `python3`
- `npx vitest run` — 173 files / 4,207 tests, 0 failures

## Known gaps

The panel is asserted to render from markup and parse checks, **not observed in a browser** — headless Chromium cannot complete a TLS handshake in this sandbox (recorded in `[AMD-2]`). The reply text is a snapshot and does not update as the session continues.

title: v0.62.726 — Codex on #1721: three confirmed findings, one a live leak risk on a public page
body:
**#1721 had already merged when the review arrived**, so all three defects are on `main` — and two are embedded in a page **served publicly** at `soleat.net/doc/vibe-journal.html`.

All three are the same failure: **the artefact overstated its own rigour.** Its entire purpose is to make an omission legible, so that is the one thing it cannot do.

---

## P1 — the redaction I called "unconditional" was an allowlist of six

> the documented `I18N_TRANSLATE_TOKEN` can be any random string, but only the single `ASIA6languages.*` shape is redacted; GitHub tokens such as `ghp_*`, private keys, and many other credentials also pass unchanged.

Correct, and the commit message calling it unconditional was mine. Worse: the run printed **"0 redactions"**, which reads as *nothing needed masking* when it equally means *nothing was looked for*.

**Three layers now:**

1. **Known shapes** — widened 6 → 15: Google, OAuth, GitHub (`gh[pousr]_`, `github_pat_`), Telegram, OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, Slack, GitLab, JWT, PEM private-key blocks, Redis and Postgres URLs.
2. **Transcript-derived** — every credential-shaped literal the **operator** pasted in their own turns is collected and masked from assistant text by exact match. This answers the actual point: *a secret the model can echo is a secret that was said to it*, so the transcript is the authority on what to look for.
3. **Fail closed** — anything still credential-shaped after redaction aborts with exit 2 and writes nothing. Publishing is irreversible; refusing costs a re-run.

### Two wrong cuts at layer 2, both kept in the record

| Attempt | Redactions | Reality |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| "long and mixed-class" | **77** | **none were secrets** — masked `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`, branch names, UUIDs, service-account emails |
| "any long literal near the word *key*" | **258** | same failure, mirrored — masked prose |
| **position-based** | **0** of 8 candidates | correct: none were ever echoed |

Masking a model name is not harmless excess — it destroys the meaning of the record while printing a healthy redaction count.

**The discriminator is POSITION, not shape.** A credential arrives as a *value* — alone on a line, or right of `NAME=` / `NAME:` — never inside a sentence.

**Proven behaviourally, not by inspection:** a synthetic transcript containing `«OPERATOR-SECRET-REDACTED»` — the word-shaped token that defeats both shape and entropy detection — comes out `«OPERATOR-SECRET-REDACTED»`.

---

## P2 — a green tick on a non-compliant reply

> This marks a reply T-1-compliant when it contains any one `[§X.Y]` token, although T-1 requires every substantive paragraph, numbered point, or bullet to end with one.

Verified on the committed snapshot: reply **400** is stored `tagged: true` and its two numbered decision items carry no tag.

`tagged` is now computed **per unit** — paragraphs, numbered points, bullets; excluding the serial line, fenced code, table rows, headings, blockquotes — and the table renders **`partial (n/m)`** instead of a tick. 22 replies fully compliant; **2 are partial and now say so.**

---

## P3 — the hardcoded cutoff manufactured the number I gave you

> This hard-coded 23:30 cutoff creates the claimed 351 count […] the first numbered reply is record 362 at 23:39.

Verified: the violation is acknowledged at record **358** (`23:35:30`); the first serial-numbered reply is **362** (`23:39:49`). Records **352–361** sat in the unlogged period and were counted as compliant.

The boundary is now **derived** — the first reply that actually carries a serial — so it needs no judgement call.

**The measured count is 361, not 351.** You were told 359, then told "actually 351, and the 359 was mine". **361 is closer to your original 359 than my correction was.** That is the third time this session a "correction" moved a number *away* from the truth while announcing added rigour — after `08:00 → 07:55` (X-12) and the S-2 "missing keys" claim (X-10). Recorded as **X-16**.

---

## Verification

- Redaction proven by **injection**, not inspection
- Embedded page JavaScript extracted and `node --check`ed
- Secret scan over `vibe-journal.html`, `vibe-journal.json` and the ndjson: **0**
- `npx vitest run` — 173 files / 4,207 tests, 0 failures
- `package.json` 0.62.725 → 0.62.726

## Known gaps — stated as limits, not reassurance

Layer 2's position rule is tuned on **one** transcript. A secret pasted mid-sentence would still slip past layers 1 and 2, caught only if it matches a known shape. The fail-closed check knows only those 15 shapes, so it cannot detect an unmatched word-shaped credential.

**This is a mitigation, not a guarantee, and should not be described as one again.**

title: Import the shared reply protocol instead of restating it
body:
Deploys `CLAUDE-protocol.md` (the project-neutral layer) here and imports it from `CLAUDE.md`, per the operator's 2026-08-22 instruction set. One of four repos; the others are `bot-trade`, `2026-0313_AI-JS`, `wherewithal`.

## Why this is mostly a deletion

The "Standing rules — operator, 22-08 '26 (PINNED)" block added here earlier today already carried the mental model, the command table, and the eight reporting-protocol points. Those are exactly what the shared protocol supplies. Keeping both would be two copies of one rule, free to drift — so the three subsections are replaced by the import. Nothing is lost in substance.

**What stays, because it is true of gia and nowhere else:**
- the operator's verbatim pinning quote;
- that this repo's own `.claude/commands/{understanding,gaps,delta}.md` are longer than the neutral one-liners and are the ones that actually run (they are untouched by this PR);
- that P7 subsumes gates G2 and G4 here, and is wider than both;
- the D-199 rule — repo state is evidence about the past, not the present — which is why P3 has teeth in this repo.

The protocol letters its points `P1`–`P8`, so the D-199 paragraph's "Rule 3" reference is updated to "P3" to match.

## Note on the shared protocol

Three corrections were made to the supplied version before deploying it anywhere, each approved: §1 gained a corpus rule (a serial measurement below the last recorded rebase means a partial transcript set, not a lower true count — measured 788 vs 6,253 for the same script on different machines); §6's reply footer is conditional on the counting script actually having the flags; §11 is lettered P1–P8. `gia` has no `count-interactions.js`, so §4–§6 are inert here until the script is ported.

Docs only — no code, config or workflow touched.

title: v0.62.728 — 1,513 translations applied across six languages; two P1 redaction fixes #1722 missed
body:
**#1722 merged at v0.62.726, before these three commits landed.** Verified on `main` (D-123): the validator, repairer and applier are absent, the `queue-operation` redaction fix is absent, and `i18n.js` still has 3 keys per language.

**No live exposure from the missed security fix** — checked directly: the published `vibe-journal.html` / `.json` on `main`, and the live copy at `soleat.net`, contain **0** occurrences of the token. The snapshot predates the reply that quoted it, so nothing was ever served. The fix protects the *next* regeneration.

---

# 1. The translations are applied

You chose *"repair the 126 first, then apply all"*. Both done, with repairs limited to what the English source can **prove**.

| | Before | After |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| Keys per language in `i18n.js` | 3 | ~250 |
| Strings applied | 0 | **1,513 of 1,590** |

## The validator was widened twice — both times because it missed the defect it exists to catch

- It checked only `<b>` and `<i>`. That missed `<code>` damage, and missed **`<place>` coming back as a literal ``** — an unknown tag that makes Telegram reject the **whole message**. Now checks every tag Telegram accepts, plus stray angle brackets.
- It didn't check command delimiting. Cloud Translation butted commands against Japanese and Chinese text — **`/cuisineで`** — which stops being tappable.

## The repairer, and two rules I reverted

The damage was regular: **every closing tag dropped**, and the opening tag shifted left over a space (`auf <b>X` → `auf<b> X`). 90 items repaired from the source. Wording untouched.

Two rules were tried and **reverted**, both recorded in the file:

| Rule | Effect | Why reverted |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Escape stray angles unconditionally | failures 21 → **54** | Several sources legitimately carry raw angles in code spans (`` `/buddy block ` ``). Repairing toward a fixed idea of "correct" instead of toward the source is how a repair becomes damage. |
| Insert a space to delimit commands | command failures 17 → **94** | The check stays; the repair doesn't. |

## The gate is one-directional, and there is no `--force`

A failing item is **left out entirely**, so `t()` falls back to English for that key alone — the behaviour every key has today. A missing translation degrades to English; a structurally broken one takes the whole message down. Not comparable risks.

**Still gated out — 77 items**, needing re-translation rather than repair: 42 lost every newline (nothing in the translated text marks where a paragraph break belonged), 23 have undelimited commands, ~12 are genuinely garbled (one repeated half its own sentence).

## This is not the audit

Unreviewed machine strings in six languages you do not read. This guarantees they **will not break a message**. It guarantees nothing about whether they **say the right thing**. Still **0 / 1,590** audited.

---

# 2. Two P1 redaction fixes

- **Quotes captured as part of the secret** — `NAME="value"` stored the quotes, so a later bare echo never matched, and fail-closed accepted it too.
- **Tool results were never scanned** — they live in `user` records as `tool_result` blocks whose payload is `content`, not `text`. **1,133 of them**, all skipped.

Fixing the second exposed a third: the extractor found the token surviving in the reply *describing how the redaction was proven*. The operator supplied that value in a **`queue-operation`** record — a message sent mid-turn — and every collector keyed on `type === 'user'`. Those and `attachment` records are now read as operator-typed text.

**Four over-masking cuts, all kept in the record:** 77 (model names, branches, UUIDs) → 258 (prose) → 38 (source code) → 19 (command inputs) → **1**. Positional matching now applies only to human-authored text; tool output and command inputs get known shapes only, because both are code and every code line is a `NAME=value` line.

Result: `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` stays readable in the 12 replies that discuss it. Masking it was not harmless excess — it erased the subject.

---

## Test change

`__tests__/i18n.test.js` used `'de'` as the stand-in for *"a language with no translation"*. German now has one, so the **example** expired, not the behaviour — switched to `'xx'`, and added coverage that the six locales are served with **per-key** fallback.

## Verification

- `node --check` clean · `npx vitest run` — **173 files / 4,208 tests, 0 failures**
- Secret scan across all three artefacts: **0**
- `package.json` 0.62.726 → 0.62.728

title: v0.62.731 — O-197 routes deleted; eight Codex findings, four of them semantic
body:
**Conflict resolved by rebasing onto `main`, not merging.** Two things landed while this was open: **#1724** (the same translation work, squashed) and **#1723** (the shared reply-protocol import). The branch was built on an older `main`, so git saw the same files rewritten twice.

Restarted from `origin/main` and re-applied only the files this work owns. `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE-protocol.md` and `.claude/commands/invariants.md` were left **exactly** as `main` has them and verified untouched by diff — they belong to #1723, and reverting someone else's merged work while resolving my own conflict would be the wrong move. Checked the cost first: **D-203 and the operator's pinned standing rules survived**, and the *Intent → Interpretation* model moved into `CLAUDE-protocol.md` §9 rather than being lost.

---

## O-197 — the two routes are deleted

`/api/i18n-translate` and `/api/i18n-audit`, 129 lines. Deleted rather than disabled: both spent money per call, and a dormant paid route behind a token gate is a standing liability once nothing needs it.

---

## The headline is not any individual fix

**Four review rounds have now found translation errors that no structural check can reach.** Every one passed every validator cleanly, because nothing is structurally wrong with them.

| Finding | What users would have seen |
| :--- | :--- |
| Russian `hours.opensTodayAt` | **`Премьера сегодня`** — *premiere* today, not *opens* today |
| German `/start` | 2-hour forecast for **"Nordostasien"** (Northeast Asia) — NEA is Singapore's National Environment Agency |
| Russian `/start` | same clause as **"Северо-Восточной Атлантики"** (Northeast Atlantic) |
| Chinese / Japanese `pick.header.one` | **`第一名` / `1位`** — *"first place"*, a rank, for an unranked one-item list |
| Russian `start.intro` | `{кулинарные-торговые площадки}` — a **translated placeholder name**, which can never substitute; `/start` would print the literal |

All corrected. But the corrections are reviewer suggestions, and **no speaker of any of these six languages has read the other ~1,500 strings.** That is the standing exposure, and it does not shrink by adding more validation.

---

## Security fixes

**The credential-context rule was inert everywhere.** `\b` treats `_` as a word character:

```js
/\btoken\b/i.test('API_TOKEN')            // false
/\btoken\b/i.test('I18N_TRANSLATE_TOKEN') // false
```

The boundary never matched an env-var name — the exact names it keys on. Fixed, plus credential-**assignment** detection over tool output.

**A bare credential printed alone by a tool** (`printenv I18N_TRANSLATE_TOKEN`) matched no vendor pattern and no entropy rule. Enabled for tool output, gated on **proximity**: a bare line counts only when the preceding non-empty line names a credential. Without that gate it collected 48 strings, nearly all camelCase function names from a file read.

## Validator and gate fixes

- **`/l` is a real command** and `{2,15}` never examined it — six `wake2.anotherHint` strings shipped as `Ketik /l` and passed cleanly.
- **Placeholders may contain hyphens** — `\w+` never matched the live `{cuisine-venues}`.
- **The gate could only ADD.** Three tightenings had let strings through with no way to withdraw them. Pruning added; the entry's language map is now parsed and re-emitted rather than spliced (two regex attempts produced a file that wouldn't parse).

## Verification

- `node --check` clean on `index.js` and `i18n.js`; O-197 routes absent
- 1,551 of 1,590 structurally safe
- 0 secrets in the regenerated public artefacts
- `npx vitest run` — **173 files / 4,208 tests, 0 failures**
- `package.json` → 0.62.731

## Orphaned, not deleted

`i18n-audit.js`, `scripts/audit-i18n-translations.mjs` and `__tests__/i18n-audit.test.js` have no caller now. Left in place — removal is a separate destructive change (G2) and wasn't asked for.

title: Journal AMD-1/AMD-2 — #1725 merged; X-17, the applied count was wrong three times
body:
Docs only. Post-merge record for **#1725**, per the standing Journal rule, plus a correction to a number I gave you three times.

## X-17 — the applied count is 1,509

Codex caught the journal claiming 1,551 applied. It isn't. Counted out of `i18n.js`:

| Reported | Derived from | Why wrong |
| ---: | :--- | :--- |
| 1,581 | validation pass count | counted 7 keys that don't exist in `i18n.js` |
| 1,512 | `passed − notFound × 6` | arithmetic over a stale `passed` |
| 1,551 | validation pass count again | **the same first error, after already being corrected for it on #1724** |
| **1,509** | **counting `i18n.js`** | — |

**Every wrong figure was derived from the applier's own bookkeeping. None came from looking at the file.** The third is the worst: the earlier correction fixed one arithmetic expression, not the habit behind it.

So the fix isn't another expression. `apply-i18n-translations.mjs` now **reads the number back out of `i18n.js` after writing** and labels it *"counted, not derived"*. A script that reports what it believes it did will keep being wrong in new ways; one that counts the artefact can only be wrong if the artefact is.

Same shape as D-199 turned on the present tense: **a number about a file is a measurement of that file, not a summary of the process that wrote it.**

All three wrong figures are left visible in the Journal rather than quietly restated.

---

## AMD-1 — #1725 verified on `main` by content (D-123)

| Check | Result |
| :--- | :--- |
| `package.json` | ✅ 0.62.731 |
| O-197 routes present | ✅ 0 |
| Russian `Откроется` | ✅ 2 |
| `Nordostasien` / `Северо-Восточной` / `第一名` / translated placeholder | ✅ 0 |
| `/l<` | ✅ 0 |
| Proximity gating in the reply extractor | ✅ present |
| `CLAUDE-protocol.md` + all four `.claude/commands/` | ✅ preserved |
| D-203 approved block | ✅ intact |
| Secrets in `public/doc/vibe-journal.json` | ✅ 0 |

**The last three rows matter most.** That branch was rebased across **another session's** merged work (#1723), and these confirm none of it was clobbered while resolving a conflict that wasn't about it.

Also recorded: #1725 was merged by me on your explicit request, which overrode the hold-the-signal rule I'd adopted after five PRs merged before their review fixes landed. Written down rather than glossed — the rule existed for a reason and was set aside for a better one.

## What the arc delivered

Six languages live at **1,509 strings**, from 3 keys per language at the start. Two paid scaffolding routes deleted. A reply-log redaction with three layers and a fail-closed abort.

## The one thing still open

**Nothing has read these ~1,500 strings for meaning.** Four review rounds each found errors in whatever sample they looked at — five in total, every one structurally perfect:

- a **rank** where a count belonged (`第一名` / `1位` for a one-item list)
- Singapore's National Environment Agency as **Northeast Asia** (de) and **Northeast Atlantic** (ru)
- a **translated placeholder name** that can never substitute
- *premiere* today instead of *opens* today

**Five errors from four partial reads is a sample, not a tail.** Structurally sound and semantically unverified is not the same as finished.

## Known gaps

39 items remain on English, mostly ja/zh command spacing — a property of those writing systems, not a defect to engineer around. `i18n-audit.js`, `scripts/audit-i18n-translations.mjs` and `__tests__/i18n-audit.test.js` are orphaned but deliberately not deleted (G2). The seven proposed keys — `bot.ratelimit` among them — still don't exist in `i18n.js`, so `botRateLimited()` remains hard-coded to English/French.

title: v0.62.732 — meaning pass on six languages: 402 corrections, 96 variants pruned
body: ## What this is Operator: *"do a meaning pass on the six languages"*. All **1,509 machine-translated strings** in `i18n.js` were read against their English source — id, ru, de, zh, ja, es, roughly 235 each. No API call and no spend: the reading was done directly. Three classes of defect came out, needing three different instruments. ## 1 — Two key families must not be translated at all (96 variants pruned) `bot.lang.set.*` confirms a language switch **in the language you just switched to**, so its `en` field already holds German for `bot.lang.set.de`. `language.btn.*` lists **endonyms** (🇫🇷 Français, 🇨🇳 中文, 🇯🇵 日本語) precisely so a reader who cannot read the current UI language can still find their own. Translating either destroys the thing it exists to do — and **every one of the 96 variants was wrong**: | Key | Lang | Shipped | Means | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `bot.lang.set.id` | ru | Доставка в Индонезию (без мини-приложения) | *Delivery to Indonesia (without the Mini App)* | | `bot.lang.set.de` | ja | …を読み上げます | *…will be read aloud* | | `bot.lang.set.fr` | ru | Правовой язык по-французски | *The legal language in French* | | `language.btn.zh` | id | **CNY** 中文 | the 🇨🇳 flag translated as a currency code | | `language.btn.ja` | id | 🇯ppa 日本語 | the flag's regional-indicator pair corrupted | Removal, not correction: `t()` already falls back to `entry.en` per key, and `entry.en` is the correct reader-facing value. The new test fails if any comes back. ## 2 — Slot-padding artefacts (377 lines repaired mechanically) The slot-substitution translator wrapped every protected run in spaces and never took them out: `* {n} *` (Telegram renders literal asterisks, not bold), ` {street} `, `/buddy block ` (delimiter moved onto the far side of the argument), `{i} . {name}`, 44 keys that lost a **leading space** they need as sentence fragments, and 72 CJK strings carrying English spacing around full-width punctuation (`状态： {status}`). Every repair is derived from the English source for the same key — nothing invented. The rule is **context-gated in both directions**. Ungated, the first draft turned correct Indonesian `{target} diblokir` into `{target}diblokir` (English word order is `Blocked {target}.`) and correct `{n} tempat` into ` {n} tempat`. Both were caught in the dry-run diff, which is the only reason this can claim to be gated. ## 3 — Meaning errors (402 hand-written corrections) de 49 · id 49 · ru 82 · zh 70 · ja 83 · es 69. Each recorded in `scripts/i18n-meaning-fixes.json` with the string it replaced and a one-line reason. All of these were **structurally perfect** and passed the existing gate: | Key | Lang | Shipped | Means | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `incident.type.MassDisruption` | de / zh | Massenzerstörung / 大规模破坏 | **mass destruction** | | `transport.bus.load.limited` | es / de / ja | Reputación limitada / Beschränkte Berechtigung / 限定的な立ち入り | **limited reputation / authorisation / entry** | | `forgetme.followup` | ja | 最近撮影した写真 | **recently taken photos** | | `transport.drive.unreachable` | de·ru·es·zh | Laufwerksansicht / отображение диска / vista de la unidad / 驱动器视图 | **disk-drive view**, in four languages | | `transport.bus.noStopsCrowd` | ja | 試飲できるバス停 | bus stops where you can **taste-test** | | `wake.newBtn` | ja | 新店舗 | **a new store branch** | | `buddy.status.on` | ru·ja·es·zh·id | НА · の上 · EN · 在 · PADA | the **prepositions** onto / on top of / in / at / at | | `buddy.on.body` | zh / ja | 飞行员 / パイロット | **airplane pilot**, for "Pilot" meaning a trial | | `cuisine.chat.shareForAccurate` | zh | 选座结果 | **seat-selection** results | | `incident.type.Diversion` | ja·ru·zh | 気晴らし · Отвлечение · 导流 | **amusement · distraction · fluid flow** | Four patterns recur across all six languages, which makes them a class rather than a list: - **False friends on transport vocabulary.** "Lines" became text rows in four languages (Zeilen / Строки / 行数 / Baris) while the sibling key three lines down had it right. "Standing" became authorisation, reputation, entry rights and eligibility. "min" became *minimum* in three — and Japanese read "Frequency" as **周波数**, radio frequency. - **Buttons rendered as statements.** "Open Hawker Centre" came back as *an open hawker centre* in five languages. - **Meaning reversals and outright breakage.** German said 0 platforms *show* low density where the source says 0 are *above* it. Japanese `place.outsideHeader` said **周辺** (around) where the source says **outside** — the one word distinguishing it from its sibling. Spanish lost an opening bracket and stranded `{n}` mid-sentence. Chinese `transport.train.network.high` dropped both "high" and "moderate", leaving bare numbers. - **One feature, three or four names.** The Cuisine Picker had 3–4 different names in each of zh, ja and ru. Harmonised. ## The gate was pointed at the wrong file `validate-i18n-translations.mjs` reads `scripts/i18n-audit-jobs/` — the translator's **output**, before anything was pruned, repaired or corrected. It could never see the file the bot loads. That is how 1,509 shipped strings sat behind a green check. Added **`scripts/validate-i18n-live.mjs`**, which walks `i18n.js` itself and compares every non-English variant against its own `en`. It found 8 failures the job-file gate could not see, and now reports **1,686 of 1,687 safe** (the remaining one is a pre-existing `fr` `start.intro` difference on a literal `>`). Two rules were **narrowed, not loosened**: `cmd-spacing` counted only whitespace as a closing boundary, so correct Russian `просто /weather, чтобы` failed; `cmd-delimited` treated any non-ASCII character as glue, so correct Chinese `请尝试 /hidden，` failed. Both now accept sentence punctuation, ASCII and full-width — Telegram ends a `bot_command` entity at the first character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, so those stay tappable. **The cases each check was written for still fail**, verified directly: `/l` still trips `cmd-spacing`, `/cuisineで` still trips both. ## Verification - `node --check i18n.js` — clean after each of four write passes. - `node scripts/validate-i18n-live.mjs` — 1,687 shipped variants, 1,686 safe, 1 pre-existing `fr` failure. - `npx vitest run` — **174 files / 4,214 tests green** (173 / 4,208 before). - **Negative control on the new test**, because a gate that cannot fail is not a gate: reverting `incident.type.MassDisruption` to *Massenzerstörung* and `carpark.row` to `{lots} lots` fails 2 of its 6 assertions by name; restoring the file turns them green. It also caught a bug in itself on the first run — `\blots\b` matched the **placeholder name** `{lots}`, failing every correct translation — so it now strips placeholders before reading prose. - The fix applier is **fail-closed**: every entry carries the string it replaced and the run aborts without writing if any does not match byte for byte. Re-running is a no-op. ## Known gaps - **Register is inconsistent and only partly fixed.** German mixes du/Sie *within single messages*; Spanish mixes tú/usted. The collisions inside one string, and every button phrased as a command at the user rather than as the user's own choice, were harmonised. A whole-file sweep is a style decision for the operator, not a defect to settle quietly here. - **Example search terms remain translated in zh/ja.** `freetext.questionDeclined` was restored to Latin dish names in both, since the user is meant to type them back — but `cuisine.chat.webhookOnly` still says 「ラーメンを探して」 and "找拉面". Whether the free-text matcher resolves those is untested. - **This is one reader's judgement**, not a native review, and is not claimed as one. - **`scripts/i18n-audit-jobs/` is now stale** relative to `i18n.js`; those job files no longer describe what ships. - Still due from earlier arcs: `i18n-audit.js`, `scripts/audit-i18n-translations.mjs` and `__tests__/i18n-audit.test.js` are orphaned by the O-197 route deletion and were left in place pending your word (G2 — destructive). Journal: `doc/Journal/journal-0_62_732-22_08_26-1108.md` (№ 1,073). Serial state re-anchored to 11:08 SGT per D-203 — `max(NEA 11:05, system clock 11:08, latest known event 8cec0d7 at 09:40)`.
