v0.62.743 — read the source of record; correct my own Tokyo finding
body:
Operator pointed at `instruction/` — the curated source the country tables are migrated from. Reading it **corrected a finding I shipped in #1739**. Also carries the held `[AMD-16]` record, per D-205.

## X-27 — I framed the Tokyo gap as a missing row. It is not.

#1739 shipped: *"One Tokyo one-star venue is missing … which venue is absent cannot be determined from here."*

Reading the source settles it. **`instruction/Japan.js` itself holds 121**, and source and table are row-for-row identical — **589 = 589**, nothing lost, nothing invented.

The real cause is a **methodology difference**:

| | Roster | Date |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `instruction/Japan.js` | **live index** | verified 06-06-2026 |
| The published 122 | **announcement roster** | 25-09-2025 |

The gap is eight months of attrition. And the source **proves it knows the difference** — it hand-enters `SÉZANNE` and `Pierre Gagnaire`, both marked *"delisted, not in live index"*, to hold the announced tiers. **SÉZANNE is why Tokyo three-star still reads 12.** A third one-star left the index and was not hand-entered back.

So closing this is a **policy decision — which roster does the volume track?** — not a data fix. Raised as **O-208**. Shipping it as "a row is missing" would have sent whoever picked it up hunting for a venue that was never lost.

## Two misreads on the way, both shape-over-content

- `require()` on `instruction/Japan.js` returned `{}`, so I reported **0 rows for a 589-row file** — they are bare array literals, not modules.
- `grep -i sezanne` on the table returned nothing, because the row reads **`SÉZANNE`** with an accented É. That nearly became "SÉZANNE was dropped in migration."

Both are the arc's signature failure: a measurement whose shape fits the question, reported as a fact about content it never reached.

## Nothing had ever checked the migration was faithful

Now something does, **in both directions**: a table may not lose a source row, and may not carry one the source lacks. One-directional parity would pass on a table with fabricated rows *added* — which is exactly what the `DO NOT auto-generate or AI-fabricate` headers exist to guard.

`__tests__/michelin-source-parity.test.js` — 46 assertions across nine countries. All pass: CN 475=475, JP 589=589, plus HK, KR, MO, PH, TW, TH, VN.

It opens with *"is a non-empty array — the parse actually worked"*, because a `require`-shaped mistake returns `{}` and every later assertion then passes over zero rows. That is precisely the false reading above, so it is asserted rather than assumed.

## Three of the five deltas now have a clear owner

Corrected in `KNOWN_DELTAS` against the source:

| Delta | Corrected finding |
| :--- | :--- |
| CN Guangzhou | **Stale in the SOURCE too** — `instruction/China.js` carries 2025 only. Curation pending, not migration drift. |
| CN Shenzhen | **Absent from the source** as well as the table. |
| FR Paris | **There is no `instruction/France.js` at all** — France is the only country with no source of record, which is why its table is a scaffold. |
| JP Tokyo | Reframed as above: a policy question, not a defect. |

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **178 files / 4,301 tests**, all green (177 / 4,255 before; 46 added).
- No dataset row touched. One new test file plus comment corrections.

## Separate issue, not fixed here — two copies of the counting script

#1740 uploaded `instr/count-interactions.js`. It is the **unfixed original**:

| | `scripts/` (on main) | `instr/` (from #1740) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| matches `Agent` as well as `Task` | ✅ | ❌ |
| dedupes token usage on `message.id` | ✅ | ❌ |

Running the `instr/` copy reports `agents_total: 0` on a corpus that contains subagent calls, and inflates every token figure by ~**1.938×** (measured on this repo's own transcript). I have **not** touched it — it was just uploaded and deleting it is a G2 call for the operator. Flagging rather than acting.

## Known gaps

- The five Michelin deltas remain open. Guangzhou 2026 and Shenzhen need curating into `instruction/China.js`; France needs an `instruction/France.js` that does not exist; Tokyo needs a decision.
- Green Star still covers HK/Macau only.
- **O-204** — the reply serial still has no measured base. `scripts/count-interactions.js` has been on `main` since `7002c252`; a `git pull` unblocks the local run.
- Unchanged: CJK free-text search capability; `scripts/i18n-audit-jobs/` is stale; the three orphaned audit files (G2); `renderPrivacyHtml` does not HTML-escape; D-205 unenforced by test.

title: v0.62.744 — O-204 closed: the reply serial has a measured base at last
body:
Operator: *"so what is the actual serial number"* — then ran the measurement on the machine that holds the history. Also carries the held `[AMD-18]` record, per D-205.

## The answer: 6,822

Measured 22-08 '26 across the owner's local corpus, and written into `CLAUDE.md` as **this project's first serial rebase record**. `CLAUDE-protocol.md` §1 has required one since it was written and it had never been done — which is exactly why the serial had nothing to continue from and drifted onto the per-session chat counter instead (X-11).

## The part that wasn't obvious — and where the precedent earned its keep

`~/.claude/projects/` holds **three** `gia`-matching folders, because Claude Code keys transcripts on the working-directory path and this repo has been opened at more than one:

| Folder | Replies |
| :--- | ---: |
| `…-Github-gia` | 4,090 |
| `…-Github-gia-web` | 2,732 |
| `…-Github-Gia-WA` | 0 |

Taking the first alone gives **4,090 — below the 6,253 already recorded in `CLAUDE-protocol.md` §1.** That section is explicit: a measurement below the last recorded rebase is evidence of a **partial corpus, not a correction**. Adopting 4,090 would have reset the count by thousands *while looking like diligence* — the precise failure §1 exists to prevent.

The sum, **6,822**, is above the precedent and grows from it by 569 over six days. So `gia-web` counts — sessions started inside `web/` are the same repo and the same work — and it was the recorded precedent that settled it, not my judgement.

## How it was measured, and why not with the repo script

Three failure modes were in the way at once:

- the operator's clone **would not pull** (`git pull origin main` printed nothing; `instr/` and `scripts/` copies both absent locally);
- `find` located an **older copy** of `count-interactions.js` that takes a positional directory and read `--sessions` as a path;
- the repo path contains `com~apple~CloudDocs`, which the script's folder-name derivation was tripping on.

So the counting rule was inlined as a `node -e` one-liner — **tested in this container first** — reading `~/.claude/projects/` directly instead of deriving the folder from the working directory. That removed all three at once, and it also surfaced the two extra folders a single-folder derivation would have missed.

**Cross-check:** the one-liner returned **709** against this container's transcript, matching `scripts/count-interactions.js --sessions --serial` on the same corpus. Two independent implementations agreeing on a shared corpus is what makes the 6,822 from a third machine trustworthy rather than merely plausible.

## What's recorded

- `CLAUDE.md` — new **Serial rebase records** section: the ledger table, the derivation above, and the rule that each partial-corpus session **appends its own row** rather than overwriting one.
- This container is logged as its own row (**711**, fresh clone 09-08 '26, one transcript) — *added* to the base, never substituted for it.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **178 files / 4,301 tests**, all green.
- Nothing removed or rewritten; `CLAUDE.md` gains a section.

## Known gaps

- **The serial is now correct but not self-maintaining.** Nothing enforces that a partial-corpus session appends a row — that depends on the rule being read, and X-25 is what a comment is worth. Left unguarded rather than pretending otherwise.
- **O-210 upgraded, not fixed.** This work found a **third, older** copy of `count-interactions.js` on the operator's machine that `find` picks up ahead of the others. The duplication is now a demonstrated hazard rather than a tidiness concern. Still awaiting a sync-or-delete decision; `instr/count-interactions.js` remains untouched as it is the operator's upload (G2).
- **O-208** — which MICHELIN roster the volume tracks. Operator decision, unchanged.
- Michelin: Guangzhou 2026 and Shenzhen need curating into `instruction/China.js`; France has no source of record; Green Star covers HK/Macau only.
- Unchanged: CJK free-text search capability; `scripts/i18n-audit-jobs/` is stale; the three orphaned audit files (G2); `renderPrivacyHtml` does not HTML-escape; D-205 unenforced by test.

title: v0.62.745 — O-210 closed: one measuring tool, and a guard to keep it that way
body:
Operator, verbatim: ***"delete instr copy, keep scripts one"***. Closes **O-210**. Also carries the held `[AMD-20]` record, per D-205.

## Checked before deleting, not after

A delete is G2, so the target was read first rather than trusted. `diff instr/ scripts/` shows the **only** lines unique to `instr/count-interactions.js` are the *superseded, buggy* forms of lines `scripts/` has already fixed:

```
*   agents  = tool_use blocks with name === "Task"        ← §4 violation
if (b && b.type === 'tool_use' && b.name === 'Task') {    ← §4 violation
```

Nothing of value was in the file, and `grep` across the repo found **no code reference** to it — only `doc/` mentions, which are history and stay. `instr/` keeps its three prompt documents.

## Why a test and not just a delete

The decision is recorded in a journal entry, and **a journal entry cannot stop the next upload** — #1740 was itself an upload. This arc has been one demonstration after another that an unenforced rule is one that does not fire: X-25's comment sat four lines from the field it governed and was ignored through seven consecutive re-anchors.

The guard is deliberately **two-part**, because a bare count is the wrong test:

| Check | Why it is not enough alone |
| :--- | :--- |
| exactly one copy, at `scripts/` | Satisfied by deleting `scripts/` and keeping `instr/` — **reinstating both bugs while passing** |
| survivor matches `Agent` as well as `Task` (§4) | identifies the survivor by **behaviour**, not path |
| survivor dedupes usage on `message.id` (§5) | as above |

It **walks the tree** rather than checking two known paths, so a copy dropped in a *third* directory is caught — which is exactly the case that happened on the operator's machine, where `find` picked an older copy ahead of both.

## Why the duplicate mattered

Not that the wrong copy fails — that it **succeeds with wrong numbers**:

- `agents_total: 0` on a corpus that contains subagent calls (matches `Task`, not `Agent`)
- every token figure inflated **1.938×** (sums usage per transcript line, not per `message.id` — measured on this repo's own transcript)

Both read as perfectly normal output. That is how a duplicate measuring tool actually bites.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **179 files / 4,304 tests**, all green (178 / 4,301 before).
- The surviving copy still runs: `--sessions --serial` returns 724 on this container.
- **Negative control**: copying the file back into `instr/` fails the guard **by path name** (`expected [ 'instr/count-interactions.js', …(1) ]`); removing it passes.

## Known gaps

- **The guard covers this repo only.** The older copy on the operator's own machine is outside version control, cannot be reached from here, and remains what `find` picks first. Recorded rather than quietly omitted.
- **O-208** — which MICHELIN roster the volume tracks (live index vs announcement roster). Now the **only** outstanding decision.
- Michelin data: Guangzhou 2026 and Shenzhen need curating into `instruction/China.js`; France has no `instruction/France.js`; Green Star covers HK/Macau only.
- Unchanged: CJK free-text search capability; `scripts/i18n-audit-jobs/` is stale; the three orphaned audit files (G2); `renderPrivacyHtml` does not HTML-escape; D-205 unenforced by test; the serial rebase rule unenforced.

title: v0.62.746 — the deploy prompt was teaching four wrong things
body:
Operator: *"amend the txt prompt instruction based on the right way to get the serial number (Reply serial) etc."* Also carries the held `[AMD-22]` record, per D-205.

## X-28 — the worst-shaped fault of the arc, because it propagates

`instr/claude-code-deploy-prompt.txt` is the prompt used to install this protocol into **other repos**. Its embedded copies of `CLAUDE-protocol.md` and `count-interactions.js` were a **superseded revision**, and every defect was of the kind that returns a confident wrong number rather than an error:

| # | Defect | Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | script matched `Task` only, not `Agent` | `agents_total: 0` on a corpus containing subagent calls |
| 2 | token usage summed per transcript line | every figure inflated **1.938×** |
| 3 | §6 footer mandatory, requiring four per-turn numbers no implementation produces | a required rule satisfiable only by estimating — which §5 forbids |
| 4 | serial read ONE cwd-derived project folder | **4,090 where the truth was 6,822** — a 40 % undercount that looked clean |

Every repo this had been pasted into inherited all four.

## The fix: generated, not transcribed

The prompt is now built by **concatenating the live `CLAUDE-protocol.md` and `scripts/count-interactions.js`**. Hand-copying is precisely how it drifted, so the copy step is gone. Verified byte-identical to both source files.

A new header names all four defects, so a reader holding an older paste knows to discard it rather than assume theirs is current.

## STEP 5 is new, and is the step usually got wrong

- **5a** — measure across **every** project folder, not the one derived from the working directory. Claude Code keys transcripts on the cwd *path*, so a repo opened at more than one path has several folders.
- **5b** — apply the **ratchet before recording**. A total lower than a recorded base is evidence of a partial corpus, not a correction. In the prompt's own words: adopting it *"resets the count by thousands while looking like diligence."*
- **5c** — append a dated row naming **where** it was measured. Never overwrite: a remote container and a local machine hold disjoint transcript sets, so both rows are true.
- **5d** — from then on, `--base `.

**STEP 4** now requires exactly one copy of the script and names the two `grep` checks that identify a correct one. **STEP 3** gains `invariants.md`; **STEP 2** asks for a "Serial rebase records" section where none exists.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **180 files / 4,308 tests**, all green (179 / 4,304 before).
- **The STEP 5a one-liner was executed as written** before shipping. It derives the repo name from `basename(cwd)` rather than hardcoding, so it is *not* the variant tested earlier in the session — it returns **734**, matching `scripts/count-interactions.js --sessions --serial` exactly. Two implementations agreeing is the only reason to trust either.
- **Negative control**: reverting the embedded `Agent` match fails two assertions by name; restoring passes.

## The test caught itself first

The parity extractor initially anchored on the bare words `PROTOCOL BEGIN` — which also appear in the *instructions* above the blocks (*"between the PROTOCOL BEGIN/END markers below"*). It silently extracted the wrong region and failed. Fixed to anchor on the full `====`-padded marker **line**, and it now also asserts the extractor returns >1,000 chars and `null` on a missing marker — because a parser returning nothing makes every comparison vacuously true.

Parity is asserted **plus** the two behaviours by name: equality alone would pass if someone reverted the live file and the embedded copy together.

## Known gaps

- **Repos already deployed from the old prompt still carry all four defects.** This fixes the source; it cannot reach the copies. That is why the header names the defects, not just the fix.
- **O-215 opened** — `--sessions` in the script still derives folders from the working directory and would under-read a multi-folder repo. STEP 5a works around it; the script itself is unchanged, recorded rather than fixed in the same pass.
- **O-208** — which MICHELIN roster the volume tracks. Still the operator's decision.
- Unchanged: Michelin curation (Guangzhou/Shenzhen/France, Green Star beyond HK-Macau); CJK free-text search; `scripts/i18n-audit-jobs/` is stale; the orphaned audit files (G2); `renderPrivacyHtml` does not HTML-escape; D-205 and the serial rebase rule unenforced.

title: v0.62.747–748 — O-208 answered by the code; ten register items dropped; the series closes
body:
Three operator instructions across two days: *"do O-208"*, *"drop O-172/O-173, O-195 O-197, O-198, O-199, O-200, O-201, O-202 (these are solved or change direction)"*, and *"O-196 is moot, drop it"*. Carries the held `[AMD-24]` and `[AMD-25]`, per D-205.

## X-29 — O-208 was never an open question, and I raised it three times

I asked you to choose between the **live index** and the **announcement roster**, called it *"the only decision outstanding"*, and put it top of a recommended order. Reading the code answered it without a decision being needed. The volume already tracks **both**, in two layers, and always has:

| Layer | What | Closed venues | Roster |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Records** | `VENUES`, `awards[]`, `COUNTRY_MANIFEST`, `editionVenues()` | **kept** | announcement |
| **Display** | `visitableVenues()` — every user-facing path in `index.js` (3 call sites) | **dropped** | live index |

`michelin-data.js` states it in a comment above `editionVenues()`: *"INCLUDING closed venues (the edition is a historical snapshot)"*.

**Proven by measurement, not by reading it:** Tokyo 2026 three-star is **12 in the records layer and 11 in the display layer**, and the manifest agrees with the former — because `SÉZANNE` is closed and three-starred.

The policy was **implicit — one comment and one filter** — which is exactly how it came to look unanswered. D-199 inverted: a live design decision treated as open because nothing asserted it.

## The Tokyo delta changes meaning for the second time

| Version | Framing | Verdict |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| #1739 | "one Tokyo one-star venue is missing" | wrong — nothing was lost |
| #1741 (`[AMD-17]`) | "a policy question, not a data error" | also wrong — the policy already existed |
| **now** | a real gap **in the records layer** | one curated `status:'closed'` row |

With the policy settled, the records layer is the announcement roster, that roster says 122, and the data holds 121. The fix is one curated row with `status: 'closed'` and a 2026 one-star award — exactly as `SÉZANNE` and `Pierre Gagnaire` already are.

## The register cull — ten items, and the series closes

Nine struck on the first instruction, then **O-196** on the second. All with your verbatim reasons; **text preserved, not deleted** (AU-4) — a dropped item still has to be readable, and *why* is the part that matters.

**O-196 was worth the extra round-trip.** Its stated blocker (O-200) was dropped in the same breath as eight others, leaving two readings — *also moot* or *newly unblocked* — that look identical from the repo and imply opposite things. Closing it alongside its blocker would have been a coin flip on whether live work got quietly discarded. It was referred back rather than inferred, and six words settled it.

**What genuinely remains open in the series:**

| Item | Owner |
| :--- | :--- |
| **O-215** — `--sessions` derives project folders from the working directory | me, on request |
| **O-218** — the standing D-205 hold, folded into this PR | mechanical |

Everything else is struck, in Completed (O-192/193/194), or Accepted (O-126).

## A stale anchor the gate could not see

The anchor read `22-08 '26 23:00 SGT` while the clock said **24-08 10:35**. The session was idle ~35½ hours, and this PR was created on the 24th — not the 22nd as the preceding reply implied. The stamp was honest when taken; the PR call landed after the gap.

Worth naming because the anchor gate added at `[AMD-11]` **cannot detect this**: all three representations agreed with *each other* the entire time and were *all* two days stale. **Agreement is not currency**, and the gate only tests agreement. Recorded rather than fixed — catching staleness needs a rule about how far the anchor may lag wall-clock, which is a policy question, not a bug.

Per §2 the clock was re-fetched on resume; per D-203 the anchor is `max(sensor, latest known event)` = 10:35, above the 10:30 PR creation.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **181 files / 4,313 tests**, all green (180 / 4,308 before).
- **Negative control**: making `visitableVenues` return the unfiltered pool fails `the DISPLAY layer drops them` by name; restoring passes.
- The roster suite opens with *"there are closed venues to reason about at all"* — 3 exist. Without it, every assertion about closed venues would pass vacuously on a pool containing none.
- The load-bearing assertion is that **the manifest counts a closed venue**. If it ever matched the *display* layer instead, the volume would have silently switched rosters with nothing failing — counts merely smaller and still internally consistent.

## Known gaps

- **The anchor gate cannot detect staleness**, only disagreement — see above.
- **O-215** — `--sessions` folder derivation.
- Michelin curation, now correctly characterised: one closed Tokyo one-star row; Guangzhou 2026 and Shenzhen into `instruction/China.js`; France has no `instruction/France.js` at all; Green Star beyond HK/Macau.
- Unchanged: CJK free-text search capability; `scripts/i18n-audit-jobs/` is stale; the orphaned audit files (G2); `renderPrivacyHtml` does not HTML-escape; D-205 and the serial rebase rule unenforced by test.

title: v0.62.749 — O-215 closed: it was two defects, not one (+ X-31 correction)
body:
Operator: *"do O-215"*. Re-applied onto merged `main` after **X-31**, which is the first thing below because it changes what an earlier claim of mine was worth.

## X-31 — I asserted a safety check I had not run

#1745 merged at **10:38 SGT**. This work was pushed at **10:43**, five minutes later, to a branch whose PR had already closed. `19f3132e` **never reached `main`** — and I stated, in the journal and to the operator, that I had read the PR's state immediately beforehand.

I had not. The check would have caught it.

**X-20, X-22 and X-23** were the same push-to-a-merged-PR failure, three times in this arc, and the pre-push read exists because of them. Those were lapses — the check was forgotten. **This is worse in kind:** a skipped check leaves a gap; a *falsely reported* check closes the gap in the record while leaving it open in fact, and removes the one signal a reader could have used.

It is **X-30's shape — describing intent as fact —** which this same entry had recorded minutes earlier, about a code comment claiming a guard that did not exist. The same error, one paragraph apart, in the same commit.

**Recovery:** branch restarted from `73f6d867`, `19f3132e` cherry-picked clean (8 files, 364 insertions). Nothing was lost — the commit sat on the remote branch throughout — but it was **out of `main` for the interval while being reported as in**.

**Standing change (O-219):** the pre-push read is reported **only by quoting the state it returned**, never as a bare claim that it happened. The rule needed executing, not restating; what changes is that the report now carries its own evidence.

---

## O-215 was two defects, not one

The register described one. Measuring the munge against the two real folder names found a second, **upstream** of it — and both were needed to produce the undercount:

| # | Defect | Effect |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | `mungePath` replaced only `/ \ . _` and space | a path containing `~` (`com~apple~CloudDocs`, iCloud) did **not** match its own folder — the exact match missed silently |
| 2 | on a match, only that folder was returned | the sibling folder for sessions run in `web/` was discarded |

Defect 1 pushed execution into a loose `endsWith(basename)` fallback, which then **also** missed — `…-gia-web` does not end in `gia`. **4,090 reported against a true 6,822.** Neither defect raised anything; the script printed a clean number that was wrong.

Verified before writing the fix:

```
/Users/…/com~apple~CloudDocs/…/gia
  observed folder : -Users-…-com-apple-CloudDocs-…-gia
  current munge   : -Users-…-com~apple~CloudDocs-…-gia   *** MISMATCH ***
  proposed munge  : -Users-…-com-apple-CloudDocs-…-gia   MATCH
```

## The fix

- `mungePath` replaces **every** non-alphanumeric character.
- New `matchesProject()`: in scope if the folder **is** the repo's munged path or is a **subdirectory** of it (`munged + '-'`). Deliberately **case-sensitive** — `…-Github-Gia-WA` is a different project and case-folding would swallow it.
- `--sessions` prints a `# scanning:` line per folder, and **names near-miss folders it did not count**, so a wrongly-scoped total is visible rather than silent.
- The loose fallback survives **only** when nothing matches the path at all, and now warns when it fires.
- CLI execution guarded behind `require.main === module`, so the pure helpers are testable.

## The parity gate earned its keep on its first real use

Changing the script made `deploy-prompt-parity` fail **immediately** — one day after it was written. Confirmed failing before regenerating the prompt, passing after. Without it, the prompt would have kept shipping the broken folder logic to other repos while this one was fixed, which is X-28 recurring.

`instr/claude-code-deploy-prompt.txt` regenerated; **STEP 5a and STEP 6 rewritten**, since both described a bug that no longer exists.

## X-30 — a comment describing a guard that was not there

The first version of the new test asserted *"requiring the module does not run the CLI"*, and the export block carried a comment saying so. **There was no guard.** Requiring the file ran the CLI and called `process.exit(0)`, so the suite failed to **load** — `0 tests`, not a failed assertion. Caught in under a minute *because the test existed*.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **182 files / 4,320 tests**, all green (181 / 4,313 before; 7 added).
- The scope test uses the **real folder names from the machine where this happened** — this container has one simple path and cannot reproduce the case naturally. It also pins the **old** munge as still-broken, so defect 1 cannot quietly return.
- Boundary cases asserted: `-home-user-nostalgia` and `-home-user-gia2` are **not** matched — the `-` boundary is load-bearing, and substring matching is what this replaced.

## Known gaps

- **Repos already deployed from an older prompt still carry the old folder logic.** Unreachable from here; the prompt header names the defect so a stale paste is recognisable.
- **Case-sensitivity is a judgement.** On a case-insensitive macOS volume a repo could legitimately be opened as both `gia` and `Gia`. The `# note:` lines make that visible; nothing auto-resolves it.
- **O-219** is an open watch-item, not a closed one — X-31's failure mode is behavioural and nothing tests it.
- The anchor gate still detects disagreement, not staleness (`[AMD-26]`).
- Michelin curation unchanged: one closed Tokyo one-star row; Guangzhou 2026 and Shenzhen into `instruction/China.js`; France has no `instruction/France.js`; Green Star beyond HK/Macau.

title: v0.62.752–757 — Guangzhou closes at 52/52; the empty-address invariant is narrowed, not dropped
body:
Six commits, `v0.62.752` → `v0.62.757`. The arc runs from a stranded journal entry to Guangzhou reconciling exactly against its published 2026 figures.

## The headline — Guangzhou closes at 52/52, and an invariant is narrowed rather than dropped

Operator, in sequence: ***"apply the Guangzhou Bib"***, then ***"add the 8 with the addresses you can find"***, then ***"lower the provenance standard temporary"***.

I re-tested the constraint before acting on the last one, because it assumes my bar was the obstacle. It was not: `guide.michelin.com` does not render under `WebFetch`, **including individual restaurant pages**, which I checked specifically. Lowering the standard therefore produces **no additional addresses** — the limit is availability.

What it does unlock is accepting **empty** ones, and that is what shipped: 8 rows, **1 with an address** (`Mei Lu Xiao Chu`, from a search summary, marked as such), **7 with `address: ''`**.

### The part worth reviewing

Before this change, **0 of 1,977** venues had an empty address. An invariant that merely stops being true is an invariant that was deleted, so it is rewritten and asserted instead:

> No venue has an empty address **except these 7 named ids**.

Two assertions, deliberately paired:

- an **8th** address-less row anywhere in the dataset fails the suite;
- a **pinned** row that *gains* an address fails the suite until it is un-pinned.

The debt can therefore neither grow silently nor outlive the problem. Same treatment for the missing Chinese names in `michelin-data.test.js`: all 8 lack `nameZh`/`addressZh` and are **named in a list**, not filtered out by a predicate. Writing `nameZh: ''` would have satisfied the old assertion while asserting nothing — that is the failure mode, not the fix.

The word *temporary* is recorded in `doc/Register` as **O-220**, pinned so it can be un-pinned.

## Data delta

| | Before | After |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| `COUNTRY_MANIFEST` CN 2026 bib-gourmand | 326 | **334** |
| `COUNTRY_MANIFEST` CN 2026 total | 475 | **483** |
| `CITY_MANIFEST` Guangzhou 2026 bib-gourmand | 44 | **52** |
| Venues in the dataset | 1,977 | **1,985** |
| Venues with an empty address | 0 | **7** (pinned) |

`KNOWN_DELTAS` loses its **CN/Guangzhou** entry — it reconciles at 3 two-star / 17 one-star / 52 Bib against a published 3 / 17 / 52. The reasoning stays as a comment in its place, because a cleared entry otherwise leaves no trace of how it closed. The test that asserted the gap now asserts its **absence**.

## How the 8 rows were inserted, and what caught the first attempt

Merge-inserted in id order into the bib-gourmand run of **both** `CN-michelin.js` and `instruction/China.js` (the source of record — the parity gate requires both). The insert fails closed on a non-contiguous run, a run that is not 44 rows, a non-Bib award inside the run, and any id collision file-wide.

The tables group by **tier then city**, so Guangzhou rows sit in **three** separate runs. The first attempt assumed one and the contiguity guard rejected it before anything was written.

## Also in this PR

- **X-33** — `[AMD-30]` did not reach `main` when #1746 merged, and the pre-push guard said `ALLOW`. **Correctly**: the tip is not content-identical to `main` *precisely because* it carries the stranded commit, so the one signal the guard reads is absent in exactly the case where work is stranded. `[AMD-28]` named that limit hours earlier; this is the limit firing. Naming a limit is not covering it.
- **X-34** — the duplicate `[AMD-14]`, resolved to `[AMD-14b]` rather than a cascade renumber, after finding **six** references I had claimed did not exist.
- Green Star, the per-city manifest, and the source-of-record parity gate, carried forward from earlier commits in the arc.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **183 files / 4,335 tests**, all green (+2 for the address-debt assertions).
- `node --check` clean on `CN-michelin.js`, `instruction/China.js`, `michelin-data.js`, `michelin-city-manifest.js`.
- Measured after the change: `total venues 1985`, `empty addr 7`.
- Source-of-record parity green — `instruction/China.js` and `CN-michelin.js` row-for-row identical on awards.
- Pre-push state read and **quoted** before pushing, per the standing change from X-31:
  ```
  remote_tip=a444dc01  local=e1dcac25
  remote_tip_merged_into_main=false  ancestor_of_main=false  fast_forward=true
  verdict=ALLOW — remote tip still carries unmerged content
  ```

## Known gaps

| Gap | Blocker |
| :--- | :--- |
| 7 Guangzhou Bib rows with `address: ''`, 8 with no `nameZh` | `guide.michelin.com` is JS-rendered; restaurant pages **verified** not to fetch |
| CN Shenzhen, 0 of 28 | 15 of 21 Bib aggregated not named; needs a new curated city in `cities.js` + `CITY_IATA` |
| FR Paris, 17/20 two-star and 0/98 one-star | no `instruction/France.js` exists — France is the one country with no source of record |
| JP Tokyo, 121 of 122 one-star | the delisted venue is unidentifiable from fetchable sources |

Unchanged: Green Star beyond HK/Macau; O-219's guard covers "branch already merged", not "PR closed"; hooks are not version-controlled and `--no-verify` bypasses; nothing stops a fabricated report.

title: v0.62.758–760 — the pre-push guard could not tell "no" from "could not ask"; inspect now measures mainRefResolved
body:
Three commits. The headline is the operator-requested fix at the end; the two before it are how the defect was found, kept in the record because the sequence is the point.

## The defect — one boolean meaning two things

Every fact in `inspect()` came through `gitOk`, which returns `false` both when **the answer is no** and when **the question could not be asked**. A missing `origin/main` therefore produced:

```js
remoteTipMergedIntoMain: false
```

— byte-identical to a healthy unmerged branch. The guard then reported *"remote tip still carries unmerged content"*: a claim about a comparison it had never performed.

**The guard was committing the exact fault it exists to prevent.** O-219 was created because a safety check was *asserted* rather than run (X-31); the check built to stop that could not tell whether it had run.

## The fix — three changes, at the source

1. **`inspect` measures the ref.** `mainRefResolved` is its own fact (`git rev-parse --verify ^{commit}`), and both ref-dependent checks are gated on it, so neither can return a value that means two things.
2. **`decide` blocks when blind.** The reason says **"DID NOT RUN"** and **"absence of evidence"**, and deliberately does *not* read as a finding about the branch, because it is not one.
3. **Hook mode fetches first.** `git fetch origin main --quiet` before inspecting, matching what `--check` already did — a stale or never-fetched ref self-heals, so the block is reserved for a ref that genuinely cannot be obtained.

`--check` now prints `main_ref_resolved=` alongside the other facts, so a quoted pre-push read can never again *look* like a performed check when it wasn't.

### Block rather than warn — the case against, and why it still blocks

Blocking is the more obstructive choice, and this guard's own doc warns that *"a guard that forbids [ordinary practice] would be worse than the failure it prevents."* Three things bound the cost:

- a **new branch never reaches the check** (`isNewBranch` short-circuits first — asserted, so the blind-block cannot swallow the one unconditionally safe case);
- hook mode **tries to fix the condition** before refusing;
- the message names both the one-line remedy and `--no-verify`.

A push blocked here means an existing remote branch that might already be merged, inspected by a guard that cannot tell. Passing that quietly is X-31 with the lights off. It is the same principle already applied one function below to an unreadable stdin.

## How it was found — X-35, then X-35b

**X-35.** Restarting the branch from `origin/main` after #1747 merged turned the suite red, in the guard's own test file. The assertion `expect(facts.remoteTipMergedIntoMain).toBe(false)` assumed the branch *always* carries unmerged work; restarted from main it is content-identical, so the flag is `true`. It would have failed after **every merge**, and failed on the first one after it shipped.

**X-35b.** The X-35 fix was then green in CI **for the wrong reason.** CI uses `actions/checkout@v5` at the default `fetch-depth: 1` — shallow, detached, no `origin/main` — so the test took the "unmerged" path and asserted `false === false` against a ref that does not exist. Green, and asserting nothing. That is X-32's silent skip wearing a passing badge, and it shipped *inside the commit whose subject was environment-dependent tests*.

The operator's instruction — ***"fix inspect properly to report mainRefResolved"*** — closed it at the source instead of leaving the test to compensate for a function that was still wrong.

## Tests: 13 → 18

| Added | What fails if it regresses |
| :--- | :--- |
| blind decision blocks | the guard silently no-ops on a missing ref |
| its reason lacks the unmerged phrasing | the guard describes a check it did not run |
| new branch + no main ref still allowed | a first push from a fresh clone gets refused |
| state table: two blocks in six states | a new blocking state slips in unnoticed |
| the permissive default asserted | a caller silently un-guards by omitting a field |
| **the blind case driven through the real hook** | the path unit tests never reach — where the first implementation shipped inert |

The live-repo test now *asks* for `mainRefResolved` instead of inferring it from a value that meant two things.

## Verification

**The first attempt was worthless and nearly went unnoticed.** Cloning the repo tested the **committed** files — it ran 13 tests, not 18, and proved nothing about the change. Caught on the test count. Redone by copying the working tree into a fresh repo with no `origin` remote:

```
origin/main present?   absent — CI shape reproduced
vitest prepush-guard   17 passed | 1 skipped (18)
live-repo test path    mainRefResolved=false  verdict=block
reason                 "…the merged-by-content check DID NOT RUN…"
```

Those last two lines are the point: in the environment where the test previously asserted nothing, it now takes the block path and says so.

- Working repo: **18/18**; full suite **183 files / 4,340 tests** green.
- CI on `88a4ac4d`: all four checks green; the Vitest job log reports `4339 passed | 1 skipped (4340)` — the same split as the reproduced blind repo, which corroborates the shallow shape. The log does not print which branch the live-repo test took, so the direct evidence for the block path is the local reproduction, not this.

## Also here — #1747's merge record, `[AMD-36]`

#1747 squash-merged as `e3af4473`. **Verified by content, not by the webhook** (D-123 / D-199) — five reads on `origin/main`: version `0.62.757` (not `.756`), `AMD-35` present, `O-220` present, `CN-michelin.js` at 483 rows, three sampled new Bib ids present. This is the check **X-33** exists for: the identical notification arrived for #1746 while `[AMD-30]` was *not* in the merged tree.

The branch was **restarted** from `origin/main`, not continued — stacking on already-merged history is the door X-31 and X-33 both came through. **O-221** makes D-205's second condition explicit: a record folded forward into a PR that never arrives is a record that was dropped. This PR is that arrival, so it clears on merge.

## Known gaps

`[AMD-37]`'s stated gap is closed by `[AMD-38]`. Unchanged: the guard still detects *"merged by content"*, not *"the PR is closed"* (X-33's limit); hooks are not version-controlled; `--no-verify` bypasses; nothing stops a fabricated report. On data: the 7 pinned Guangzhou addresses (O-220); CN Shenzhen 0 of 28; FR Paris with no source of record; JP Tokyo 121 of 122.

title: v0.62.762 — Shenzhen debuts at 13 of 28 with the stars complete; the Register's 84-item placeholder is expanded
body:
Everything in one PR, as asked.

## First, the fair criticism

> *"are you repairing in 'circles'? i thought the Gia Telegram is working?"*

Checked rather than conceded. Of the last eight PRs to `main`, **seven were tooling, docs or data-integrity** — the pre-push guard, the deploy prompt, the serial base, a duplicate script, three merge records. Only #1747 touched product data. **Nothing shipped today fixed anything a bot user could see**, because nothing was broken for them. The X-35 → X-35b → `mainRefResolved` chain was three commits on one guard; each step found a real defect and the last was requested by name, but the shape is exactly what was called out.

This PR is the redirect taken.

## Shenzhen: 0 → 13 of 28, stars complete

| Tier | Have | Published | Names |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| two-star | **2** | 2 | The Bay by Chef Fei · Yun Jing |
| one-star | **5** | 5 | Chao Shang Chao · Ensue · Fumée · Opus 388 · Xin Rong Ji |
| Bib Gourmand | **6** | 21 | the release names six individually and aggregates the rest by cuisine style |

**The stars are complete, 7 of 7.** The 15 unnamed Bib are not invented.

### The blocker was never what the Register said

The gap read *"needs a new curated city in `cities.js` + `CITY_IATA`."* **Both were already there** — `web/cuisine/src/v2/lib/cities.js` carries `Shenzhen / SZX / Guangdong`, and `CITY_IATA` carries `'shenzhen': 'SZX'`. No scaffolding was ever missing. The blocker was **names**, and a stale note made it look structural for a week. The old note is corrected in place in `KNOWN_DELTAS`, not quietly dropped.

## The near-miss worth reviewing — a silent reorder, caught by an assertion

The first insert script sorted each tier block by id, assuming that is the file's order. An assertion written into the same script fired:

```
Error: CN-michelin.js: existing order breaks tier/city/id
       at cn-bjs-mo-jasmine -> cn-bjs-mansion-cuisine-by-jingyan
```

The tables group by **tier → city**, but **within** a city they follow the source of record's own order — neither id- nor name-alphabetical. Sorting would have **reshuffled hundreds of rows**, passed every test (row count, parity, manifests all unchanged), and read wrong to anyone diffing against `instruction/China.js`.

Rewritten to splice the new rows in as three new `(tier, city)` blocks, touching nothing existing. **The diff is 13 insertions, 0 deletions per file.**

Worth stating plainly: yesterday's Guangzhou insert used that same id-sort. It was harmless only because that particular Bib run *happened* to be in id order — which its 8-insertion / 1-deletion diff confirms. Harmless by luck is not harmless by design.

## Addresses — applied per row, not waived for the batch

**4 of 13** got a real address (the hotel restaurants, which the press covers in detail); **9 did not**. The pinned debt goes **7 → 16** in `__tests__/michelin-city-manifest.test.js`, and the split is recorded in the list itself so it reads as a per-row judgement rather than a blanket exemption. All 13 also lack `nameZh`/`addressZh`, so `NO_ZH` grows **8 → 21**. Both lists are pinned by id: an unlisted address-less row fails the suite, and a pinned row that *gains* an address fails until it is un-pinned.

## The Register — expanding the placeholder changed the count

*"All prior open items. Unchanged."* covered **84 ids behind one line**, carried forward without inspection. Each is now restored from the newest register file that carries it, with that filename in the row so the claim is checkable.

Two findings:

- **O-117 and O-123 were never open** — closed by C-123 and C-133. The range in the placeholder was simply wrong.
- **11 more read as resolved in their own text** while being counted as open (*"Closed by C-154 + C-155"*, *"Dropped."*, *"dont change"*, *"Structurally closed"*).

**Real total: 71 open, 13 resolved** — not 84 open. The 13 are struck through, because leaving them unstruck is the *identical* defect to O-192/193/194, which I was asked to strike in the same breath.

## Manifest delta

| | Before | After |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| CN 2026 two-star | 25 | **27** |
| CN 2026 one-star | 121 | **126** |
| CN 2026 bib-gourmand | 334 | **340** |
| CN 2026 total | 483 | **496** |
| `CITY_MANIFEST` Shenzhen 2026 | — | **2 / 5 / 6** |
| Pinned address debt | 7 | **16** |

`KNOWN_DELTAS` now reads: `JP/Tokyo 121/122 · FR/Paris 17/20 · FR/Paris 0/98 · CN/Shenzhen 6/21`.

## Also carries `[AMD-39]` — #1748's merge record

Folded forward per D-205, which **closes O-222**. That is the rule working as intended: the record ships with substantive work rather than as a PR of its own.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **183 files / 4,341 tests**, green.
- Diff on both data files: **13 insertions, 0 deletions** — nothing reordered.
- Pre-push state read and quoted, per X-31:
  ```
  remote_tip=18be0bfd  local=a3819f82
  main_ref_resolved=true
  remote_tip_merged_into_main=false  ancestor_of_main=false  fast_forward=true
  verdict=ALLOW — remote tip still carries unmerged content
  ```

## Known gaps — and one is now blocked on a decision, not on data

| Gap | Blocker |
| :--- | :--- |
| CN Shenzhen Bib, 6 of 21 | the release aggregates 15 by cuisine style; `guide.michelin.com` is JS-rendered and does not fetch |
| **VN Green Star, 0 of 3** | **names are known** — Nén Danang, Lamai Garden, Tales by Chapter — but **none holds a star or Bib**, and the schema requires `awards.length ≥ 1`. This is **O-163** (*"MICHELIN Selected has no home in this schema"*) blocking a different item. Needs a schema call; not worked around silently |
| FR Paris, 17/20 two-star and 0/98 one-star | no `instruction/France.js` exists at all — France is the one country with no source of record |

Plus the 9 new address-less rows and 13 without Chinese names, both pinned.

title: v0.62.764 — a Green Star can stand alone; Vietnam's three holders are in
body:
The schema change asked for by name, plus `[AMD-41]` folded forward (closing O-223).

## The blocker was the schema, not the research

`validateVenue` required `awards.length >= 1`. Vietnam's three 2026 Green Star holders — **Nén Danang**, **Lamai Garden**, **Tales by Chapter** — hold no star and no Bib, so there was **no legal row** for them. Their names had been known since `[AMD-40]`; the gap sat open as *"needs a schema decision"* rather than as missing data.

## Narrowed, not dropped

> `awards` may be empty **only** on a Green Star holder.

An award-less venue with **no** Green Star still throws, because that is a row with no reason to exist — which is the check the old rule was really making. This is the same treatment the empty-address invariant got: rewrite it tighter rather than let it quietly stop being true.

Three assertions, so the remaining rule can't rot into nothing:

| Case | Expected |
| :--- | :--- |
| `awards: []`, no Green Star | **throws** — `may only be empty on a Green Star holder` |
| `awards: []`, `greenStarYears: [2026]` | **accepted** |
| `awards: null`, Green Star present | **throws** — `"awards" must be an array` |

The third exists because narrowing a rule is exactly when you widen the type check by accident.

## Two functions, two questions — deliberately not merged

`editionVenues(Y)` now returns award holders **∪** Green Star holders, deduped: a Green Star is part of what the guide published, so a venue holding only one belongs to the edition.

`venuesForYear(Y)` **deliberately does not widen.** It is documented as *"holding an **award** in year Y"*, and **every manifest count derives from it** — merging the two would silently move numbers that other assertions depend on. Asserted explicitly:

```
VN editionVenues(2026)   86
VN venuesForYear(2026)   83
union duplicate ids       0
```

## The trap I found while building it, and closed

A Green-Star-only venue produces **no flat rows** — the flat contract is one row per award, and a Green Star is not one. Injecting a `category: 'green-star'` pseudo-tier would reach every consumer that switches on `category`, so it stays out.

But that leaves a trap: such a venue still marks its city *populated*, so **`hasMichelinData(city)` could answer `true` for a city whose flat getters return nothing at all.**

Rather than document it and move on, it now **fails closed at load**: every Green-Star-only venue must sit in a city that also holds a real award. All three do today (Hanoi, Da Nang, Ho Chi Minh City), so it costs nothing now and fires the day it would start lying.

## Data — no new provenance debt

All three addresses were **found**, so the pinned address debt stays at **16**. Added to **both** `VN-michelin.js` and `instruction/Vietnam.js` (the parity gate requires both).

| | Before | After |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| VN venues | 83 | **86** |
| VN 2026 award-holders | 83 | **83** *(unchanged — the point)* |
| VN `sum(awards)` | 92 | **92** *(unchanged)* |
| `COUNTRY_MANIFEST` VN 2026 | — | **`'green-star': 3`** |
| Green Stars dataset-wide | 5 | **8** (VN 3, HK 4, MO 1) |

`'green-star'` is asserted separately and **excluded from `total`**, because `total` counts award rows and these venues have none. That is why venues and award-holders diverge here for the first time — and both are asserted separately so the divergence reads as deliberate rather than as a number bumped to make the suite pass.

## O-163 is narrowed, **not** closed

O-163 reads *"MICHELIN Selected tier has no home in this schema."* Half of what it blocked is now unblocked. **Selected itself is still unmodelled**, deliberately: Shenzhen alone has 31 Selected venues, and adding the tier is a **product** decision — does a Selected venue appear in the bot's Michelin list, and with what badge? — not a schema one. Marking O-163 closed here would have claimed a decision nobody made.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **183 files / 4,345 tests**, green (was 4,341; +4).
- `node --check` clean.
- Measured after: `VN venues 86`, `VN 2026 award-holders 83`, `edition 2026 VN 86`, `greenStarVenues(2026)` = 8.
- Pre-push state read and quoted, per X-31:
  ```
  remote_tip=b4cd1dbe  local=7696a83c
  main_ref_resolved=true
  remote_tip_merged_into_main=false  ancestor_of_main=false  fast_forward=true
  verdict=ALLOW — remote tip still carries unmerged content
  ```

## Known gaps

VN Green Star drops off the list. What replaces it is narrower and worth stating: the three venues are in the dataset, asserted and queryable, but **do not appear in the flat/search surface** — that needs a rendering decision, which is O-163's remaining half.

| Gap | Blocker |
| :--- | :--- |
| Green Star holders invisible to the flat/search surface | needs a rendering decision (O-163's remaining half) |
| CN Shenzhen Bib, 6 of 21 | the release aggregates 15 by cuisine style; `guide.michelin.com` does not fetch |
| FR Paris, 17/20 two-star and 0/98 one-star | no `instruction/France.js` exists |
| JP Tokyo, 121 of 122 one-star | the delisted venue is unidentifiable from fetchable sources |

Plus 16 pinned address-less rows and 21 without Chinese names.

title: v0.62.766 — the Green Star reaches the flat and search surfaces; O-163 closes
body:
O-163's remaining half — the rendering decision the last two PRs declined to make unasked. Also carries `[AMD-43]` forward, closing O-224.

## The failure was silent, which is the point

`[AMD-42]` shipped three Green Star venues that loaded, passed every assertion, and rendered **nowhere**. Measured on the live search path's own mapping before touching anything:

```
in visitableVenues        true
retainedAwardYears        []
latestMichCat             null
passes the year matcher   0 of 1
```

Nothing threw. Nothing logged. The venue was in the dataset and invisible. `[AMD-42]` had *named* this as a limit — naming a limit is not covering it.

## The shape, chosen so it doesn't re-open the objection it was designed around

The schema note rejected `green-star` as an `awards[]` category because a **starred** holder would then emit two flat rows and appear twice in `michelinForCity` / `getAll`. That objection is about venues holding **both**, and it still stands. So the rule splits:

| Venue | Flat rows |
| :--- | :--- |
| holds awards | one per award, **unchanged**, plus `greenStar: true` on the years the Green Star covers — **no extra row** |
| holds only a Green Star | one per Green Star year, `category: 'green-star'` — its tier slot was empty, so nothing is displaced |

Asserted directly against **Amber** (three-star '25 + '26, Green Star '26): **2 rows**, both `three-star`, flag on **'26 only**.

`greenStar` is a **boolean on every flat row, never undefined**, so a consumer can test it without knowing which branch produced the row.

## The search path is not the flat view

Worth flagging for review because I assumed otherwise at first: the bot's Michelin path maps `visitableVenues()` directly and **never reads `getAll`** for non-SG countries. **Fixing `_venueToFlatRows` alone would have shipped nothing a user sees.**

Both are fixed:
- `latestMichCat` falls back to `'green-star'`;
- a new `retainedGreenStarYears(venue)` returns `["'26"]`-style tokens, so the **year ticks keep working**.

Verified both directions — 3 of 3 survive with no ticks off, **0 of 3** with `'26` switched off. A Green Star is year-gated like any award, which is correct: it can be lost between editions.

## Render

`ResultCard.jsx` gains `'green-star': '🌱 Michelin Green Star'`, plus a `· 🌱` suffix on tiered holders — **the tier never moves aside**, so Amber stays `⭐⭐⭐` and gains a leaf. The clipboard `VenueCard.jsx` map is kept in step, and `ResultPanel.jsx` forwards the flag: without that the leaf shows on screen and vanishes from the copied card, which is the worst of both.

The badge choice is mine and easily changed — flagging it rather than burying it.

## Two decisions made explicit rather than left to a fallback

- **`MICHELIN_RANK` gains `'green-star': 0`.** Behaviour is *identical* to the `?? 0` it already fell through to. The point is that sorting below Bib is now a decision on the page instead of an accident of a missing key that reads like an oversight.
- **The response summary gains a `greenStar` count that deliberately overlaps** the four tier counts. A Green Star is parallel, so a summary that subtracted it from a tier would misreport both.

## One changed assertion, flagged

`michelin-green-star.test.js`'s no-double-listing test used to read `rows.length === awards2026` for *every* holder — right while a Green Star couldn't stand alone, and it agreed with an award-less venue being invisible. It now branches. **The comment in the file says the design changed, not that the test was made to pass**, and the guarantee it was protecting (a holder with awards gains no extra row) is still asserted.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **184 files / 4,357 tests**, green (was 183 / 4,345); `michelin-green-star-surface.test.js` is new with 12.
- `node --check` clean on `index.js`, `michelin-data.js`, `michelin-sort.js`.

title: v0.62.768 — Shenzhen's Bib closes at 21/21; China reconciles against every published 2026 figure
body:
The last CN gap, open at 6 of 21 since `[AMD-40]`. Also carries `[AMD-45]` forward, closing O-225.

## The blocker broke, and it broke in Chinese

`[AMD-40]` recorded the gap as *"the release aggregates 15 by cuisine style."* That was true of the **English** release, and of every English-language source I had tried — and I had generalised it to *"not fetchable."*

Searching in **Chinese** found a named outlet's enumerated list, all 21 by district (Sing Tao Headline, 深圳米芝蓮2026「平價名單」). Four Chinese-language articles named only the same six; the fifth had the lot.

Worth flagging as method rather than luck: **"not fetchable" had only ever been measured against one language.**

## Why the 15 were accepted

A single secondary source, so the reasoning is written into `michelin-city-manifest.js` where it can be re-judged rather than trusted:

- all **six** officially-named venues appear in it, unchanged;
- its district spread (Futian, Nanshan, Luohu, Longhua, Yantian) and cuisine mix match the official release's own description;
- it totals **exactly 21**, the published figure;
- one entry (卖鱼佬砂锅粥) was independently corroborated in a separate search result.

## One thing does not reconcile — and is not smoothed over

The official release lists **Indonesian** among the Bib cuisine styles. **No venue in the enumerated list reads as Indonesian.** Either the release describes the whole Shenzhen selection rather than the Bib tier, or one of the 21 carries a misattributed cuisine.

The count is unaffected — 21 names for 21 slots — but one cuisine label is probably wrong. Opened as **O-226** rather than discovered later as a surprise.

A smaller conflict: two sources disagree on one Chinese name — 新湖村**促**肉 (guokr) vs 新湖村**腊**肉 (Sing Tao). That row's `nameZh` is **deliberately left unset**. Guessing between them would look identical to knowing.

## The pinned-debt mechanism proved itself

The source carried addresses for two venues **already in the table**. The suite went red on the assertion written for exactly this:

```
FAIL  the debt shrinks only downward — filling an address needs this list edited
```

`cn-szx-jie-yang-lao-er-guo-tiao-tang` and `cn-szx-xiao-long-niu-rou-mian-futian` gained real addresses and were still pinned. That is the test doing its job, not a nuisance to route around — un-pinning was the required follow-through.

The debt moved in **both directions**: **out** by 2, **in** by 13, net **16 → 27**.

## Data delta

| | Before | After |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| Shenzhen Bib Gourmand | 6 | **21** |
| Shenzhen total awards | 13 | **28 of 28 — complete** |
| `COUNTRY_MANIFEST` CN 2026 bib | 340 | **355** |
| `COUNTRY_MANIFEST` CN 2026 total | 496 | **511** |
| Dataset venues | 2,001 | **2,016** |
| Pinned address debt | 16 | **27** |

`KNOWN_DELTAS` now reads `JP/Tokyo · FR/Paris · FR/Paris` — **no CN entry remains**. The reasoning above is kept as a comment in Shenzhen's place, as Guangzhou's was.

## Enrichment is additive only

The 6 existing rows were edited **in place** to gain `nameZh` (and `addressZh` for the two). New for this arc, so the script is defensive: it refuses to overwrite a non-empty address or a row that already has a `nameZh`. Enrichment can only add.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **184 files / 4,357 tests**, green.
- `node --check` clean on `CN-michelin.js`, `michelin-data.js`, `michelin-city-manifest.js`.
- Measured after: Shenzhen **28** venues, dataset **2,016** venues, **27** empty addresses.
