title: v0.62.770–771 — Paris and Tokyo close; KNOWN_DELTAS is empty for the first time
body:
Two commits. Paris (0 of 98 one-stars) and Tokyo (121 of 122) were the last two published-figure deltas in the dataset. Both close here, and the list they were on is now **empty**.

Also carries `[AMD-47]` forward, closing O-227.

---

# Tokyo — the note prescribed the wrong fix

This is the part worth reviewing. The `KNOWN_DELTAS` entry had been **corrected twice already** and still ended with a wrong instruction:

> *"Fix: one curated row with `status: 'closed'` and a 2026 one-star award."*

It reasoned by analogy from SÉZANNE and Pierre Gagnaire — both hand-entered as *"delisted, not in live index"* — and concluded the 122nd venue must be another delisting.

**It is not.** The missing venue is **氣分 (Kibun)**, Nishiazabu, Minato, and it is **open** — live MICHELIN Guide page, online booking. Never a delisting; an **omission** from the curation pass.

Had the prescribed fix been applied, the count would have reconciled at 122 and `visitableVenues()` — which drops `status:'closed'` and backs **every user-facing path** — would have gone on hiding an operating one-star. **The gate would have gone green while the product got quietly worse.**

A note that names a fix is not a note that diagnosed the cause. This one had only ever seen the symptom.

## How it was found

Search in the local language — third time now (Shenzhen, Paris, Tokyo), deliberate rather than stumbled into. A Japanese aggregator enumerates all 122 by ward, and its ward subtotals sum to 122 independently: `9 + 31 + 49 + 9 + 2 + 7 + 1 + 14`.

The first fetch returned only **119** names — Minato's header said 49 but listed 46. That was visible **only because the subtotals were checked against the running numbering**. A second fetch scoped to Minato produced the missing three — Daigo, EWIG, Alchimiste — **all already in the repo**. The shortfall was the summariser's, not the source's.

## The diff needed care

**19** names on the page absent from the repo, **21** in the repo absent from the page — which reads like wholesale disagreement and is almost entirely **romanisation**:

| Page | Repo |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Beige Alain Ducasse Tokyo` | `BEIGE Alain Ducasse` |
| `marge` | `mærge` |
| `Tenma` (天雅) | `TEN-MASA` |
| `Oniku Hanaryu` (花柳) | `Oniku Karyu` |
| `Nihonbashi Soba no Ji` | `Nihombashi Sonoji` |
| …and fourteen more | |

Under an accent- and case-insensitive normaliser, **exactly one name on each side had no partner**: `Kibun`. `121 + Kibun = 122`.

**Name chosen on evidence:** the aggregator writes *Kiibun*; MICHELIN's own guide URL is `/restaurant/kibun`. Slugs strip characters but don't delete them, so `kibun` is evidence MICHELIN writes **Kibun**. `nameJa: '氣分'` carries the authoritative form regardless.

## An empty list needed a new kind of assertion

`KNOWN_DELTAS` can reach `[]` two ways: **the data reconciles**, or **someone deletes rows from the list**. Those look identical from the test. So both are asserted — the array is empty **and** the computed set (built by walking every published figure against the repo) is empty. Without the second line the test would pass on a truncated array.

---

# Paris — I had it blocked for the wrong reason too

`[AMD-47]` called Paris *"blocked on **building a source file** rather than on finding data."* Wrong. `FR-michelin.js`'s v1 header deferred one-stars because *"guide.michelin.com list pages return HTTP 403."* **Still true** — what changed is searching **in French**.

Four checks on the enumerated 127, one the source didn't intend:

- totals **9 + 20 + 98**, matching published exactly;
- its 3- and 2-star sections agree **row-for-row** with what was already curated — the three missing two-stars were Le Meurice Alain Ducasse, Sushi Yoshinaga, Table; nothing present was contradicted;
- its **per-arrondissement subtotals sum to 98** independently of its own 1–98 numbering;
- an **independent** outlet's eleven new 2026 one-stars are fully contained in it.

Three source typos corrected and named: `Augsute` → **Auguste**, `II Carpaccio` → **Il Carpaccio**, `Constrate` → **Contraste**.

## What the Paris rows do NOT have

**No `address`, no `cuisine`.** The arrondissement is recorded as `postal` (750NN) — a derivation, not a guess.

- The missing address is **not load-bearing**: `index.js` resolves by `name + city` through Places and renders `placesData?.formattedAddress || entry.address`. **Checked before deciding.**
- The missing cuisine **is** a real loss: `availableCuisines('FR')` still returns 3 slugs, so these 101 venues are absent from cuisine-filtered searches. Opened as **O-228**.

## The debt list split, and the split is asserted

| List | Rows | What "no address" means |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| `ADDRESS_DEBT` | 27 (CN) | street not findable; **no postal either** |
| `ADDRESS_DEBT_FR` | 101 | arrondissement precision; **every row carries a postal** |

Every FR row must match `/^750\d{2}$/`; **no CN row may have a postal**. The same phrase can't quietly mean two things.

**FR stays out of the parity gate, deliberately.** Manufacturing an `instruction/France.js` from the same input used to build the table would make it compare a file with its own copy. A gate that cannot fail is worse than a missing one — it reads like coverage.

---

## Result

| | Before | After |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| FR venues | 29 | **130** |
| Paris 2026 | 9 / 17 / 0 | **9 / 20 / 98 = 127** |
| JP venues | 589 | **590** |
| Tokyo 2026 one-star | 121 | **122** |
| Dataset venues | 2,016 | **2,118** |
| Pinned address debt | 27 | **128** (101 with a postal) |
| **`KNOWN_DELTAS`** | **3 entries** | **0 — empty** |

**No published-figure delta remains anywhere in the dataset.**

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **184 files / 4,361 tests**, green (was 4,357; +4).
- `node --check` clean on every changed `.js`.
- Measured after: `KNOWN_DELTAS: 0 entries`, dataset **2,118**, JP **590**, Tokyo one-star **122**, Kibun `status: open` and present in `visitableVenues()`.
- The manifest gate fired first on the Tokyo insert, as designed: `expected 278, got 279`.
- Pre-push state read and quoted, per X-31:
  ```
  remote_tip=52b04a16  local=3c9dd470
  main_ref_resolved=true
  remote_tip_merged_into_main=false  ancestor_of_main=false  fast_forward=true
  verdict=ALLOW — remote tip still carries unmerged content
  ```

## Known gaps

Everything outstanding is now a **field** gap, not a **row** gap:

| Gap | Item |
| :--- | :--- |
| 128 rows with `address: ''` (101 carrying a postal) | pinned in two asserted lists |
| 101 FR rows with no `cuisine` | O-228 |
| 32 CN rows without full Chinese fields | — |
| one Shenzhen Bib cuisine probably mislabelled | O-226 |

title: v0.62.773–776 — the i18n gate and the hole Codex found in it; O-185: the admin gate failed OPEN
body:
Two commits. Also carries `[AMD-50]` forward, closing O-229.

> **⚠️ Before merging, please check one thing:** is `TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID` set on Railway? If it is **unset**, this change locks admin commands for **you too** until you set it. I could not read the variable from this session — the Railway MCP was disconnected — so it is recorded as **unknown**, not assumed. Details below.

---

# O-185 — the admin gate failed OPEN

Four lines in `index.js`:

```js
const owner = process.env.TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID;
if (!owner) return true;                 // <-- fails OPEN
return String(chatId) === String(owner);
```

It guards **17 call sites** — `/cost`, `/ver`, `/log`, the Recount commands, and `/api/oversight/stats`, which returns a **403** and is the only one reachable **without Telegram**. With the variable unset, every one of them answered **yes to every user**.

The existing comment called this *"deliberate for local dev"*, and for local dev it is. But a convenience whose failure mode is *"admin opens to everyone"* is not a convenience — it's a **default**, and defaults are what production runs on.

## The fix is an inversion, not a tightening

| `TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID` | `GIA_ALLOW_UNOWNED_ADMIN` | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| set | — | exact match, **unchanged** |
| unset | `'1'` | open (local dev) |
| unset | anything else, or absent | **CLOSED** |

### Why not `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` — the fix that would have *looked* like one

That was my first idea. It only holds if something actually sets `NODE_ENV=production` on the host, and **nothing in this repo guarantees Railway does**. A gate hung on it would pass review, read as fixed, and leave the hole exactly where it was. An explicit opt-in can't fail that way, because production never sets it.

### The opt-in is `=== '1'`, not truthy

A truthy check would make `GIA_ALLOW_UNOWNED_ADMIN=false` **open** the gate — the same bug reappearing one level down. Asserted against `'0'`, `'false'`, `'true'`, `'yes'`, `''`, `' '`, `'on'`, `undefined`, `null`.

## My own tests caught two things I had wrong

Both were written as assertions *before* they were known to be true — the only reason they fired:

1. **A second copy that wasn't a copy.** The "old line is gone" test matched `const owner = process.env.TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID;` — in **`spendGuardTick`**, which reads the same variable to decide *who to DM*. That use is correct (`if (!owner) return;` = "nobody to tell") and deleting it would have broken spend alerts. The fail-open signature is the **return value**, not the variable read, so the assertion was narrowed — and `spendGuardTick` is now **pinned** so a future cleanup can't take it out.
2. **The count was wrong.** The Register said *"20 call sites"*; my first assertion said 20. It is **17**. Caught before it shipped in a security note, which is where a wrong number does real damage.

Also corrected: the comment above the function still read *"When the env var is unset /ver stays open so the bot still self-reports for any caller."* That described the behaviour accurately, and that behaviour **was** the bug. Corrected in place rather than deleted.

## What this does not fix

**O-184 stays open.** Verbose sessions started by non-owners before the earlier fix still hold a `verbose:` key until its 24 h TTL; this change doesn't revoke them. Separate item.

There is also no `.env.example` or README documenting either variable, so the new opt-in is discoverable only from `owner-gate.js` itself.

---

# v0.62.773 — the translation pipeline was already finished

The Register said *"`i18n.js` is still **0 / 276** keys translated"* and *"**120 damaged items** unrepaired."* Measured:

| | |
| :--- | ---: |
| keys | **276** |
| differ in all 7 non-EN locales | **242** |
| identical in ≥1 locale | **34** |
| meaning-fixes applied | **402 / 402** |
| `privacy.body` / `legal.body` | translated in **all 8** |

Not stale — **inverted**. What was missing was a **gate**: nothing stopped any of it regressing, which is how the entry stayed four versions out of date without anything contradicting it.

All **165** identical *(key, locale)* pairs are pinned individually with a reason — `endonym` (56), `confirms-in-target` (56), `format-only` (33), `cognate` (13), `proper-noun` (7). **Zero unclassified.** A category rule like *"`language.btn.*` is exempt"* would silently absorb a future key that genuinely needed translating.

Both directions asserted, plus **placeholder drift** across 87 keys / 609 comparisons — a translation that renames `{dist}` renders the literal token and looks fine in review.

### And I nearly re-opened something you'd closed

The audit corpus (1,590 items, no verdicts) needs a paid key, so I drafted a Register item — then found **O-196**, the same thing, which you **dropped on 24-08** as moot. A successor would have quietly reversed that ruling under a new number. **Withdrawn before shipping.** It surfaced only because a routine secret scan matched `I18N_TRANSLATE_TOKEN` in that row's prose — **the catch was luck, not process.**

The corpus is instead pinned with no new item: 36 files, 1,590 items, and an assertion that **no item carries a verdict**, so a future run fails the suite and forces the record to update in the same change.

---

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **186 files / 4,382 tests**, green (was 184 / 4,361; +21).
- `node --check` clean on `index.js` and `owner-gate.js`.
- `owner-gate` truth table exercised directly: owner-match, mismatch, unowned-closed, unowned-open-by-opt-in, blank-owner-as-unset, and `undefined` chatId refused **even with the opt-in on** (that's `req.tg?.user?.id` when initData carries no user).
- Pre-push state read and quoted, per X-31:
  ```
  remote_tip=b6dfd28d  local=f0144b96
  main_ref_resolved=true
  remote_tip_merged_into_main=false  ancestor_of_main=false  fast_forward=true
  verdict=ALLOW — remote tip still carries unmerged content
  ```

`owner-gate.js` is new and pure — `decideOwner({chatId, owner, optIn})` → `{allow, reason}`. The `reason` exists so a refusal is diagnosable rather than a silent 403. `index.js` delegates; **no call site changed**.

title: v0.62.777 — the translation gap was rendering, not writing: ~5,300 strings never reached a reader
body:
You asked *"continue with the translation. have you finish"*. My previous answer — that translation was complete — was **right about the Mini App string tables and wrong about everything downstream of them.**

Also carries `[AMD-55]`, #1754's merge record, folded forward per D-205.

---

## The headline: zh, ja and es were translated and then thrown away at render

`web/cuisine/src/v2/lib/fun-facts.js` had:

```js
const OVERLAY_LANGS = new Set(['id', 'ru', 'de']);
```

while **both** overlays already carried six languages — the fun-facts overlay has `de/es/id/ja/ru/zh`, the dish-note overlay has `id/ru/de/zh/ja/es`. `factBody` branched on that set and could only ever read **one** of the two sources:

| language | in `OVERLAY_LANGS`? | what it read | result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| id, ru, de | yes | `_i18n[lang]` | translated ✅ |
| **zh, ja** | no | flat `fact[lang]` — which **does not exist** for dish facts | **English** ❌ |
| **es** | no, and not in `SUPPORTED_LANGS` either | `deviceFactLang()` never even returned `es` | **English** ❌ |

Roughly **5,300 written strings** (1,685 dish rows + 72 fact rows, × zh/ja/es) that no user could reach. Now resolved **curated flat key → generated overlay → English**, for every language.

### Precedence — I had it backwards, and a fixture caught it

My first draft read the overlay *before* the curated flat key, so a machine draft beat a hand-authored Japanese body. `nation-overlay.js` already states the rule for dish notes — *"hand-authored notes ALWAYS win"* — and the `ramen` fixture failed immediately. Pinned in both directions now.

### A comment that claimed coverage it did not have

> `// the global facts carry zh/ms/ta/ja/ko/th too`

Measured: **8 of 72** carry those, and **none** carries `es`. Corrected in place rather than deleted.

---

## The smaller, real gap: 28 dish notes with no translation row

`nation-overlay-dishnotes.generated.js` gained dishes after the last generator run — 1 argentinian, 13 brazilian, 14 french — and the i18n overlay never caught up.

Written **by hand**: `scripts/translate-content.mjs` needs `GEMINI_API_KEY`, and the standing instruction is not to spend on external APIs. Each row carries all six languages, so a future generator run **skips** it (it only fills rows missing a target language) rather than overwriting. The exception is recorded in that file's own header instead of being smuggled past its *"GENERATED, do not hand-edit"* line.

**Base keys with no overlay row: 28 → 0.**

---

## One stale test corrected rather than deleted

It selected an SG fact by `!f.ja` and asserted English. `!f.ja` only means *"no **flat** ja"* — the fact had `_i18n.ja` all along, so the assertion was pinning the discard, not the fallback. There is now **no** fact missing `ja` both ways, so that is asserted directly and the fallback is tested on a constructed fact.

## Verification

- `factBody` run on `french::croissant` across all 8 locales: zh/ja/es returned the English body **before**, return Japanese/Chinese/Spanish **after**.
- `deviceFactLang()` resolves an `es-ES` device to `es`.
- `npx vitest run` — **186 files / 4,390 tests** green (was 4,388; +2), re-run *after* the last edit.
- Cuisine app builds.
- Pre-push state read and quoted, per X-31:
  ```
  remote_tip=74da63c8  local=35fd3a71
  main_ref_resolved=true
  remote_tip_merged_into_main=false  ancestor_of_main=false  fast_forward=true
  verdict=ALLOW — remote tip still carries unmerged content
  ```

## What is still open, and it is large

**French.** `TARGET_LANGS` in `translate-content.mjs` is `['id','ru','de','zh','ja','es']` — **no `fr`**. Of 1,681 merged dish notes only **32** carry `note.fr`, and `dishFactsFromPlate` sets `fr: ${name} — ${note.fr || note.en}`. So **1,649 dish notes render English to French readers** while six other languages read their own.

Two further corpora have **no translation overlay at all**:

| corpus | rows | locales held | short by |
| :--- | ---: | :--- | ---: |
| `classics-notes.js` | 1,677 | en + fr | 10,062 |
| `city-plates.js` history | 279 | en + fr | 1,674 |

Not started — the scope is yours to set.

title: v0.62.778 — O-306: French, the one locale the dish notes skipped (1,653 notes, by hand)
body:
**O-306 closed.** 1,681 dish notes now carry all 8 locales; before this, **1,649 of them rendered English to French readers** while six other languages read their own.

Also carries `[AMD-57]` (#1755's merge record) and the **O-305 … O-309** Register rows, both held per D-205 and folded forward.

---

## The root cause was one missing list entry

```js
const TARGET_LANGS = ['id', 'ru', 'de', 'zh', 'ja', 'es'];   // no 'fr'
```

`scripts/translate-content.mjs` has skipped French **since the day it was written**. So the overlay filled six languages, and `dishFactsFromPlate` fell back with `fr: ${name} — ${note.fr || note.en}` — English, for the product's own second language, the one every Mini App has shipped from the start.

`'fr'` is now in that list, so newly added dishes cannot reopen the hole. That fix is one line; the other 1,653 were the work.

## 1,653 French notes, written by hand

`translate-content.mjs` needs `GEMINI_API_KEY` and the standing rule is **no external-API spend**, so these were written rather than generated. **No external API was called.**

They go into `nation-overlay-dishnotes-i18n.generated.js`. `nation-overlay.js` merges any language an overlay row carries, and a hand-authored `note.fr` still wins, so **no product code changed for the data itself**.

| | before | after |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| merged dish notes | 1,681 | 1,681 |
| carrying `fr` | **32** | **1,681** |
| rows short of 8 locales | 1,649 | **0** |

## The gate that should have existed

`__tests__/dish-notes-i18n.test.js` is new. I checked first rather than assuming: **nothing had ever asserted anything** about the largest body of user-facing prose in the repo.

It reads the **merged** table via `nation-overlay.js`, because reading either file alone understates or overstates coverage — which is exactly how this stayed invisible **twice this month** (v0.62.777's 28 missing rows, and this).

Three directions, and **proved by mutation rather than by a green tick**: I deleted the `fr` line from `french::croissant` and removed `'fr'` from `TARGET_LANGS`, and **all three assertions failed**. Both restored, re-run green.

The third assertion is the one a data check can't do: the corpus can be complete today while the *generator* still omits a language, so the next batch of dishes reopens the hole.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **187 files / 4,393 tests** green (was 186 / 4,390), re-run *after* the last edit.
- Cuisine app builds.
- Across the 1,653 new strings: no placeholder drift, no stray markup or newlines, no suspiciously short value.
- Pre-push state read and quoted, per X-31:
  ```
  remote_tip=a254abc9  local=b5e6cc38
  main_ref_resolved=true
  remote_tip_merged_into_main=false  ancestor_of_main=false  fast_forward=true
  verdict=ALLOW — remote tip still carries unmerged content
  ```

## Stated plainly rather than buried

**The French is mine and unreviewed by a native speaker.** It is consistent in register and preserves every proper noun and dish name, but 1,653 strings written in one pass by one author is a volume no review saw. **The gate protects coverage, not quality.** If you want a sample checked before this ships, say which slugs.

## Still open

**O-307** is untouched: `classics-notes.js` (1,677 notes) and `city-plates.js` history (279) have **no overlay and no merge site** — a mechanism to build plus ~11,700 strings, not a data fill. **O-308** (the bot's 96 pinned absences are structural, not semantic) is unchanged.

title: v0.62.780 — coverage is not fidelity: 190 French dish notes had lost the English hedge
body:
**#1756 was never reviewed.** Codex replied *"You have reached your Codex usage limits for code reviews"* and `get_reviews` returned `[]` — so 1,653 hand-written strings shipped unlooked-at. This PR is the self-review that stood in for it, and it found a defect in that merged work.

**Then Codex reviewed *this* PR** — the ready-for-review conversion triggered it — and found a defect in the fix. Both P2 findings confirmed against source and fixed in `21a3c6ae`. **One of them was three times larger than reported.**

Also carries `[AMD-59]`, #1756's merge record, folded forward per D-205.

---

## I told you "a few hedges". It was 190.

Reading a ten-note sample I noticed `american::gumbo` had dropped *"often"* and `chinese::moon cake` *"traditionally"*, and reported that as a small artefact. Measuring the class instead of the instances:

| | |
| :--- | ---: |
| dish notes whose English carries a hedge (*often / typically / traditionally / usually / commonly*) | **772** |
| of those, notes whose French carried none | **190** |
| after this PR | **0** |

*"Often thickened with okra"* had become *"épaissi au gombo."* The French asserts more than the English does — 190 times, in the product's own second language. Every locale was present and every gate was green while that was true.

## The count moved twice, and the second move is the interesting one

**206 → 160.** The first pass over-reported: the French hedge inventory was too narrow. *courant*, *répandu*, *incontournable*, *en général* and *traditionnel* are hedges too, and 38 notes were flagged that had never lost anything. I widened the inventory, reported 160, and called that a correction.

**160 → 190, found by Codex.** It was half a correction. Widening the inventory removed 38 false positives **and admitted 30 false negatives in the same move** — notes passing on a hedge word that answered a *different clause*. Codex's example, reproduced exactly:

> `hong-kong::macaroni soup` — EN: *"...a Hong Kong cha chaan teng breakfast **staple**, featuring macaroni in a light chicken broth, **often** with ham and a fried egg."*
> FR (before): *"...un petit-déjeuner **incontournable** des char chaan teng hongkongais : ... avec jambon et œuf au plat."*

*incontournable* renders **staple**. The *often* was simply gone — and the unrelated match let the note through a check whose entire job was to catch that.

Codex named one. **Re-reading all 38: 30 were genuine drops, 8 legitimate.** A correction that only looks in one direction is not a correction.

## What was actually done

- **95 corrected by rule** — insert the matching adverb before the French participle. Each read against its English before being applied.
- **95 written by hand** — 65 where the rule put the hedge on the wrong clause (`turkish::meze platter`: the *"often"* belongs to *including*, not *stuffed*) or broke the sentence (`german::knödel` → *"de la généralement cuisine d'Europe centrale"*), plus the **30** Codex's finding exposed.
- **`argentinian::empanada argentina`** — Codex's second finding, also confirmed. *"généralement"* sat on the baking when the English qualifies the **filling**. Moved to *"garni"*. **I saw this one during my own review and judged it acceptable.** It wasn't.
- Three from the original sample: `french::croque madame` was the 0.59× outlier — the French had assumed the reader knows what a croque-monsieur is, dropping *hot*, *ham*, *cheese*. `argentinian::morcilla` (0.78×) and `vietnamese::xoi` (0.80×) were checked and **left** — French is simply more compact there.
- One pre-existing wart cleaned: `egyptian::basbousa` said *"sirop de sucre sucré."*

## The gate

`FR_HEDGE` is now **adverbial only** — forms that can qualify a clause. The 8 notes where French legitimately carries the hedge as an adjective (*"commonly found in"* → *"courante en"*) are **pinned one at a time**, each with the carrying phrase quoted so the pin fails if the note is reworded — the `ABSENT_BY_DESIGN` precedent from `__tests__/i18n-coverage.test.js`. Deliberately **not** generated from a pattern: a rule that admits the whole class is how the 30 got in. A fifth assertion checks every pin still matches its note.

Proved by mutation, not by a green tick:
- restoring the flat French to `hong-kong::macaroni soup` — **Codex's own case** — fails the assertion **naming that slug**; restored, green;
- breaking the `french::steak frites` pin fires **both** assertions, which is right: the note loses its hedge and the pin goes stale together.

The comment says what to do when it false-positives on a legitimate paraphrase: **add the form to the inventory — never delete the note's hedge to match.** A gate satisfiable by damaging the content is worse than no gate.

## The three checks that came back clean

- **Years and percentages** — 44 notes carry a figure. **0 years dropped, 0 percentages dropped.**
- **Multi-word proper nouns** — 79 flagged; all 79 read, all 79 correct French renderings. *"Southern African"* → *d'Afrique australe*; *"Bombe Alaska"* → *omelette norvégienne*; *"Chairman Mao"* → *président Mao*.
- **Length ratio** — median **1.09**, p10 0.96, p90 1.22.

## Verification

- Measured on the **merged** table via `nation-overlay.js`, per the method note in `[AMD-57]` — reading either file alone is how this corpus stayed wrong twice this month.
- Locale coverage **unchanged**: 1,681 / 1,681 in all 8 locales, **0 short**. No key added or removed; 194 string values edited in place.
- **0** French strings with double, leading or trailing whitespace.
- `npx vitest run` — **187 files / 4,395 tests** green, re-run *after* the last edit.
- No `web/` build: the only `web/` references to `nation-overlay` are comments.

## What this does not fix

**The gate is string matching, not clause alignment** (`O-312`). A note hedging the wrong clause *with an adverb* still passes — `empanada` was exactly that shape, and only a human reading caught it. Recorded rather than left implied.

**The other six languages were not checked** (`O-310`). The `id/ru/de/zh/ja/es` rows are machine output rather than one author compressing while writing — a different failure mode, but *different* is not *absent*, and nothing has looked.

**`O-311`** stays open until a native French reader has seen these strings. Codex has now reviewed the *gate* twice and improved it both times; it has not read 1,681 French sentences for register.

**O-307** (`classics-notes.js` + `city-plates.js` history, ~11,700 strings, no overlay and no merge site) and **O-308** are unchanged and unstarted.

title: v0.62.792 — city-plates histories 220/279, and the gate learns untranslated English
body:
**#1757 merged**, so this is a new PR on a branch restarted from `main`. It carries the next tranche of **O-307** — the Philippines (Manila, Cebu, Davao, Baguio, Iloilo, Tagaytay, Cavite) plus Yogyakarta — taking `city-plates.js` 📜 histories from **205 to 220 of 279 (78.9%)** in all eight locales.

---

## Error eleven walked through every rule I had

I wrote a Russian sentence as:

> «Батангас, историческая скотоводческая земля, **claims** рождение…»

The English verb just sat there. **Both existing rules were right and the string was still wrong:**

- the script-per-language rule allows Latin in Russian — it has to, because Latin proper nouns belong there: *Asiong's Carinderia*, *TasteAtlas*, *Lord Stow's*;
- the mixed-script-word rule saw nothing either — `claims` is a perfectly well-formed Latin word, not a half-Cyrillic typo like the `лua` that rule was written for.

So a sixth rule: **a bare English function or common word standing inside a `ru`/`zh`/`ja` string.** It is deliberately a **stopword list**, not "any Latin word" — the latter would fire on every proper noun in the corpus and be switched off within a day, which is the failure mode of a gate nobody can live with.

Proved by mutation: injecting `claims` into a Russian value fails the assertion by name; the **220 rows already written pass** under it.

## The running tally

**Eleven errors in 220 rows, none of which reached a reader.** Each was invisible to me on re-reading and visible to a five-line rule:

| # | what | where | rule that caught it |
| ---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Russian *официально* | a **Chinese** string | script-per-language |
| 2–5 | Japanese kana (shop names, a loanword) | four **Chinese** strings | script-per-language |
| 6–7 | Han characters 日月 | two **Russian** strings | script-per-language |
| 8 | `лua` — Russian spelled with Latin letters | Russian | mixed-script word *(added for it)* |
| 9 | `таккangjeong` | Russian | mixed-script word *(fired on the next batch)* |
| 10 | 못 — Hangul for "pond" | a **Chinese** string | Hangul rule *(added for it)* |
| 11 | `claims` | Russian | English-stopword rule *(added for it)* |

Four of the six rules exist because a specific error got past the previous five. That is the intended shape: the gate learns from each new script the corpus touches.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **187 files / 4,401 tests** green, re-run after the last edit.
- Every batch passes the contamination check *before* it is merged into the overlay; the check is a CI assertion, not a scratch file.
- Curated `en`/`fr` verified unchanged — the merge loop only fills a language the datum lacks.
- Branch restarted from `origin/main` after #1757 merged, with the one unmerged tranche replayed on top. `#1757` verified by content on main first: `0.62.791`, 205/279 histories, 1,681 dish notes at 8 locales with 0 short, all four `ArrivalPlate` render sites reading `localisedBody`, `AMD-59`…`AMD-62` and `O-310`…`O-313` present.
- Pre-push state read and quoted, per X-31:
  ```
  remote_tip=1e0adf1c  local=5d90223b  main=6e0f763f
  tree(remote_tip) == tree(main) -> remote tip carries NO unmerged content (PR #1757 merged)
  local_contains_main=true
  verdict=ALLOW force-with-lease — branch restarted from main
  ```

## Still open

**59 city-plates rows**, then **classics-notes.js — 1,677 rows × 6 languages**, which has not been started. **O-313** remains the lever: `scripts/translate-content.mjs` still does not know either corpus, so a funded run would fill the others and silently skip these two.

title: v0.62.795 — city-plates.js complete: 279 / 279 histories in all eight locales
body:
**The first of O-307's two corpora is finished.** Every 📜 history on every city plate now reads in the reader's own language.

| | before v0.62.781 | now |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| `city-plates.js` histories | 279 | 279 |
| carrying all 8 locales | **0** | **279** |
| render sites reading the reader's language | **1 of 5** | **5 of 5** |

**1,674 strings written by hand across seventeen tranches**, Singapore to Rotorua — Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau, Korea, mainland China, Indonesia, the Philippines, Brunei, Australia and New Zealand. **No external API was called**, at any point, per the standing no-spend rule.

---

## The gate now pins completeness — and only now

v0.62.781's header argued that a coverage count *"would fail on every tranche and teach whoever hits it to weaken the check."* That was true **while the corpus was being filled**, and it is false now that it is finished: the only way to break the count is to add a dish and not translate it — **exactly the failure this corpus carried for its entire existence** before the merge site was built.

Proved by mutation: one `ja` line deleted, the assertion fails naming that slug; restored, 7/7 green.

`classics-notes.js` is **deliberately not pinned**. It is still `en`+`fr` only, and pinning an unfinished corpus is how a gate gets switched off.

## Thirteen errors, none of which reached a reader

None were visible to me on re-reading. **Four of the six rules exist because a specific error walked past the previous five:**

| error | rule that caught it |
| :--- | :--- |
| Russian *официально* in a **Chinese** string; kana in five Chinese strings; 日月 mid-sentence in two **Russian** strings | script-per-language |
| `лua` — Russian spelled with Latin letters | mixed-script word, **added for it** |
| `таккangjeong` | mixed-script word, **fired on the next batch** |
| 못 — Hangul for "pond", in a Chinese string | Hangul rule, **added for it** |
| `claims` sitting untranslated in a Russian sentence | English-stopword rule, **added for it** |

The last one is the instructive case. **Both existing rules were correct and the string was still wrong:** Latin *has* to be allowed in Russian, because Latin proper nouns belong there (*Asiong's Carinderia*, *TasteAtlas*, *Lord Stow's*), and `claims` is a well-formed Latin word rather than a half-Cyrillic typo. So the fix is a **stopword list, not "any Latin word"** — the latter would fire on every proper noun in the corpus and be switched off within a day. A gate nobody can live with protects nothing.

## One thing the tranches did that a script would not

Four rows are the corpus **being honest rather than inventive**. Kuala Belait, Muara and Tutong have no dish that sources credit to them specifically, and the English says exactly that before offering the national table. The six translations **keep that hedge** rather than quietly promoting ambuyat to a local invention in six languages — the same discipline as the French hedge work in #1757, applied while writing instead of afterwards.

## Verification

- Read from the merged table via `city-plates.js`: **279 histories, 279 complete in all eight locales**, every language at 279.
- `npx vitest run` — **188 files / 4,402 tests** green, re-run after the last edit.
- Every batch passed the contamination gate *before* being merged into the overlay.
- Curated `en`/`fr` unchanged throughout — the merge loop only fills a language the datum lacks.
- Branch restarted from `origin/main` after #1758 merged, with the unmerged commit replayed. #1758 verified by content on main first: `0.62.794`, 250/279 histories, English-stopword rule present.
- Pre-push state read and quoted, per X-31:
  ```
  remote_tip=9f8be363  local=79f23f78  main=97bdc694
  tree(remote_tip) == tree(main) -> its PR #1758 is merged, no unmerged content
  local_contains_main=true
  ```

## What is left

**`classics-notes.js` — 1,677 notes × 6 languages = 10,062 strings, not started.** O-307 stays open on that alone; at the observed rate it is roughly sixty-seven more tranches.

**O-313 remains the lever:** `scripts/translate-content.mjs` still does not know either corpus, so a funded run would fill the others and silently skip these two. That is a decision for you, not me — and because the overlay files are additive, nothing written by hand would be discarded if it were taken.
