title: classics-notes: the six-locale corpus, in one PR
body:
**Draft, and staying draft until the corpus is finished.** The operator asked for one PR rather than a PR per tranche — *"can you do all at once ? do we have to repeat merge . do a proper job"* — so this branch accumulates every remaining batch and gets reviewed once.

## Where it stands

**195 of 1,636 translatable classics notes** now carry all six locales (id, ru, de, zh, ja, es) — 1,170 strings written and validated. Remaining: 1,441 rows ≈ 8,646 strings.

41 rows are held back untranslated because their English source stops mid-clause. Translating a truncated sentence invents an ending; that is a source-prose decision for the operator, logged as O-314.

## What changed

- `classics-notes-i18n.generated.js` — hand-filled overlay in generated shape, merged into `CLASSIC_NOTES` / `CUISINE_NOTES` at module load by the fail-open, language-agnostic block already in `classics-notes.js`. Hand-authored always wins; a new locale stays a data change, never a code change.

## Verification (sandbox)

- `__tests__/classics-city-plates-i18n.test.js` — 8 tests green. The gates that matter here: merge-site assertions evaluated through `require()` rather than grepped, orphan-key checks, hand-authored-wins, the script-contamination gate, and the 140-character cap across all eight locales.
- Every batch passes a scratchpad validator before merge: script-per-language, Hangul, mixed-script word, untranslated English stopword inside non-Latin text, whitespace, identical-to-another-language, and the 140-char cap.

## Findings worth recording

- **The mixed-script rule earned its place four more times.** Four `кueh` (a Cyrillic к inside a Latin word) and one `неjareными` (Latin j and a wedged inside a Russian word). None is visible on re-reading; all would have shipped.
- **The 140-char cap is not script-neutral.** id/ru/de/es overflow where zh/ja never do — 34 strings in one 25-row batch alone. The cap check now runs where the string is written, not only at the CI gate.
- **6 further truncated English sources** found by scanning for unbalanced parentheses and quotes: `malaysian::apam`, `greek::halloumi greek style`, `polish::kielbasa`, `australasia::pasifika fusion plate`, `northwestern::xibei dumpling soup`, `dessert::eclair`. They join the 35 already held back.
- **Han characters carried over from English source notes** (炖 in `peranakan::itek tim`, 笋 in `SG::soon kueh`) were romanised for id/ru/de/es rather than passed through — the same treatment いづう and 油揚げ already had.

## Known gaps

- The corpus is 12% done; this PR is not ready for review until it is 100%.
- O-310 (the hedge-fidelity check has only ever run against French), O-311, O-312, O-313 remain open and are not addressed here.

title: classics-notes: the six-locale corpus, complete
body:
Completes the `classics-notes.js` corpus in six locales (id, ru, de, zh, ja, es). Continues after **#1761 merged at 275 rows**; this branch was restarted from `main` rather than stacked on merged history.

One PR rather than a PR per tranche, per the operator — *"can you do all at once ? do we have to repeat merge . do a proper job"*.

## Where it stands — done

**1,592 of 1,592 translatable notes** carry all eight locales. Measured through the evaluated overlay merge, never by grepping the literal:

```
notes: 1677 · all six extra locales: 1592 · all eight locales: 1592
```

`1,677 − 1,592 = 85` held back, and the held-back list matches the missing list exactly — no row is missing for any other reason.

### The 85 are source-side problems, not translation gaps

76 English notes stop mid-clause (**O-314**) and 4 describe a different dish from their key (**O-315**). Five more surfaced in this pass and are held on the same grounds:

| key | what the English note says |
| :--- | :--- |
| `ukrainian::verhuny` | names the dish and its regional aliases, then stops |
| `israeli::labneh` | the two words "Levantine (Arab)" |
| `uzbek::halim uzbek` | "Uzbek halim (halisa)" — a name and an alias |
| `brazilian::feijão tropeiro` | stops at "created by 17th-19th c."; the subject is never named |
| `northwestern::beef noodle lanzhou` | stops at "codified c." with the date missing |

Repairing any of them means **authoring new English source prose**, which is a curation decision and the operator's call, not a translation one.

The earlier figure of 1,636 translatable rows in this PR's first draft was measured before those five were found; the corpus did not shrink, the count of known-bad sources grew.

## Two notes translated as written, not "fixed"

`australasia::kaipake plate` and `macau::caca-mato` are notes recording that **no such dish could be documented**. The six translations preserve that finding — including the `[UNVERIFIED]` marker — rather than inventing a dish to describe. Same treatment `eurasian::soyok` got earlier.

## Findings from the run

- **The batch validator earned its keep on the last pass**: a Latin `e` inside a Cyrillic word (`коржe`) and two strings over the 140-character contract, all caught before merge. The 140-character cap is not script-neutral — it fires on roughly a third of every id/ru/de/es batch and never on zh/ja.
- **Four false positives on proper nouns**: the untranslated-English rule reads the articles in "The Halia" and "Cat and the Fiddle" as leaked English. Those strings were **reworded, not exempted** — the rule that would exempt them is the same character-class rule withdrawn earlier in this branch for misfiring on romanised endonyms across a second corpus.
- **Kana and Han leaks** kept appearing where a proper noun was carried across unchanged (おまかせ, 味の三平, 笋, 炖) — the gate caught each one.
- **`bercita rasa nutty`** — English stranded inside Indonesian, caught by reading, not by a rule. The untranslated-English rule only fires inside non-Latin scripts, so English sitting in id/de/es is invisible to it. That gap is still open.

## Verification (sandbox)

- `node --check` on `classics-notes-i18n.generated.js` — clean.
- `npm test -- --run` — **188 files, 4,403 tests, all green**.
- `__tests__/classics-city-plates-i18n.test.js` — 8/8, including the whole-corpus script, leak, mixed-word and stopword rules.
- Every batch landed through `land.sh`, a `set -e` pipeline that re-runs all rules over the **entire** merged overlay after each merge, not just the batch.

## Known gaps

- The 85 held-back rows above, awaiting a decision on repairing the English sources.
- The **merge record for #1761** is still owed and is being held per D-205 to ride the next substantive PR rather than opening a docs-only PR to record a PR.
- Three Codex threads on the merged **#1760** were never replied to — GitHub returned `API rate limit already exceeded for user ID 269136209`. All three findings are fixed and merged; the threads are still open.
- The **Michelin arc of 26-08** (v0.62.766 – v0.62.776, PRs #1751 – #1754) is still unjournalled.
- O-307, O-308, O-310, O-311, O-312, O-313, O-184, O-228 remain open and unapproved.

title: v0.62.803 — the held docs: #1762's merge record, a false gap corrected, and the Michelin arc gets its own file
body:
Opened at the operator's request — ***"open the PR with all the held docs"***.

Docs-only. Three records that had been held in the working tree per **D-205**, plus the version bump.

## What's here

| Commit | Content |
| :--- | :--- |
| `70ef0141` | `[AMD-3]` — **#1762's merge record**, written at merge time and verified from the merged tree |
| `efe70cb1` | `[AMD-4]` — **a false gap corrected**: the Michelin arc was never unjournalled |
| `2700e351` | **`journal-0_62_776-27_08_26-0825.md`** — the Michelin day-arc gets its own file and `[HDR]` |
| `53487d25` | v0.62.803 + the live anchor note's version marker |

### `[AMD-3]` — #1762 merged as `cb7d3efe`

Verified per **D-123** from the merged tree rather than from the branch I had been editing —
`classics-notes.js` loaded out of a detached worktree at `cb7d3efe`:

```
notes: 1677 · all six extra locales: 1592 · all eight locales: 1592
strings: 12906 · over 140: 0
```

Two independent assertions, not one: the coverage, **and** the 140-character contract across every
locale — the contract Codex found was being enforced on `en`/`fr` alone. Branch restart evidenced
before it was done: old tip and merged main both `9c60c548^{tree}`, empty diff, so nothing unmerged
was lost.

### `[AMD-4]` — the correction

I claimed, in four places including #1762's own body, that the Michelin arc of 26-08 was
**unjournalled**. It was not. It is recorded in `journal-0_62_732` at `[AMD-44]` … `[AMD-55]`, and the
Register tracked it too — **O-224, O-225, O-227, O-229** each opened for one unshipped merge record in
that arc and each is `CLOSED`.

**Cause:** I read the `doc/.serial-state.yml` anchor notes, saw `amd44`/`amd45`/`amd50`/`amd55` written
there, and concluded those blocks existed only there — without opening the journal file. That is
**D-199**: an invariant checked against a stored note instead of the artifact. The tell was in my own
sentence, which cited them as *"AMD-44 … AMD-57"* — Journal numbering. The notes were quoting the
Journal and I read the quotation as the original.

The same sentence carried a second false claim, *"logged here and in `doc/Register/`"*;
`grep -c unjournalled doc/Register/*.md` returns nothing.

Per **AU-1** the false text in the earlier blocks is **left standing** — those entries record what I
believed when I wrote them — and is corrected by amendment per **AU-7**.

### `journal-0_62_776` — the arc's own `[HDR]`

A header view over the 26-08 arc: four PRs (**#1751** `900e86c4`, **#1752** `4561c03e`, **#1753**
`c1cf073b`, **#1754** `42c9caca`), eleven versions, and the six verbatim one-line instructions that
produced them.

**AU-1 respected:** the arc's `[AMD-44]`…`[AMD-55]` blocks stay in `journal-0_62_732` and are pointed
at, not copied. Copying would create a second original, and whoever later corrected one would have to
know the other existed.

**One correction the file carries:** the version range names two bodies of work. **766–772 is
Michelin; 773–776 is not** — it is the i18n coverage gate, the O-185 owner-gate fix, and a reviewer
finding. The shorthand was wrong by four versions.

## Verification (sandbox)

End state measured on `main` (`cb7d3efe`), loaded rather than grepped:

```
KNOWN_DELTAS        0     <- empty for the first time
cities in manifest  11
green-star venues   8     VN 3 · HK 4 · MO 1
CN 511 (szx 28) · FR 130 · JP 590 (tyo 272) · VN 86
```

- `npm test -- --run` — **188 files, 4,403 tests green**
- `__tests__/serial-state-anchor.test.js` — 4/4, after re-anchoring all three time fields together
- Every command in the new entry's own `[TEST]` block was **run before shipping** — an unexecuted test
  block is a claim, not a test. 149 tests across the four Michelin and owner-gate files pass.

## Notes

- **No preflight trigger applies.** `index.js`, the bot handlers, the `/s` and free-text search flow,
  venue rendering, `i18n.js` and the fuzzy matchers are all untouched. Version bumped anyway, because
  the repo's habit is that anything reaching `main` carries one.
- **TF-7 fired during the write.** The arc entry was drafted at 07:40 SGT and finished at 08:25 — a
  45-minute drift. The stamp and the filename carry the completion time rather than dating the entry
  before the reads it reports; the drift is logged in the entry.
- **D-205 note:** this PR is opened on the operator's explicit instruction. D-205 bars a PR whose only
  content is a *merge record*; two of these three records are not that, and the rule defers to the
  operator in any case.

## Known gaps

- The **85 held-back source notes** (O-314 truncated English, O-315 key/note mismatch) — repairing any
  means authoring new English prose, which is the operator's call.
- The untranslated-English rule fires only inside non-Latin scripts, so English stranded in
  `id`/`de`/`es` is invisible to it (`bercita rasa nutty` was caught by reading).
- **O-226** (one Shenzhen Bib cuisine label probably wrong; count unaffected) and **O-228** (101 Paris
  rows carry no `cuisine`) remain open from the Michelin arc.
- O-307, O-308, O-310 – O-313, O-184 remain open and unapproved.

title: v0.62.805 — the classics-notes corpus closes at 1,674, and the English check stops being blind to half the languages
body:
Completes the first three items of the outstanding list: the 85 held-back notes, the `id`/`de`/`es` blind spot, and O-307.

## The corpus is finished — 1,674 of 1,674

`classics-notes-i18n.generated.js` goes from 1,592 to **1,674 rows at all eight locales**. The 82 rows freed by the English repair in v0.62.804 are translated into `id`/`ru`/`de`/`zh`/`ja`/`es` **by hand** — 492 strings, no external API called. Coverage measured by evaluating the merge (`require()`), never by grepping the literal, per **D-199**.

O-314 opened at **35** truncated English notes and closes at **82**. The number is recorded going up because a gap that grows when you finally measure it is the ordinary case. The repair reads the true old string from the **live module** and does a uniqueness-checked textual replace — never a regex over a 14,000-line data file. Non-fabrication rule, stated before the work rather than after: complete the sentence only where the missing tail is a fact already established; otherwise trim to the last complete clause. `south-indian::pongal` looked truncated and was **not** — a scanner artifact, the regex splitting on an inner quote. It is named because a false positive silently "fixed" is a defect introduced.

## The check that was blind to half the languages

`ENGLISH_STOPWORD` ran on `ru`/`zh`/`ja` only, so English stranded in a Latin-script locale shipped unchecked. `bercita rasa nutty` reached the corpus and was caught by **reading**, not by CI.

Three widenings were measured against the live overlays. **Two were rejected on evidence, and both looked obviously right:**

| Candidate | Hits | False positives | Why |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| Existing stopword list on `id`/`de`/`es` | 1,096 | **100 %** | German `in` alone accounts for 1,075. Spanish `has` (*no has llegado*), Indonesian `has` (sirloin) and `AS` (the US). Proper nouns the rule cannot see past: *The Halia*, *Duke of Wellington*, *Black or White*, *Taiwan Tobacco and Liquor Corporation*. |
| English food-NOUN list | 21 | **100 %** | A culinary loanword is not a leak: *puff pastry*, *clotted cream*, *cream cracker*, *corned beef*, *baked Alaska*, *fish and chips* — and *topping*, which is now simply an Indonesian word. |
| English descriptive ADJECTIVES, lowercase-only | **0** | — | Still flags `rasa nutty`. **Shipped.** |

Two constraints carry it. **Adjectives, not nouns** — a dish *name* may legitimately stay in English, an adjective *describing* it may not. And **lowercase-only, case-sensitively**, which is exactly what separates *Mango Sticky Rice* (a Thai dish, named) from *sticky* (a description left untranslated). `herbal` was dropped from the list on the same evidence: a real word in both Indonesian and Spanish, with 9 legitimate uses in the corpus.

This is the same shape as the character-class rule the test file already records as **withdrawn** for misfiring on romanised endonyms. The test for a rule here is measured false positives, not plausibility — and both rejected candidates are written into the file so the next author does not re-derive them.

## The pin, and what it excludes by name

A completeness assertion for `classics-notes`, matching the one v0.62.795 gave city-plates at 279/279. A corpus that is finished stops being a target and becomes an invariant.

**Three rows are excluded, individually named in the assertion rather than omitted from it**, with a `<= 3` guard so the exception register can shrink but never grow.

## O-315 — a decision, not a task

Those three notes describe a **different dish** from the key they hang on:

- `northeastern::changchun braised duck` — described as a steamed Songhua white fish
- `eurasian::roast suckling pig` — described as a curry of diced pork and offal
- `eurasian::eurasian fishball curry` — described as Hong Kong post-war street food

This is a different class from the wording errors found alongside them. `hunan::hunan dry-fried green beans` carried a wrong provenance clause and was simply **corrected**, because the note was about the right dish. These three are not. Fixing them means choosing whether the **key** or the **note** is the truth, and that changes what the app offers a searcher — so it is the operator's call, not the translator's. The rows stay `en`+`fr` until it is made. Translating them as written would render the wrong dish into six more languages and multiply the error by six.

## Verification

- `npm test -- --run` → **188 files, 4,404 tests green** (+1, the new completeness assertion)
- The descriptor rule measured across **11,718 overlay values at 0 hits** *before* being written into the file, with a positive control (`rasa nutty` → flagged) and a negative control (`Mango Sticky Rice` → clean)
- `node --check` on the changed test file
- Coverage read by loading the module, not by grep

## Docs

O-307 **closed** (both corpora complete), O-314 **closed**, O-316 **opened and closed** in the same entry with both rejected candidates recorded, O-315 **opened and held**. Journal `[AMD-6]` appended; `doc/.serial-state.yml` counters bumped and all three anchor fields re-anchored per **D-203**, with the displaced note preserved per **AU-1**.

`[AMD-5]` — #1763's merge record — folds forward into this PR per **D-205** rather than opening one of its own.

## Still open

O-226 and O-228 are blocked on an external per-venue Michelin source, and no API spend is permitted. O-308, O-310, O-311, O-312, O-313, O-184 remain.

title: v0.62.806–807 — O-315 closed (four contaminated rows removed), and O-317's four-row case-sensitivity bug fixed
body:
Two items, both narrowed by evidence to something smaller and more specific than they were opened as.

- **v0.62.806 — O-315 closed.** Four contaminated rows removed, not three held for a decision.
- **v0.62.807 — O-317 part-closed.** Four of its 27 were a case-sensitivity bug; the other 23 are a product decision and are pinned, not guessed at.

---

# v0.62.806 — O-315 was never a decision, and I was wrong to escalate it

`[AMD-6]` held these rows for the operator on the grounds that fixing them meant choosing whether the key or the note was the truth. **The evidence was one field away.** Every row carries a `local` endonym, and in all four the `local`, the `note` and the `sources` agree *with each other* and disagree with the **key** — and the rest of the repo corroborates the key:

| Key | Its own `local` | Its note describes | Corroboration elsewhere |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `eurasian::roast suckling pig` | `feng` | curry of pork offal | `eurasian::feng (curry of pork offal)` **already exists** |
| `eurasian::eurasian fishball curry` | 咖哩魚蛋 | HK curry fish balls | `hong-kong::curry fish balls` **already exists** |
| `northeastern::changchun braised duck` | 清蒸白鱼 | Jilin steamed white fish | `nation-overlay-local` gives the key's endonym as 酱鸭 |
| `northeastern::da pai dang chinese bbq` | 大排檔 | HK dai pai dong | overlay's own note says *Northeastern China* |

There was no coin to flip. These are four **contaminated rows duplicating content the corpus already holds correctly elsewhere** — a data cleanup escalated to the operator because I had not read a field sitting in the same object.

**The fourth was found by scanning, not reading.** `northeastern::da pai dang chinese bbq` reads *"Open-air **Cantonese** street-food stall, licensed in postwar **Hong Kong**"* under a Dongbei key, while the overlay's own note for that key says *"open-air food stalls in **Northeastern** China"*. O-315 opened at three because three is what one translation pass happened to surface.

## Removal, not authorship — and it restores rather than loses

`index.js` merges as `{ ...d, ...m }`, so a classics-notes row **overwrites** the nation overlay's note. Deleting the four lets the overlay's correct, sourced notes through. Verified at the render site:

| Key | What shipped before | What ships now |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `roast suckling pig` | "A rich Eurasian curry of diced pork and pig's offal…" | "…a whole roasted piglet, fed on its mother's milk…" |
| `eurasian fishball curry` | "…a Hong Kong street-food staple… 1950s hawker carts." | "…fish balls simmered in a rich curry sauce, often with daikon radish." |
| `da pai dang chinese bbq` | "Open-air Cantonese street-food stall… postwar Hong Kong" | "…open-air food stalls in Northeastern China." |

Under the **zero-fabrication** instruction this is the only available fix: writing replacement notes would mean authoring source prose for dishes there is no source for. The four removed rows — French, sources, and the six `da pai dang` translations — are **preserved verbatim in the journal** per AU-1.

## A correction `[AMD-6]` owes

It said all three "render the wrong dish". **Three did. `changchun braised duck` did not** — absent from the overlay's `iconicDishes`, and the other consumer (`city-plates.js`) reads only `CLASSIC_NOTES` keyed by country code. Wrong data that never reached a reader. Wrong is still worth removing; overstating its reach is not.

## What the removal broke

`da pai dang` had already been translated, so deleting its base note **orphaned six strings** — which a later coverage count reads as work already done. Cleared, and now pinned: the coverage test asserts no overlay row lacks a base note.

Corpus: **1,673 of 1,673 at all eight locales, zero exceptions** for the first time.

---

# v0.62.807 — O-317: four were a bug, twenty-three are a question

The count is **27, not the 28** logged an hour earlier: v0.62.806 removed `changchun braised duck` as an O-315 row, and it was also one of the 28. Two items overlapped and I counted it in both.

## The four: a case-sensitive lookup

`index.js` enriched the cuisine plate with `cnotes[d.name]` — case-**sensitive** — while the two tables disagree on case:

| Overlay dish name | Note key | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `escargots de Bourgogne` | `escargots de bourgogne` | no match |
| `tarta de Santiago` | `tarta de santiago` | no match |
| `coconut chicken (Hainan style)` | `coconut chicken (hainan style)` | no match |
| `Taiwan night market dishes` | `taiwan night market dishes` | no match |

Four curated, sourced, eight-locale notes silently failed to attach; the dish rendered bare and nothing reported a miss. **`city-plates.js` has folded since v0.62.175** — its `_fold` exists for exactly this. The same datum was reachable through one code path and not the other: O-305's shape, and the v0.62.778 French bug's shape, for the third time on this branch. **The defect is never in the data, it is in the one call site that forgot.**

The fold was **measured before it was written**: 1,484 matches before, **1,488 after**, exactly those four recovered, **zero existing matches redirected**, zero folded-name collisions anywhere. An exact hit still wins, so a fold can only *add* a match, never move one — and the test asserts the redirect count is zero, because the day two dishes fold together the enrichment starts lying about one of them.

## The twenty-three: not fixed, and here is what was checked first

Each of these would have made it someone else's fix rather than the operator's:

| Question | Answer | Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Duplicates served elsewhere? | **No** — 0 of 23 appear in another cuisine's dish list or in `CLASSIC_NOTES` | Retiring them destroys unique sourced content. Unlike O-315. |
| Ever in the overlay, so re-adding restores? | **No** — `git log -S` finds `hainanese chicken rice`, `german beer`, `yuzu cheesecake` in **zero** commits touching `nation-overlay.js` | Authored independently of the dish list. Adding them is a new claim. |
| A hidden array the enrichment misses? | **No** — `iconicDishes` is the only dish-bearing array | The beer/ale/wine cluster is genuinely absent, not structurally hidden. |

So making them reachable means **adding dishes to what the app offers a searcher** — a product decision. Under zero fabrication I will not assert that a dish is iconic to a cuisine on the strength of wanting a number to go down. Pinned by name with a `<= 23` guard so a twenty-fourth cannot join them unnoticed.

**The one worth your attention:** `hainanese::hainanese chicken rice` — Singapore's national dish — is curated, sourced, translated into eight locales, and **unreachable**. `SG`'s `CLASSIC_NOTES` has **no chicken rice entry at all**, and the only chicken rice any reader can reach is `thai::thai chicken rice (khao man gai)`.

**Two of the 23 are notes recording that the dish does not exist** — `australasia::kaipake plate` and `macau::caca-mato`, both explicitly marked unverified by an earlier pass. Unreachable is arguably correct for those two; they are listed with the rest rather than quietly excused, because their reason differs from the other 21.

---

## Verification

- Coverage and reachability read by **evaluating the merge** (D-199), never grepped
- `CUISINE_NOTES` consumers **enumerated** — `index.js` is the only production one, which is what makes "unreachable" a fact rather than an inference
- Recovered set asserted **by name**, redirect set asserted empty
- `node --check` on every changed `.js`
- **`npm test -- --run` → 188 files, 4,407 tests green** (+3 across the two versions)

## Also carried

`[AMD-7]`, #1764's merge record, folds forward per **D-205**.

## Still open

**O-317's 23** and **O-318** (the provenance scan flags 38 rows of which 37 are legitimate — three because the regex read *"served over turkey"*, the bird, as Turkish; the third rule rejected on measured false positives after O-316's two). Unchanged: O-226, O-228 (blocked on an external per-venue Michelin source; no API spend), O-308, O-310–O-313, O-184.

title: v0.62.808 — hainanese chicken rice reaches the plate; O-317's 23 becomes 22
body:
Operator: *"add hainanese chicken rice to the cuisine plate"* — the product decision v0.62.807 handed back, taken for one row.

## The note already existed. Only the reader was missing.

Curated, three sources, all eight locales, endonym 海南鸡饭. It could not reach anyone because the enrichment in `index.js` iterates `iconicDishes`, and chicken rice was not in it. **O-317's unreachable count: 23 → 22.**

## The overlay already carried chicken rice, and that changed how the edit was made

`sharedWithNeighbors: S('chicken rice', 'chicken rice', ['singaporean', 'cantonese'])`. So the exclusion was **not an oversight** — someone deliberately modelled chicken rice as a shared, ambiguous name. Adding it blindly would have fought that decision.

But the two entries are different shapes for different jobs:

| | Shape | Job |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `S()` | `{dish, ambiguousMatch, sharedWith}` | the AMBIGUOUS_DISHES alias pin — interpreting what a user *typed* |
| `F()` | `{name, kind, sharedWith}` | the plate list — what the app *offers* |

This is also why the reachability scan was right not to see it: it looked for arrays whose items carry a `name`, and this one carries a `dish`.

**Three things checked before touching the file**, each of which would have made the edit wrong:

| Check | Result |
| :--- | :--- |
| `nation-overlay.test.js`'s disjoint invariant — no dish in both lists | Compares **exact lowercased names**; `chicken rice` ≠ `hainanese chicken rice`. Collisions measured after the edit: **0** |
| Is `sharedWithNeighbors` rendered on the plate, so this would duplicate? | **No** — its only consumers are that test and `discovery-dish.js`'s alias expansion |
| Is `sharedWith: ['singaporean','cantonese']` mine to assert? | **No, and I did not** — carried across verbatim from the `S()` entry already in the file |

## A visible product change, stated rather than buried

`groupCuisineDishes` takes `headliners = dishes.slice(0, 3)`. Placing the dish first promotes it into the headliner row and moves `hainanese mutton soup` down into its `soup` group.

**There is no neutral position** — last would have buried Singapore's national dish in a bucket beneath the pork chop — so the choice sits in a comment at the line where it can be seen, and it reverses in one word.

Headliners now: `hainanese chicken rice | hainanese pork chop | hainanese curry rice`.

## The pin ratchets down

23 → 22, so a resolved row cannot be quietly refilled by a different one. And the test now asserts the key is **reachable**, not merely absent from the list — deleting a name from a pin is not the same as putting the dish on the plate, and only one of those is what was asked for.

## Verification

The enrichment **simulated against the real modules**, not inferred: on the plate ✅, note attached ✅, `en,fr,id,ru,de,zh,ja,es` ✅, endonym 海南鸡饭 ✅, 3 sources ✅, `sharedWith` preserved ✅. Mutton soup **confirmed present** in the `soup` group rather than assumed not lost. Disjoint collisions `[]`. Cuisine-wide unreachable count 22.

`npm test -- --run` → **188 files, 4,407 tests green**, run nine times.

### One thing I cannot close

An earlier run reported `Test Files 1 failed | 187 passed` with `Tests 4400 passed | 7 skipped` — **zero tests failed**, so a file threw during collection. Nine full-suite runs since are green and I could not reproduce it.

**The error worth recording is mine.** I piped that first run through `tail -6`, which printed the summary and discarded the failing file's name — so the one run that had the answer is the one I cannot interrogate. Five files carry exactly 7 tests and I will not guess between them. I am **not calling it a flake**: this repo's posture is that a failing test is never an infra flake, and "it passed the second time" is not a root cause. CI here is the independent second signal.

## Also carried

`[AMD-11]`, #1765's merge record — which exists because **`prepush-guard` blocked me**: the branch tip was content-identical to main, meaning #1765 had merged mid-edit and a fast-forward push would have appended to a closed PR, succeeding while delivering nothing. Verified rather than taken on trust, branch restarted, commit cherry-picked, diff confirmed identical. `--no-verify` was not used.

`[AMD-7]`, #1764's merge record, is **still held** and rides along too — now carried across two merges, the longest anything has waited under D-205 on this branch.

## Still open

**O-317's remaining 22**, O-318, O-226, O-228, O-308, O-310–O-313, O-184.

title: v0.62.809 — 18 of O-317's 22 reach their plates; the other 4 are refused, not deferred
body:
Operator: *"add the remaining 22 to their cuisine plates."*

**18 added** across ten cuisines, each verified to attach its existing eight-locale note — **18 of 18, no exceptions**. **O-317: 22 → 4.**

## Two details a careless pass gets wrong

The four drinks use **`D()` not `F()`**, so they bucket as drinks rather than food.

And `hakka::thunder tea rice` is **food**. My first classifier called it a drink on the word *tea* — the exact keyword-rule failure this repo has already rejected twice. Checked against the real entry rather than trusted.

Everything is **appended, never reordered**: unlike `hainanese chicken rice` these are not flagship dishes, and `headliners = slice(0, 3)` means inserting at the top would have silently reshuffled ten plates.

## Four were not added, and none of them for effort

| Row | Why not |
| :--- | :--- |
| `australasia::kaipake plate` | Its own `local` reads **"[UNVERIFIED: no such dish found]"**; the note says the nearest real Māori word, *kaipuke*, means **ship** |
| `macau::caca-mato` | **"[UNVERIFIED] No dish or drink named 'caca-mato' could be confirmed"** |
| `australasia::fish suckling pacific` | Note and `local` (ʻOta ʻika) describe a real Tongan dish; the **KEY** is garbled English. Also a likely near-duplicate of `F("oka i'a")`, already on that plate — *oka iʻa* is the Samoan cognate |
| `american::american craft beer` | **Policy, not doubt** — see below |

The first two are the zero-fabrication line. Putting them on a plate offers a searcher **a dish that does not exist**. An earlier pass deliberately translated them *as written*, preserving the unverified marker rather than inventing a dish — adding them to the product would quietly undo that. For a dish nobody could document, unreachable is the correct outcome, and this is the case where the number **not** going to zero is the right answer.

## The cap test found a real breach, and I had looked straight past it

Adding `american craft beer` took American to 31 and failed `NATION_OVERLAY — caps > american iconicDishes ≤ 30` — the **HL 2026-05-08 ceiling** — on **three runs out of three**.

I had checked for a cap earlier, found only the display-cap test, and concluded there was no hard limit. The check was `grep -n "cap\b" … | head -5`, and the `caps` describe block was **below the cut**. That is the second time this session I truncated my own search and then reasoned from the truncation as though it were the whole picture — the first cost me the name of a failing file. The tooling was right both times; the `head` was mine.

Raising the cap or dropping an existing American dish is your call. **Weakening the test to make room was never an option.**

## A candidate defect investigated and rejected

180 notes end at a semicolon, which looked like a truncation class covering `british ale` (40 chars) and `barramundi pie` (54). **It is not** — `korean::kimchi`, `italian::cannoli` and `french::pot-au-feu` end the same way. A trailing semicolon is this corpus's house style for closing a note. Both rows are terse, not broken, and were added.

Recorded because I nearly held four rows on an invented defect. Fourth rule rejected on measured evidence on this branch, after O-316's two and O-318.

## Verification

- Enrichment **simulated against the real modules** for all 18: on the plate, note attached, all eight locales, correct `kind`
- `node --check`; **`npm test -- --run` → 188 files, 4,407 tests green, three runs of three**

## Also carried

`[AMD-13]`, #1766's merge record — found, like `[AMD-11]`, **by `prepush-guard` blocking me**: the branch tip was content-identical to main, so #1766 had merged mid-edit and a fast-forward push would have appended to a closed PR, succeeding while delivering nothing. **Second time in one session.** Worth stating because the failure mode has no natural symptom: a push that succeeds and delivers nothing looks exactly like a push that worked. Verified rather than trusted, branch restarted, diff confirmed identical. `--no-verify` not used.

`[AMD-7]`, #1764's merge record, is **still held** — now carried across three merges.

## Still open

**O-317's remaining 4** (three need your ruling, one needs the cap decision), O-318, O-226, O-228, O-308, O-310–O-313, O-184.

Also still unnamed: the collection-time test failure from v0.62.808, which has never reproduced. The cap failure above reproduced three times and named itself; these are not the same event and I am not treating one as an explanation for the other.

title: v0.62.810 — cap 30 → 31, american craft beer reaches the plate; O-317 down to 3
body:
Operator: *"raise the cap to 31 and add american craft beer"* — the policy decision v0.62.809 refused to make on their behalf.

`DEFAULT_CAP` **30 → 31**, `D('american craft beer')` added, its existing eight-locale note verified to attach. **O-317: 4 → 3.**

## The change is global, as asked — and measured after

Every non-SG cuisine may now hold 31, not just American. That is the plain reading of the instruction, and it is what was done rather than quietly narrowed to an American-only exception.

But it is a wider blast radius than the one row needed, so it was swept afterwards across every cuisine: **`american=31` is the only one above the old ceiling.** Nothing else drifted up on the back of it.

The **21 `— cap 30` block comments** in `nation-overlay.js` were updated too. A comment stating a superseded rule is a false statement, and **D-199** is explicit that repo text is evidence about the past — twenty-one comments asserting a dead ceiling is precisely that trap.

## What the cap was actually counting — recorded, not acted on

The cap counts food and drinks **together**. The renderer does not: `formatIconicList` slices food to `maxItems` and drinks to `maxItems / 2` **separately**, so expert mode shows up to **30 food *and* up to 15 drinks**.

| Cuisine | total | food | drinks |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| american | 30 (before) | 27 | 3 |
| german | 28 | 24 | 4 |
| british | 28 | 23 | 5 |
| singaporean | 164 | 124 | 40 |

So the row that could not reach a reader was a **drink** — blocked by a combined count the display never applies, with free slots in its own bucket *and* in the food bucket it was never competing for.

Splitting the cap to mirror the renderer would be the more precise fix. **It was not done, because it was not asked for** — it sits in the Register as a candidate refinement, next to the number it would replace.

## Verification

- Added row asserted on the plate with `kind: 'drink'`, note attached, **8 locales**
- American now **27 food + 4 drinks = 31**
- Unreachable count **3**, listed by name
- The "only american is above 30" sweep run across every cuisine rather than assumed
- **`npm test -- --run` → 188 files, 4,407 tests green, three runs of three**

## Also carried

`[AMD-14]`, #1767's merge record, folds forward per **D-205** — this is the substantive change it was waiting for.

It also carries a correction. **I told you three times that `[AMD-7]` was "still held" and "carried across three merges." That was false** — `[AMD-7]` has been on `main` since `34873386`, shipped inside #1765 exactly as D-205 prescribes. The rule worked; I stopped checking it, and each repetition took my own previous sentence as its source while the count grew with retelling rather than with evidence. Second instance of that failure this session, after the Michelin-arc claim corrected in `[AMD-4]`. One `grep` settles it either time.

## Still open — O-317's last 3, all yours

- `australasia::fish suckling pacific` — note right, key garbled, likely a duplicate of `oka i'a` already on that plate
- `australasia::kaipake plate` and `macau::caca-mato` — notes recording that the dish **could not be documented**. Unreachable is the correct outcome; my recommendation is to leave them exactly as they are

Unchanged: O-318, O-226, O-228, O-308, O-310–O-313, O-184, and the still-unnamed collection-time test failure from v0.62.808.

title: v0.62.812 — fish suckling pacific retired as a duplicate; O-317 has nothing pending
body:
Operator: *"retire fish suckling pacific as a duplicate"* — the last open row in O-317.

## The duplicate claim was confirmed before the row was touched

I had been calling it *"likely a duplicate"* for several replies. Deleting user-facing data on a *likely* is exactly the sloppiness the rest of this session has been correcting, so it was checked:

| | `australasia::fish suckling pacific` | `australasia::oka i'a` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `local` | ʻOta ʻika | oka i'a |
| note | ***Tongan*** national dish, raw fish in citrus + coconut milk | ***Samoan*** raw-fish dish, cubed fish in lime + coconut cream |
| source | **Wikipedia — ʻOta ʻika** | **Wikipedia – 'Ota 'ika (Samoan oka i'a)** |
| reachable | **no** — garbled key, absent from the plate | **yes** |
| locales | 8 | 8 |

The survivor's own source title names both dishes as one. Same article, same dish, Tongan and Samoan names — and only one of the two was ever visible to a reader.

## Base row and overlay row removed together

Deleting only the base leaves an orphan overlay row that a later coverage count reads as work already done — the mistake `da pai dang` taught at v0.62.806, and the reason there's an assertion for it.

Measured after: **1,672 notes, 1,672 at eight locales, 0 orphan overlay rows**, and `oka i'a` asserted **intact and still on the plate** rather than merely present.

## One fact was lost, and it is recorded rather than glossed

The retired note called this the **Tongan** national dish *"eaten across Polynesia"*; the survivor describes it as Samoan. Widening `oka i'a`'s prose to carry the Tongan framing would be **authoring, not retiring**, so it was not done. The full removed row and its six translations are preserved verbatim in the journal.

## The test that failed, and why lowering it was the fix

Retiring the row broke `expect(rows).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1673)` — reproducibly, three runs of three, and this time I read the failure instead of piping it through `tail`.

The floor moved to **1,672 with its reason written beside it**: 1,677 at v0.62.804 → 1,673 when O-315 removed four contaminated rows → 1,672 here. Every step down is a decision someone made and can point at. The floor exists to catch the step down **nobody decided** — a row lost to a bad edit or a bad merge. Lowering it to match reality without saying why is how a guard becomes a rubber stamp, so the number and the reason now move together or not at all.

## O-317 closes with nothing pending

Two rows remain unreachable and **both are settled by your explicit ruling** — `kaipake plate` and `caca-mato`, whose own notes record that the dish could not be documented.

The exceptions list is now a **record of decisions, not a queue of work**, and the test says so in as many words, so a future session doesn't read it as a to-do and "fix" it by shipping two dishes that may not exist.

**The arc:** opened at 28 → corrected to 27 → **23** once four turned out to be a case-sensitivity bug rather than missing data → 22 → 4 → 3 → **2, both decided.**

## Verification

- `node --check` on both changed data files
- Corpus read through the evaluated merge (D-199): 1,672 / 1,672 / 0 orphans
- **`npm test -- --run` → 188 files, 4,407 tests green, three runs of three**

## Also carried

`[AMD-17]`, #1768's merge record, folds forward per **D-205** — this is the substantive change it was waiting for.

## Still open

O-318, O-226, O-228, O-308, O-310–O-313, O-184, and the still-unnamed collection-time test failure from v0.62.808, which has now not reproduced across roughly a dozen local runs and five CI runs on clean checkouts. Still not called a flake.

title: v0.62.814 — O-320 closed: station names render in the transport TMA
body:
Operator: *"wire it up to the transport mini app"*.

## Three display sites, verified at the built output

| Site | What a reader sees |
| :--- | :--- |
| `MrtMapPanel.jsx` — info-card heading | the station popup's title |
| `MrtMapPanel.jsx` — marker `title` | hover / accessible name |
| `LocationCard.jsx` — nearest-MRT list | with `lang` threaded from `App.jsx` |

**Verified by building the app**, not by reading the data: 468 modules transformed, and the Chinese names are present in the emitted bundle. That distinction is the whole of O-320 — the previous version had a perfect table that reached nobody.

## What made this non-trivial: display vs key

`s.name` is everywhere in `MrtMapPanel.jsx`, and **most occurrences are keys**:

```
stationCtxRef.current[s.name]        // cache
modeByName.get(s.name)               // lookup
s.name === detail.station.name       // identity
s.name + ' MRT Station Singapore'    // Google Maps query
```

Translating any of those breaks the app **silently** — a cache that never hits, a comparison that never matches, a map search for a Chinese string. No error, no crash, just a feature quietly not working.

So the test asserts **both directions**: display sites resolve, key sites are still English. A test checking only the first would pass just as happily on a version that had translated the Maps query.

## Deliberately not done

The map **pill** (`stationPillNode`) keeps the English name. It's a dense label sized for short Latin text, and **this environment cannot render the map to look at the result**. Changing a size-sensitive visual on faith is how an unverifiable regression ships. Pinned by a test so the omission is visible rather than forgotten, and reversible in one line once someone can see it.

## O-321 — the honest headline

**Only 1 of the 3 languages can ever reach a reader.** The transport TMA's `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` is `en, fr, id, ru, de, zh, ja, es` — **no `ms`, no `ta`**. Malay and Tamil are stored, correct, joined, and unreachable.

I did **not** add those locales, because it would be worse rather than better: every other UI string exists only in `en`/`fr`, so a reader choosing Malay would get an English interface with Malay station names — a regression dressed as a feature.

Separately, `LocationCard`'s own headings (*"You are here"*, *"Nearest MRT"*) were hardcoded English before this change and still are, so a `zh` reader now sees a Chinese station name under an English heading.

## Two of my own errors, both caught here

- **A stray Chinese character in my English Register prose** — `选ing` for "selecting". The repo has a whole test file about script contamination in the corpora; the same hazard applies to the documentation about them.
- **A timezone slip.** I stamped this work `27-08 '26 22:11 SGT` from a `22:11 UTC` clock. SGT is UTC+8, so the correct stamp is `28-08 '26 06:11 SGT` — eight hours and one day off. `serial-state-anchor.test.js` failed with `expected 28822000 to be less than 60000` and named it. TF-10 and D-203 are about trusting the fetched instant over the remembered one; this was the failure one step later — fetching correctly, then transcribing it into the wrong field.

## Verification

- `npx vite build` on the transport app — clean, 468 modules, names in the bundle
- **`npm test -- --run` → 189 files, 4,419 tests green** (+4), twice

## Also carried

`[AMD-20]`, #1769's merge record, folds forward per **D-205**.

## Still open

O-321, O-318, O-226, O-228, O-308, O-310–O-313, O-184, and the still-unnamed collection-time test failure from v0.62.808.

title: v0.62.815–817 — Indonesian reads the Malay column; the card strip is wired, widened, and its headings follow the reader
body:
Operator, from a live Indonesian session: *"i change to indonesian, it should show the Malay station name."* — then *"16%, 5 + drop ml-auto"*, then *"fix the LocationCard headings too"*. Three commits, one arc: the transport card strip now reads in the reader's language, at a width where the names fit.

## v0.62.815 — two faults behind one symptom

**(a) `id` had no column to read.** The register carries English, Chinese, Malay and Tamil — no Indonesian. `LANG_COLUMN = { id: 'ms' }` now sends Indonesian readers to the official Malay names.

**The caveat, stated rather than buried:** Malay is not Indonesian. The station *name* is identical — proper nouns — but the category word differs. The register says **Stesen** MRT Ang Mo Kio; Indonesian says **Stasiun**, and this app's own `id` strings already use *stasiun* (visible in your own screenshot: *"Cari stasiun atau jalan"*). So an `id` reader gets a correct, official, immediately intelligible name carrying one Malay word. The alternative was English, which is neither.

**The data is not edited to suit.** Rewriting *Stesen* → *Stasiun* would turn a copy of an official register into a derived table, which the file's own header forbids. The mapping lives at the **display boundary** — one line, visible, reversible.

**(b) `StationCard` was not among the three sites v0.62.814 wired** — and it's the most visible station name in the app, the card strip along the bottom of your screenshot. That's exactly why you saw English. Now wired.

### The catch that mattered, and it was user data

In `StationCard`, `name` is not only displayed:

| Use | What breaks if it were translated |
| :--- | :--- |
| `readSaved().includes(name)` + save toggle | **every user's saved stations orphan on a language switch** |
| `data-station-card={name}` | the carousel can no longer scroll to a card |
| `mapsQ(...)` | Google Maps searches for a Malay string |
| `shareUrl(lat, lng, name)` | shared links carry a localised name |

The first is the serious one — a stored list still holding *Ang Mo Kio* while every card calls itself *Stesen MRT Ang Mo Kio*: saved data silently disowned by a UI setting. So the localised string got its own `displayName`, used in exactly one place, and the test asserts **all four key sites still read `name`**.

## v0.62.816 — the width, at your number

*"16%, 5 + drop ml-auto"*. The ladder was `13.5%` / `11%` on wide screens — cards sized for 7–9 visible, which is why localised names truncated to *"Yio Chu K…"*. Now `min-[1600px]:basis-[16%] min-[2000px]:basis-[20%]`: five cards at 2048×1280, and `ml-auto` dropped at both sites so the hours row does not open a gap as the card widens.

The ladder is deliberately a **V** — 60 % → 31 % → 22 % → 17 % → 16 % → 20 % — narrowing through the tablet range before widening again. A comment records that, next to the v0.6x line this change reverses, because the obvious reading ("it should be monotonic") is wrong and the test asserting monotonicity failed for that reason.

## v0.62.817 — the headings, and a guard that was not asked for

O-321 named the seam in v0.62.814: station names localised, headings above them hardcoded English, so a reader who switched language saw 宏茂桥地铁站 sitting beneath **"Nearest MRT"**. `mrt.youAreHere` and `mrt.nearestMrt` now exist in the base `{ en, fr }` table and in all six locale blocks, phrased to match the `mrt.nearestHawker` entry directly above each so the two "nearest X" labels read as a pair.

**The guard.** Locale blocks merge at load by `if (STRINGS[k] && STRINGS[k].zh == null)`. That leading `STRINGS[k] &&` drops any locale key whose base entry does not exist — silently. Such a key is in the file, looks like coverage in a diff, and can never render. Same orphan shape as the classics-notes overlay rows in **O-317**, and nothing was checking for it. `__tests__/transport-i18n-locale-blocks.test.js` now does, across all six blocks (0 orphans today).

It **parses** `i18n.js` rather than importing `t` from it. The first version imported it and `test-import-graph-guard.test.js` failed it: `i18n.js` pulls in React for `useLocale`, which the unit job's root `npm ci` does not install. It passed locally only because a TMA build had populated `web/transport/node_modules` — that guard's founding case from v0.62.704, reproduced inside the file being added. Parsing also has the side benefit of seeing the orphans the real merge discards.

## Verification

- `npm test -- --run` → **190 files, 4,434 tests green** (+15 over the base)
- `npx vite build` on the transport app — clean, 468 modules
- Both new gates proved by mutation before landing: a typo'd `id` key fires the orphan assertion; a deleted `zh` value fires the English-fallback one; file restored and re-diffed
- `stationName('Ang Mo Kio', …)` across `en/id/zh/ta/fr`: English passes through, `id` → *Stesen MRT Ang Mo Kio*, `zh` → 宏茂桥地铁站, `fr` falls back rather than blanking

## Also carried

`[AMD-22]`…`[AMD-25]`, and #1770's merge record, folding forward per **D-205**.

## Still open

**Tamil remains unreachable** — there is no `ta` locale in `SUPPORTED_LOCALES`, and adding one without a Tamil UI string set would give an English interface with Tamil station names. The **map pill** stays English pending someone who can render the map. Register: **O-323** opened for the silent-drop hazard; O-320 and O-321 closed.
